Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Dīghanikāyo

The Long Discourses

Pāthikavaggapāḷi

The Pāṭika Division

1. Pāthikasuttaṃ

1. The Pāṭika Sutta

Sunakkhattavatthu

The Story of Sunakkhatta

1. Evaṃ [M 3.0001][P 3.0001][V 3.0001][T 3.0001] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā mallesu viharati anupiyaṃ nāma anuppiyaṃ nāma (syā.) mallānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya anupiyaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “atippago kho tāva anupiyāyaṃ anupiyaṃ (ka.) piṇḍāya carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena bhaggavagottassa paribbājakassa ārāmo, yena bhaggavagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya”nti.

1. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Mallians in a market town of the Mallians named Anupiya. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having dressed and taking his bowl and robe, entered Anupiya for alms. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: "It is still too early to wander for alms in Anupiya. What if I were to go to the hermitage of the wanderer Bhaggavagotta, to the place where the wanderer Bhaggavagotta is?"

2. Atha [P 3.0002][V 3.0002] kho bhagavā yena bhaggavagottassa paribbājakassa ārāmo, yena bhaggavagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho bhaggavagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “etu kho, bhante, bhagavā. Svāgataṃ, bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā, idamāsanaṃ paññatta”nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Bhaggavagottopi kho paribbājako aññataraṃ [T 3.0002] nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho bhaggavagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “purimāni, bhante, divasāni [M 3.0002] purimatarāni sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ etadavoca – ‘paccakkhāto dāni mayā, bhaggava, bhagavā. Na dānāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharāmī’ti. Kaccetaṃ, bhante, tatheva, yathā sunakkhatto licchaviputto avacā”ti? “Tatheva kho etaṃ, bhaggava, yathā sunakkhatto licchaviputto avaca”.

2. Then the Blessed One went to the hermitage of the wanderer Bhaggavagotta, to the place where the wanderer Bhaggavagotta was. Then the wanderer Bhaggavagotta said this to the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One come, venerable sir. Welcome, venerable sir, is the Blessed One's arrival. It has been a long time, venerable sir, since the Blessed One made this occasion to come here. Let the Blessed One sit, venerable sir; this seat has been prepared." The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. The wanderer Bhaggavagotta also, taking a certain low seat, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Bhaggavagotta said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, on former days, some time ago, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son approached where I was; having approached, he said this to me: ‘Now, Bhaggava, the Blessed One has been renounced by me. I no longer live in dependence on the Blessed One.’ Is it indeed so, venerable sir, just as Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son said?" "It is indeed so, Bhaggava, just as Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son said."

3. Purimāni, bhaggava, divasāni purimatarāni sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘paccakkhāmi dānāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ. Na dānāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmī’ti. ‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘api nu tāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ avacaṃ, ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Tvaṃ [P 3.0003] vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhīti. Napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmīti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa, ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi? Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca [T 3.0003] yāva ca (ka.) te idaṃ aparaddha’nti.

3. On former days, Bhaggava, some time ago, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son approached where I was; having approached and paid homage to me, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son said this to me: ‘I now renounce the Blessed One, venerable sir. I will no longer live in dependence on the Blessed One, venerable sir.’ When this was said, Bhaggava, I said this to Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son: ‘Did I, Sunakkhatta, ever say to you, “Come, Sunakkhatta, live in dependence on me”?’ ‘No, indeed, venerable sir.’ ‘Or did you, in turn, say to me, “I, venerable sir, will live in dependence on the Blessed One”?’ ‘No, indeed, venerable sir.’ ‘So it seems, Sunakkhatta, that I did not say to you, “Come, Sunakkhatta, live in dependence on me,” nor did you say to me, “I, venerable sir, will live in dependence on the Blessed One.” This being so, you empty man, who are you to be renouncing whom? See, you empty man, how great this offense of yours is!'

4. ‘Na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotī’ti. ‘Api nu tāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ avacaṃ – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissāmī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Tvaṃ vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissatī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissāmī’ti; napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissatī’ti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa[V 3.0003], ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi? Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, kate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye akate vā uttarimanussadhammā [M 3.0003] iddhipāṭihāriye yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti? ‘Kate [P 3.0004] vā, bhante, uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye akate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye yassatthāya bhagavatā dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, kate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye, akate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye, yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa [T 3.0004] sammā dukkhakkhayāya. Tatra, sunakkhatta, kiṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kataṃ karissati? Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha’nti.

4. ‘But, venerable sir, the Blessed One does not perform for me any miracle of psychic power beyond the human state.’ ‘Did I, Sunakkhatta, ever say to you, “Come, Sunakkhatta, live in dependence on me, and I will perform for you a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state”?’ ‘No, indeed, venerable sir.’ ‘Or did you, in turn, say to me, “I, venerable sir, will live in dependence on the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will perform for me a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state”?’ ‘No, indeed, venerable sir.’ ‘So it seems, Sunakkhatta, that I did not say to you, “Come, Sunakkhatta, live in dependence on me, and I will perform for you a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state,” nor did you say to me, “I, venerable sir, will live in dependence on the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will perform for me a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state.” This being so, you empty man, who are you to be renouncing whom? What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Whether a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state is performed or not, does the Dhamma taught by me, for the sake of which it was taught, lead one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering?’ ‘Whether a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state is performed or not, venerable sir, the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, for the sake of which it was taught, leads one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering.’ ‘So it is, Sunakkhatta. Whether a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state is performed or not, the Dhamma taught by me, for the sake of which it was taught, leads one who practices it to the complete destruction of suffering. In that case, Sunakkhatta, what will the performance of a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state accomplish? See, you empty man, how great this offense of yours is!’

5. ‘Na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā aggaññaṃ paññapetī’ti paññāpetīti (pī.)? ‘Api nu tāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ avacaṃ – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te aggaññaṃ paññapessāmī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Tvaṃ vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me aggaññaṃ paññapessatī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te aggaññaṃ paññapessāmīti. Napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me aggaññaṃ paññapessatī’ti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa, ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi? Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, paññatte vā aggaññe, apaññatte vā aggaññe, yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti? ‘Paññatte vā, bhante, aggaññe, apaññatte vā aggaññe, yassatthāya bhagavatā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti. ‘Iti [P 3.0005] kira, sunakkhatta, paññatte vā aggaññe, apaññatte vā aggaññe, yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya. Tatra, sunakkhatta, kiṃ aggaññaṃ paññattaṃ [T 3.0005] karissati? Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddhaṃ’.

5. ‘But, venerable sir, the Blessed One does not declare to me the knowledge of beginnings.’ ‘Did I ever say to you, Sunakkhatta, “Come, Sunakkhatta, live depending on me, and I will declare to you the knowledge of beginnings”?’ ‘No, venerable sir.’ ‘Or did you ever say to me, “Venerable sir, I will live depending on the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me the knowledge of beginnings”?’ ‘No, venerable sir.’ ‘So it seems, Sunakkhatta, that I never said to you, “Come, Sunakkhatta, live depending on me, and I will declare to you the knowledge of beginnings,” nor did you ever say to me, “Venerable sir, I will live depending on the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me the knowledge of beginnings.” This being the case, foolish man, who are you, and whom are you repudiating? What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Whether the knowledge of beginnings is declared or not, does the Dhamma taught by me lead one who practices it accordingly to the complete destruction of suffering?’ ‘Whether the knowledge of beginnings is declared or not, venerable sir, the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One leads one who practices it accordingly to the complete destruction of suffering.’ ‘So it seems, Sunakkhatta, whether the knowledge of beginnings is declared or not, the Dhamma taught by me leads one who practices it accordingly to the complete destruction of suffering. In that case, Sunakkhatta, what would a declaration of the knowledge of beginnings accomplish? See, foolish man, how great this transgression of yours is.’

6. ‘Anekapariyāyena kho te, sunakkhatta, mama vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme – itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato [M 3.0004] lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, anekapariyāyena mama vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme.

6. ‘In many ways, Sunakkhatta, my praise has been spoken by you in the Vajjian village: “That Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly self-enlightened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-farer, knower of the world, an unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.” Thus, Sunakkhatta, in many ways my praise has been spoken by you in the Vajjian village.

‘Anekapariyāyena [V 3.0004] kho te, sunakkhatta, dhammassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme – svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhīti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, anekapariyāyena dhammassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme.

‘In many ways, Sunakkhatta, praise for the Dhamma has been spoken by you in the Vajjian village: “The Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One, visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be realized personally by the wise.” Thus, Sunakkhatta, in many ways praise for the Dhamma has been spoken by you in the Vajjian village.

‘Anekapariyāyena kho te, sunakkhatta, saṅghassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, anekapariyāyena saṅghassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme.

‘In many ways, Sunakkhatta, praise for the Sangha has been spoken by you in the Vajjian village: “The Sangha of the Blessed One's disciples is practicing the good way, practicing the straight way, practicing the methodical way, practicing the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals—this is the Sangha of the Blessed One's disciples. They are worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.” Thus, Sunakkhatta, in many ways praise for the Sangha has been spoken by you in the Vajjian village.

‘Ārocayāmi kho te, sunakkhatta, paṭivedayāmi kho te, sunakkhatta. Bhavissanti kho te, sunakkhatta, vattāro, no visahi sunakkhatto licchaviputto samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ, so avisahanto [T 3.0006] sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattoti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, bhavissanti vattāro’ti.

‘I declare to you, Sunakkhatta, I make it known to you, Sunakkhatta. There will be those who will say of you: “Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi son, was not able to practice the holy life under the ascetic Gotama; being unable, he has renounced the training and reverted to a lesser life.” Thus, Sunakkhatta, there will be those who will say this of you.’

Evaṃ pi [P 3.0006] kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

‘Even when spoken to thus by me, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son departed from this Dhamma and Discipline, just like one destined for the plane of misery, for hell.’

Korakkhattiyavatthu

The Story of Korakkhattiya

7. “Ekamidāhaṃ, bhaggava, samayaṃ thūlūsu bumūsu (sī. pī.) viharāmi uttarakā nāma thūlūnaṃ nigamo. Atha khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sunakkhattena licchaviputtena pacchāsamaṇena uttarakaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Tena kho pana samayena acelo korakkhattiyo kukkuravatiko catukkuṇḍiko catukuṇḍiko (sī. pī.) catukoṇḍiko (syā. ka.) chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādati, mukheneva bhuñjati. Addasā kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ kukkuravatikaṃ [M 3.0005] catukkuṇḍikaṃ chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādantaṃ mukheneva bhuñjantaṃ. Disvānassa etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpo vata, bho, ayaṃ arahaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) samaṇo catukkuṇḍiko chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādati, mukheneva bhuñjatī’ti.

7. “On one occasion, Bhaggava, I was dwelling among the Thūlus in a market town of the Thūlus named Uttarakā. Then, Bhaggava, in the morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and outer robe, I entered Uttarakā for alms-food with Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi son, as my attendant monk. At that time, the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, a practitioner of the dog-vow, going on all fours, was chewing and eating with his mouth alone the food that had been placed on the ground. Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi son, saw the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, the practitioner of the dog-vow, going on all fours, chewing and eating with his mouth alone the food that had been placed on the ground. Having seen him, this thought occurred to him: ‘Sirs, this ascetic is indeed of a virtuous nature! Going on all fours, he chews and eats with his mouth alone the food that has been placed on the ground.’”

“Atha khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattassa licchaviputtassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya sunakkhattaṃ [V 3.0005] licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘tvampi nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo moghapurisa sakyaputtiyo (sī. syā. pī.) paṭijānissasī’ti! ‘Kiṃ pana maṃ, bhante, bhagavā evamāha – ‘tvampi [P 3.0007] nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo moghapurisa sakyaputtiyo (sī. syā. pī.) paṭijānissasī’ti? ‘Nanu te, sunakkhatta, imaṃ acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ kukkuravatikaṃ catukkuṇḍikaṃ chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādantaṃ mukheneva [T 3.0007] bhuñjantaṃ disvāna etadahosi – sādhurūpo vata, bho, ayaṃ samaṇo catukkuṇḍiko chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādati, mukheneva bhuñjatī’ti? ‘Evaṃ, bhante. Kiṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā arahattassa maccharāyatī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, moghapurisa, arahattassa maccharāyāmi. Api ca, tuyhevetaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ, taṃ pajaha. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, maññasi acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ – sādhurūpo ayaṃ samaṇoti maññasi “acelo korakhattiyo sādhurūpo arahaṃ samaṇoti” (syā.). So sattamaṃ divasaṃ alasakena kālaṅkarissati. Kālaṅkato kālakato (sī. syā. pī.) ca kālakañcikā kālakañjā (sī. pī.), kālakañjikā (syā.) nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatra upapajjissati. Kālaṅkatañca naṃ bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍessanti. Ākaṅkhamāno ca tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyāsi – jānāsi, āvuso korakkhattiya acela korakhattiya (ka.), attano gatinti? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ te acelo korakkhattiyo byākarissati – jānāmi, āvuso sunakkhatta, attano gatiṃ; kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatrāmhi upapannoti.

“Then, Bhaggava, having known with my mind the thought in the mind of Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi prince, I said this to him: ‘Foolish man, do you indeed claim to be an ascetic, a son of the Sakyans?’ ‘But why, venerable sir, does the Blessed One say this to me: “Foolish man, do you indeed claim to be an ascetic, a son of the Sakyans?”’ ‘Is it not so, Sunakkhatta, that when you saw this naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, the practitioner of the dog-vow, going on all fours, chewing and eating with his mouth alone the food that had been placed on the ground, this thought occurred to you: “Sirs, this ascetic is indeed of a virtuous nature! Going on all fours, he chews and eats with his mouth alone the food that has been placed on the ground”?’ ‘It is so, venerable sir. But why, venerable sir, does the Blessed One begrudge Arahantship?’ ‘I do not begrudge Arahantship, foolish man. Rather, it is in you that this evil view has arisen. Abandon it. May it not be for your detriment and suffering for a long time. As for this naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, Sunakkhatta, whom you think to be an ascetic of a virtuous nature, he will die on the seventh day from an illness of indigestion. And having died, he will be reborn there, in the host of asuras named Kālakañjikā, the lowest of all asura hosts. And having died, they will cast him out in a charnel ground on a patch of bīraṇa grass. If you wish, Sunakkhatta, you may approach the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya and ask: “Friend Korakkhattiya, do you know your own destination?” It is a possibility, Sunakkhatta, that the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya will declare to you: “I know my destination, friend Sunakkhatta. I have been reborn there, in the host of asuras named Kālakañjikā, the lowest of all asura hosts.”’

“Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yena acelo korakkhattiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ etadavoca [M 3.0006] – ‘byākato khosi, āvuso korakkhattiya, samaṇena gotamena – acelo korakkhattiyo sattamaṃ divasaṃ alasakena kālaṅkarissati. Kālaṅkato [P 3.0008] ca kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo[T 3.0008], tatra upapajjissati. Kālaṅkatañca naṃ bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍessantī’ti. Yena tvaṃ, āvuso korakkhattiya, mattaṃ mattañca bhattaṃ bhuñjeyyāsi, mattaṃ mattañca pānīyaṃ piveyyāsi. Yathā samaṇassa gotamassa micchā assa vacana’nti.

“Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi prince, went to where the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya was. Having approached, he said this to the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya: ‘Friend Korakkhattiya, a prophecy has been made about you by the ascetic Gotama: “The naked ascetic Korakkhattiya will die on the seventh day from an illness of indigestion. And having died, he will be reborn there, in the host of asuras named Kālakañjikā, the lowest of all asura hosts. And having died, they will cast him out in a charnel ground on a patch of bīraṇa grass.” Therefore, friend Korakkhattiya, you should eat food in moderation and drink water in moderation, so that the word of the ascetic Gotama may become false.’”

8. “Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto ekadvīhikāya sattarattindivāni gaṇesi, yathā taṃ tathāgatassa asaddahamāno. Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo korakkhattiyo sattamaṃ divasaṃ alasakena kālamakāsi. Kālaṅkato ca kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatra upapajji. Kālaṅkatañca naṃ bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍesuṃ.

8. “Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi prince, counted off the seven days and nights one by one, disbelieving the word of the Tathāgata. Then, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya died on the seventh day from an illness of indigestion. And having died, he was reborn there, in the host of asuras named Kālakañjikā, the lowest of all asura hosts. And they cast him out, having died, in a charnel ground on a patch of bīraṇa grass.”

9. “Assosi [V 3.0006] kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto – ‘acelo kira korakkhattiyo alasakena kālaṅkato bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍito’ti. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yena bīraṇatthambakaṃ susānaṃ, yena acelo korakkhattiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ tikkhattuṃ pāṇinā ākoṭesi – ‘jānāsi, āvuso korakkhattiya, attano gati’nti? Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo korakkhattiyo pāṇinā piṭṭhiṃ paripuñchanto vuṭṭhāsi. ‘Jānāmi, āvuso sunakkhatta, attano gatiṃ. Kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatrāmhi upapanno’ti vatvā tattheva uttāno papati paripati (syā. ka.).

9. “Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi prince, heard the news: ‘It is said that the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya has died from an illness of indigestion and has been cast out in a charnel ground on a patch of bīraṇa grass.’ Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi prince, went to the charnel ground, to the patch of bīraṇa grass, to where the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya was. Having approached, he struck the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya three times with his hand, saying: ‘Friend Korakkhattiya, do you know your own destination?’ Then, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya arose, wiping his back with his hand. He said: ‘I know my own destination, friend Sunakkhatta. I have been reborn there, in the host of asuras named Kālakañjikā, the lowest of all asura hosts.’ Having said this, he fell down supine right in that very place.”

10. “Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava[T 3.0009], sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yatheva te ahaṃ acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ ārabbha byākāsiṃ, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, aññathā vā’ti? ‘Yatheva me, bhante, bhagavā acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ ārabbha byākāsi, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, no aññathā’ti. ‘Taṃ [M 3.0007][P 3.0009] kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yadi evaṃ sante kataṃ vā hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, akataṃ vāti? ‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, no akata’nti. ‘Evampi kho maṃ tvaṃ, moghapurisa, uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karontaṃ evaṃ vadesi – na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotīti. Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha’nti. “Evampi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

10. “Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince approached me; having approached, he paid homage to me and sat down to one side. Bhaggava, to Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince who was sitting to one side, I said this: ‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Just as I made a declaration to you concerning the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, did that result turn out just so, or otherwise?’ ‘Venerable sir, just as the Blessed One made a declaration to me concerning the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, so did that result turn out, not otherwise.’ ‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? If this is so, was a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state performed or not performed?’ ‘Surely, venerable sir, if this is so, a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state was performed, not unperformed.’ ‘Even so, you foolish man, while I was performing a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state, you say this: “Venerable sir, the Blessed One does not perform for me a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state.” See, foolish man, how great this fault of yours is!’ Even when spoken to thus by me, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince departed from this Dhamma and Discipline, just as one destined for the plane of misery, for hell.”

Acelakaḷāramaṭṭakavatthu

The Account of the Naked Ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka

11. “Ekamidāhaṃ, bhaggava, samayaṃ vesāliyaṃ viharāmi mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme. Tassa sattavatapadāni sattavattapadāni (syā. pī.) samattāni samādinnāni honti – ‘yāvajīvaṃ acelako assaṃ, na vatthaṃ paridaheyyaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ brahmacārī assaṃ, na methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyyaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ surāmaṃseneva yāpeyyaṃ, na odanakummāsaṃ [T 3.0010] bhuñjeyyaṃ. Puratthimena vesāliṃ udenaṃ nāma cetiyaṃ, taṃ nātikkameyyaṃ, dakkhiṇena vesāliṃ gotamakaṃ nāma cetiyaṃ, taṃ nātikkameyyaṃ, pacchimena vesāliṃ sattambaṃ nāma cetiyaṃ, taṃ [P 3.0010] nātikkameyyaṃ, uttarena vesāliṃ bahuputtaṃ [V 3.0007] nāma bahuputtakaṃ nāma (syā.) cetiyaṃ taṃ nātikkameyya’nti. So imesaṃ sattannaṃ vatapadānaṃ samādānahetu lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme.

11. On one occasion, Bhaggava, I was dwelling in Vesālī, in the Great Wood, at the hall with the peaked roof. At that time, the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka was living in Vesālī, having reached the peak of gain and fame in the Vajjian villages. He had undertaken and was observing seven vows: ‘For as long as I live, I will be a naked ascetic; I will not wear clothes. For as long as I live, I will be celibate; I will not engage in the sexual act. For as long as I live, I will subsist only on liquor and meat; I will not eat cooked rice or gruel. I will not go beyond the Udena shrine to the east of Vesālī, nor the Gotamaka shrine to the south, nor the Sattamba shrine to the west, nor the Bahuputta shrine to the north.’ It was because of undertaking these seven vows that he reached the peak of gain and fame in the Vajjian villages.

12. “Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yena acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ pañhaṃ apucchi. Tassa acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyāsi. Asampāyanto kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhattassa licchaviputtassa etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpaṃ vata bho arahantaṃ samaṇaṃ āsādimhase asādiyimhase (syā.). Mā vata no ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’ti.

12. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince approached the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka; having approached, he asked the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka a question. When asked the question, the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka could not answer satisfactorily. Being unable to answer satisfactorily, he displayed anger, aversion, and displeasure. Then, Bhaggava, this thought occurred to Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince: ‘Alas, we have assailed a recluse of virtuous nature, an arahant! May this not lead to our harm and suffering for a long time!’

13. “Atha [M 3.0008] kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘tvampi nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo paṭijānissasī’ti! ‘Kiṃ pana maṃ, bhante, bhagavā evamāha – tvampi nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo paṭijānissasī’ti? ‘Nanu tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ apucchi. Tassa te acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyāsi. Asampāyanto kopañca dosañca [T 3.0011] appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Tassa te etadahosi – “sādhurūpaṃ vata, bho, arahantaṃ samaṇaṃ āsādimhase. Mā vata no ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante. Kiṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā arahattassa maccharāyatī’ti? ‘Na [P 3.0011] kho ahaṃ, moghapurisa, arahattassa maccharāyāmi, api ca tuyhevetaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ, taṃ pajaha. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, maññasi acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ – sādhurūpo ayaṃ arahaṃ (syā.) samaṇoti, so nacirasseva parihito sānucāriko vicaranto odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjamāno sabbāneva vesāliyāni cetiyāni samatikkamitvā yasā nihīno yasānikiṇṇo (ka.) kālaṃ karissatī’ti.

13. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince approached me; having approached, he paid homage to me and sat down to one side. To Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince, who was sitting to one side, I said this: ‘You too, you worthless man, do you claim to be a Sakyan recluse?’ ‘But why, venerable sir, does the Blessed One say this to me: “You too, you worthless man, do you claim to be a Sakyan recluse?”’ ‘Did you not, Sunakkhatta, approach the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka and ask him a question? When asked the question, he could not answer satisfactorily. Being unable to answer satisfactorily, he displayed anger, aversion, and displeasure. And did not this thought then occur to you: “Alas, we have assailed a recluse of virtuous nature, an arahant! May this not lead to our harm and suffering for a long time!”?’ ‘Yes, venerable sir. But, venerable sir, does the Blessed One begrudge arahantship?’ ‘I do not begrudge arahantship, you worthless man. Rather, this evil view has arisen in you—abandon it! May it not lead to your harm and suffering for a long time. As for this naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka whom you consider to be a recluse of virtuous nature, he will, before long, wear clothes, wander about with a female companion, eat cooked rice and gruel, transgress all the shrines of Vesālī, and die diminished in fame.’

“‘Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako nacirasseva parihito sānucāriko vicaranto odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjamāno sabbāneva vesāliyāni cetiyāni samatikkamitvā yasā nihīno kālamakāsi.

Then, Bhaggava, not long after, the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka, wearing clothes, wandering about with a female companion, eating cooked rice and gruel, having transgressed all the shrines of Vesālī, died diminished in fame.

14. “Assosi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto – ‘acelo kira kaḷāramaṭṭako parihito sānucāriko vicaranto odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjamāno sabbāneva vesāliyāni cetiyāni samatikkamitvā yasā nihīno kālaṅkato’ti. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto [V 3.0008] licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yatheva te ahaṃ acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ ārabbha byākāsiṃ, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, aññathā vā’ti? ‘Yatheva [T 3.0012] me, bhante, bhagavā acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ ārabbha byākāsi, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, no [M 3.0009] aññathā’ti. ‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yadi evaṃ sante kataṃ [P 3.0012] vā hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ akataṃ vā’ti? ‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, no akata’nti. ‘Evampi kho maṃ tvaṃ, moghapurisa, uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karontaṃ evaṃ vadesi – na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotī”ti. Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha’nti. “Eva’mpi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

14. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince heard: ‘The naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka, it is said, wearing clothes, wandering about with a female companion, eating cooked rice and gruel, having transgressed all the shrines of Vesālī, has died diminished in fame.’ Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince approached where I was; having approached and paid homage to me, he sat down at a suitable place. To Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince, who was seated at a suitable place, I said this: ‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Regarding the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka, I made a declaration to you; has that result come to be exactly so, or otherwise?’ ‘Venerable sir, just as the Blessed One made a declaration to me concerning the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka, that result has come to be exactly so, not otherwise.’ ‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? If it is so, has a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state been performed, or has it not been performed?’ ‘Surely, venerable sir, if it is so, a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state has been performed; it has not been unperformed.’ ‘Worthless man, even though I perform a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state, you speak thus of me: “Venerable sir, the Blessed One does not perform for me a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state.” See, worthless man, how great this offense of yours is!’ Even when spoken to thus by me, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi prince indeed departed from this Dhamma and Discipline, just as one destined for the plane of misery, for hell.

Acelapāthikaputtavatthu

The Story of the Naked Ascetic Pāthikaputta

15. “Ekamidāhaṃ, bhaggava, samayaṃ tattheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena acelo pāthikaputto pāṭikaputto (sī. syā. pī.) vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme. So vesāliyaṃ parisati evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsati – ‘samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo, ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ. Samaṇo gotamo upaḍḍhapathaṃ āgaccheyya, ahampi upaḍḍhapathaṃ gaccheyyaṃ. Te tattha ubhopi uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kareyyāma. Ekaṃ ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, dvāhaṃ karissāmi. Dve ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni [T 3.0013] karissati, cattārāhaṃ karissāmi[P 3.0013]. Cattāri ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, aṭṭhāhaṃ karissāmi. Iti yāvatakaṃ yāvatakaṃ samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmī’ti.

15. Bhaggava, at one time I was dwelling right there in Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof. Now at that time, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta was dwelling in Vesālī, in a village of the Vajjis, having reached the pinnacle of gain and the pinnacle of fame. He spoke these words in the assembly in Vesālī: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of knowledge, and I too am a proponent of knowledge. A proponent of knowledge is worthy to display a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state with another proponent of knowledge. Let the ascetic Gotama come halfway, and I too will go halfway. There, we both shall perform a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state. If the ascetic Gotama performs one miracle of psychic power beyond the human state, I will perform two. If he performs two miracles of psychic power beyond the human state, I will perform four. If he performs four miracles of psychic power beyond the human state, I will perform eight. Thus, however many miracles of psychic power beyond the human state the ascetic Gotama performs, I will perform double that number.’

16. “Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘acelo, bhante, pāthikaputto vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme. So vesāliyaṃ parisati evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsati – samaṇopi [V 3.0009] gotamo [M 3.0010] ñāṇavādo, ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ. Samaṇo gotamo upaḍḍhapathaṃ āgaccheyya, ahampi upaḍḍhapathaṃ gaccheyyaṃ. Te tattha ubhopi uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kareyyāma. Ekaṃ ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, dvāhaṃ karissāmi. Dve ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, cattārāhaṃ karissāmi. Cattāri ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, aṭṭhāhaṃ karissāmi. Iti yāvatakaṃ yāvatakaṃ samaṇo gotamo uttari manussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmī”ti.

16. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son approached where I was; having approached and paid homage to me, he sat down at a suitable place. Seated at a suitable place, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son said this to me: ‘Venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is dwelling in Vesālī, in a village of the Vajjis, having reached the pinnacle of gain and the pinnacle of fame. He speaks these words in the assembly in Vesālī: “The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of knowledge, and I too am a proponent of knowledge. A proponent of knowledge is worthy to display a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state with another proponent of knowledge. Let the ascetic Gotama come halfway, and I too will go halfway. There, we both shall perform a miracle of psychic power beyond the human state. If the ascetic Gotama performs one miracle of psychic power beyond the human state, I will perform two. If he performs two miracles of psychic power beyond the human state, I will perform four. If he performs four miracles of psychic power beyond the human state, I will perform eight. Thus, however many miracles of psychic power beyond the human state the ascetic Gotama performs, I will perform double that number.”’

“Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, sunakkhatta, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi [T 3.0014] tassa vipateyyā’ti.

When this was said, Bhaggava, I said this to Sunakkhatta the Licchavi son: ‘Sunakkhatta, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, and without relinquishing that view. If it should even occur to him, “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, and without relinquishing that view,” his head would surely split apart.’

17. ‘Rakkhatetaṃ, bhante, bhagavā vācaṃ, rakkhatetaṃ sugato vāca’nti. ‘Kiṃ [P 3.0014] pana maṃ tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ vadesi – rakkhatetaṃ, bhante, bhagavā vācaṃ, rakkhatetaṃ sugato vāca’nti? ‘Bhagavatā cassa, bhante, esā vācā ekaṃsena odhāritā ovāditā (ka.) – abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Acelo ca, bhante, pāthikaputto virūparūpena bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgaccheyya, tadassa bhagavato musā’ti.

17. “Venerable sir, the Blessed One should guard this statement, the Sugata should guard this statement.” “Why do you say this to me, Sunakkhatta: ‘Venerable sir, the Blessed One should guard this statement, the Sugata should guard this statement’?” “Because, venerable sir, this statement has been definitively uttered by the Blessed One: ‘The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, without relinquishing that view. If it should even occur to him, “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, without relinquishing that view,” his head would surely split apart.’ And, venerable sir, if the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta were to come into the Blessed One’s presence in an altered form, that would be a falsehood for the Blessed One.”

18. ‘Api nu, sunakkhatta, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā dvayagāminī’ti? ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, bhagavatā acelo pāthikaputto cetasā [M 3.0011] ceto paricca vidito – abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti?

18. “Sunakkhatta, would the Tathāgata utter speech that could have a twofold outcome?” “But, venerable sir, has the Blessed One known the mind of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, comprehending it with his own mind, thus: ‘The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, without relinquishing that view. If it were to occur to him, “Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, without relinquishing that view, I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,” his head would surely split apart’?”

‘Udāhu[V 3.0010], devatā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – abhabbo, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti?

“Or did the deities inform the Blessed One of this matter: ‘Venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into the presence of the Blessed One without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, without relinquishing that view. If it were to occur to him thus: “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that mind, without relinquishing that view,” his head would surely split apart’?”

19. ‘Cetasā ceto paricca vidito ceva me, sunakkhatta[T 3.0015], acelo pāthikaputto abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

19. “Sunakkhatta, having encompassed his mind with my mind, it was known to me: ‘The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it were to occur to him thus: “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view,” his head would split apart.’”

‘Devatāpi me etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – abhabbo[P 3.0015], bhante, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

“The deities also informed me of this matter: ‘Venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into the presence of the Blessed One without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it were to occur to him thus: “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view,” his head would split apart.’”

‘Ajitopi nāma licchavīnaṃ senāpati adhunā kālaṅkato tāvatiṃsakāyaṃ upapanno. Sopi maṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamārocesi – alajjī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto; musāvādī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto. Mampi, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto byākāsi vajjigāme – ajito licchavīnaṃ senāpati mahānirayaṃ upapannoti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, mahānirayaṃ upapanno; tāvatiṃsakāyamhi upapanno. Alajjī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto; musāvādī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto; abhabbo ca, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa [M 3.0012] evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

“And Ajita, the general of the Licchavis, who recently died, has been reborn among the Tāvatiṃsa devas. He too approached me and said: ‘Venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is shameless; he is a liar. Venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta also declared about me in the Vajjian village: “Ajita, the general of the Licchavis, has been reborn in the great hell.” But, venerable sir, I was not reborn in the great hell; I have been reborn among the Tāvatiṃsa devas. Venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is shameless; he is a liar. And, venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into the presence of the Blessed One without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it were to occur to him thus: “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view,” his head would split apart.’”

‘Iti kho, sunakkhatta, cetasā ceto paricca vidito ceva me acelo pāthikaputto abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā [V 3.0011] mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Devatāpi me etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – abhabbo, bhante[T 3.0016], acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

“Thus, Sunakkhatta, having encompassed his mind with my mind, it was known to me that the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it were to occur to him thus: ‘I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view,’ his head would split apart. The deities also informed me of this matter: ‘Venerable sir, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into the presence of the Blessed One without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it were to occur to him thus: “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view,” his head would split apart.’”

‘So kho panāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkamissāmi divāvihārāya. Yassadāni tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, icchasi, tassa ārocehī’ti.

“Then, Sunakkhatta, after wandering for alms in Vesālī and having returned from the alms round after the meal, I will go to the park of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta for the day’s sojourn. You may now inform whomever you wish.”

Iddhipāṭihāriyakathā

The Discourse on the Miracle of Psychic Power

20. “Atha [P 3.0016] khvāhaṃ atha kho svāhaṃ (syā.), bhaggava, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ divāvihārāya. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto taramānarūpo vesāliṃ pavisitvā yena abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā abhiññāte abhiññāte licchavī etadavoca – ‘esāvuso, bhagavā vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Abhikkamathāyasmanto abhikkamathāyasmanto, sādhurūpānaṃ samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissatī’ti[M 3.0013]. Atha kho, bhaggava, abhiññātānaṃ abhiññātānaṃ licchavīnaṃ etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpānaṃ kira, bho, samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā [T 3.0017] iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissati; handa vata, bho, gacchāmā’ti. Yena ca abhiññātā abhiññātā brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā nānātitthiya (syā.) samaṇabrāhmaṇā tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā abhiññāte abhiññāte nānātitthiye nānātitthiya (syā.) samaṇabrāhmaṇe etadavoca – ‘esāvuso, bhagavā vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Abhikkamathāyasmanto abhikkamathāyasmanto, sādhurūpānaṃ samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Atha [V 3.0012] kho, bhaggava, abhiññātānaṃ abhiññātānaṃ nānātitthiyānaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpānaṃ kira, bho, samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissati; handa vata, bho, gacchāmā’ti.

20. “Then, Bhaggava, in the morning, having dressed and taking my bowl and robe, I entered Vesālī for alms. After wandering for alms in Vesālī and returning from the alms-round after the meal, I went to the grove of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta for the day’s sojourn. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi, in a hurry, entered Vesālī and approached the most prominent Licchavis. Having approached them, he said to the most prominent Licchavis: ‘Sirs, the Blessed One, after wandering for alms in Vesālī and returning from the alms-round after the meal, has gone to the grove of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta for the day’s sojourn. Come forth, venerable sirs, come forth! There will be a superhuman miracle of psychic power on the part of worthy ascetics.’ Then, Bhaggava, it occurred to the most prominent Licchavis: ‘Indeed, sirs, a superhuman miracle of psychic power will be performed by worthy ascetics. Come now, sirs, let us go!’ He then approached the most prominent brahmins of great wealth, wealthy householders, and ascetics and brahmins of other sects. Having approached them, he said to the most prominent ascetics and brahmins of other sects: ‘Sirs, the Blessed One, after wandering for alms in Vesālī and returning from the alms-round after the meal, has gone to the grove of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta for the day’s sojourn. Come forth, venerable sirs, come forth! There will be a superhuman miracle of psychic power on the part of worthy ascetics.’ Then, Bhaggava, it occurred to the most prominent ascetics and brahmins of other sects: ‘Indeed, sirs, a superhuman miracle of psychic power will be performed by worthy ascetics. Come now, sirs, let us go!’”

“Atha [P 3.0017] kho, bhaggava, abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Sā esā, bhaggava, parisā mahā hoti parisā hoti (sī. syā. pī.) anekasatā anekasahassā.

Then, Bhaggava, the very prominent Licchavis, and the very prominent brahmins of great wealth, wealthy householders, and ascetics and brahmins of various sects all approached the grove of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta. That assembly, Bhaggava, was large, numbering many hundreds, many thousands.

21. “Assosi kho, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto – ‘abhikkantā kira abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo mayhaṃ ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno’ti. Sutvānassa bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso udapādi. Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto [T 3.0018] bhīto saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo tenupasaṅkami.

21. Then, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta heard: ‘It is said that the very prominent Licchavis have arrived, and so have the very prominent brahmins of great wealth, wealthy householders, and ascetics and brahmins of various sects. The ascetic Gotama is also seated in my grove for the day’s abiding.’ Upon hearing this, fear, trembling, and horripilation arose in him. Then, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, frightened, alarmed, and with his hair standing on end, went to the grove of the wanderers at the Tinduka tree stump.

“Assosi kho, bhaggava, sā parisā – ‘acelo kira pāthikaputto bhīto saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo [M 3.0014] tenupasaṅkanto’ti tenupasaṅkamanto (sī. pī. ka.). Atha kho, bhaggava, sā parisā aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi –

Then, Bhaggava, that assembly heard: ‘It is said that the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, frightened, alarmed, and with his hair standing on end, is approaching the grove of the wanderers at the Tinduka tree stump.’ Then, Bhaggava, that assembly addressed a certain man:

‘Ehi tvaṃ, bho purisa, yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkama. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ evaṃ vadehi – abhikkamāvuso, pāthikaputta, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā, samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno; bhāsitā kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo, ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ. Samaṇo [P 3.0018] gotamo upaḍḍhapathaṃ āgaccheyya ahampi upaḍḍhapathaṃ gaccheyyaṃ. Te tattha ubhopi uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kareyyāma. Ekaṃ ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, dvāhaṃ karissāmi. Dve ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, cattārāhaṃ karissāmi. Cattāri ce samaṇo gotamo [T 3.0019] uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati[V 3.0013], aṭṭhāhaṃ karissāmi. Iti yāvatakaṃ yāvatakaṃ samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmī’ti abhikkamasseva abhikkamayeva (sī. syā. pī.) kho; āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno’ti.

‘Come, good man, go to the grove of the wanderers at the Tinduka tree stump, where the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is. Approach him and speak to him thus: “Go forth, friend Pāthikaputta. The very prominent Licchavis have arrived, and so have the very prominent brahmins of great wealth, wealthy householders, and ascetics and brahmins of various sects. The ascetic Gotama is also seated in your grove for his day’s abiding. And, friend Pāthikaputta, this statement was indeed declared by you in the assembly at Vesālī: ‘The ascetic Gotama professes knowledge, and I too profess knowledge. It is fitting for one who professes knowledge to demonstrate a superhuman miracle of psychic power to another who professes knowledge. Let the ascetic Gotama come halfway, and I will go halfway. There, we two shall perform a superhuman miracle of psychic power. If the ascetic Gotama performs one superhuman miracle of psychic power, I will perform two. If the ascetic Gotama performs two superhuman miracles of psychic power, I will perform four. If the ascetic Gotama performs four superhuman miracles of psychic power, I will perform eight. Thus, for whatever number of superhuman miracles of psychic power the ascetic Gotama performs, I will perform double that number.’ Go forth now, friend Pāthikaputta, to the halfway point. The ascetic Gotama, having come first of all, is already seated in your grove for his day’s abiding.”’

22. “Evaṃ, bhoti kho, bhaggava, so puriso tassā parisāya paṭissutvā yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā [M 3.0015] kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā – samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo; ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ…pe… taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmīti. Abhikkamasseva kho, āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno’ti.

22. Bhaggava, saying, ‘Very well, sirs,’ that man replied to the assembly and went to the grove of the wanderers at the Tinduka tree stump, where the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta was. Having approached, he said this to the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta: ‘Go forth, friend Pāthikaputta. The very prominent Licchavis have arrived, and so have the very prominent brahmins of great wealth, wealthy householders, and ascetics and brahmins of various sects. The ascetic Gotama is also seated in your grove for his day’s abiding. And this statement, friend Pāthikaputta, was indeed spoken by you in the assembly at Vesālī: “The ascetic Gotama professes knowledge; I too profess knowledge. It is fitting for one who professes knowledge to demonstrate a superhuman miracle of psychic power to another who professes knowledge… I will perform double that number.” Go forth now, friend Pāthikaputta, to the halfway point. The ascetic Gotama, having come first of all, is already seated in your grove for his day’s abiding.’”

“Evaṃ vutte, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi [P 3.0019] āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati saṃsabbati (ka.), na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ. Atha kho so, bhaggava, puriso acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃ su nāma te, āvuso pāthikaputta, pāvaḷā su nāma te pīṭhakasmiṃ allīnā, pīṭhakaṃ su nāma te pāvaḷāsu allīnaṃ? Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappasi, na sakkosi āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evampi kho, bhaggava, vuccamāno acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati[T 3.0020], na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ.

When this was said, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, saying, ‘I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,’ just sank down right there; he was not able to rise even from his seat. Then, Bhaggava, that man said this to the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta: ‘What is this, friend Pāthikaputta? Are your thighs stuck to the stool, or is the stool stuck to your thighs? Saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,” you just sink down right there; you are not able to rise even from your seat.’ Even when spoken to thus, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, saying, ‘I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,’ just sank down right there; he was not able to rise even from his seat.

23. “Yadā kho so, bhaggava, puriso aññāsi – ‘parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ acelo pāthikaputto. Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Atha taṃ parisaṃ āgantvā evamārocesi – ‘parābhūtarūpo, bho parābhūtarūpo bho ayaṃ (syā. ka.), parābhūtarūpo (sī. pī.), acelo pāthikaputto. Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, āvuso, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā [V 3.0014] mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ‘ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyya’nti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti.

23. “When, Bhaggava, that man knew, ‘This naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta has the nature of one who is defeated. Saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,” he just sinks down right there; he is not able to rise even from his seat,’ he then went to that assembly and announced: ‘Sirs, this naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta has the nature of one who is defeated. Saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,” he just sinks down right there; he is not able to rise even from his seat.’ When this was said, Bhaggava, I said this to that assembly: ‘Sirs, the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it should occur to him, “Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view, I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,” his head would surely split apart.’”

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is concluded.

24. “Atha [M 3.0016] kho, bhaggava, aññataro licchavimahāmatto uṭṭhāyāsanā taṃ parisaṃ etadavoca – ‘tena hi, bho, muhuttaṃ tāva āgametha, yāvāhaṃ gacchāmi [P 3.0020] paccāgacchāmi (?). Appeva nāma ahampi sakkuṇeyyaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ imaṃ parisaṃ ānetu’nti.

24. “Then, Bhaggava, a certain Licchavi high minister, having risen from his seat, said this to that assembly: ‘Well then, sirs, please wait for a moment while I go. Perhaps I might be able to bring the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta to this assembly.’”

“Atha kho so, bhaggava, licchavimahāmatto yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkantaṃ te seyyo, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā [T 3.0021] licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā – samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo…pe… taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmīti. Abhikkamasseva kho, āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho panesā, āvuso pāthikaputta, samaṇena gotamena parisati vācā – abhabbo kho acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkamaneneva te jayaṃ karissāma, samaṇassa gotamassa parājaya’nti.

“Then, Bhaggava, that Licchavi high minister went to the park of the wanderer at the Tinduka stump, where the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta was. Having approached, he said this to the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta: ‘Proceed, friend Pāṭikaputta; your proceeding is excellent. The very renowned, very renowned Licchavis have come; and the very renowned, very renowned Brahmin magnates, wealthy householders, and ascetics and brahmins of various sects have come. The ascetic Gotama is seated in the venerable one's park for the day's abiding. And this statement, friend Pāṭikaputta, was indeed spoken by you in the assembly at Vesālī: “The ascetic Gotama is one who speaks of knowledge… I will perform one that is twice and twice again as great.” Proceed now, friend Pāṭikaputta, to the halfway point. Having come before all others, the ascetic Gotama is seated in the venerable one's park for the day's abiding. Furthermore, friend Pāṭikaputta, this statement was indeed spoken by the ascetic Gotama in the assembly: “The naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it should occur to him… his head would surely split apart.” Proceed, friend Pāṭikaputta! By your very act of proceeding we will bring about your victory and the defeat of the ascetic Gotama.’”

“Evaṃ vutte, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti [P 3.0021] āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ. Atha kho so, bhaggava, licchavimahāmatto acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃ su nāma te, āvuso pāthikaputta, pāvaḷā su nāma te pīṭhakasmiṃ allīnā, pīṭhakaṃ su nāma te pāvaḷāsu allīnaṃ[M 3.0017]? Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappasi, na sakkosi āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti[V 3.0015]. Evampi kho, bhaggava, vuccamāno acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ.

“When this was said, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta, saying, ‘I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,’ just sank down right there; he was not able to rise even from his seat. Then, Bhaggava, that Licchavi high minister said this to the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta: ‘What is this, friend Pāṭikaputta? Are your buttocks stuck to the stool, or is the stool stuck to your buttocks? Saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,” you just sink down right there; you are not able to rise even from your seat.’ Even when spoken to thus, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta, saying, ‘I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,’ just sank down right there; he was not able to rise even from his seat.”

25. “Yadā kho so, bhaggava, licchavimahāmatto aññāsi – ‘parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ acelo pāthikaputto āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi [T 3.0022] āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Atha taṃ parisaṃ āgantvā evamārocesi – ‘parābhūtarūpo, bho parābhūtarūpo (sī. pī.), parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ (syā.), acelo pāthikaputto āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, āvuso, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya. Sace pāyasmantānaṃ licchavīnaṃ evamassa – mayaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ varattāhi yāhi varattāhi (syā. ka.) bandhitvā goyugehi āviñcheyyāmāti āviñjeyyāmāti (syā.), āvijjheyyāmāti (sī. pī.), tā varattā chijjeyyuṃ pāthikaputto vā. Abhabbo pana acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa [P 3.0022] evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

25. “When, Bhaggava, that Licchavi high minister knew: ‘This naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta has the nature of one defeated; saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming,” he sinks down right there and is unable even to rise from his seat,’ he then went to that assembly and announced: ‘Sirs, the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta has the nature of one defeated; saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming,” he sinks down right there and is unable even to rise from his seat.’ When this was said, Bhaggava, I spoke to that assembly thus: ‘Sirs, the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it should occur to him: “Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view, I shall go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,” his head would surely split apart. And if it should occur to the venerable Licchavis: “Let us bind the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta with leather straps and drag him with pairs of oxen,” those leather straps would break, or Pāṭikaputta himself would be torn apart. Indeed, the naked ascetic Pāṭikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it should occur to him: “Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view, I shall go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,” his head would surely split apart.’”

26. “Atha kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī uṭṭhāyāsanā taṃ parisaṃ etadavoca – ‘tena hi, bho, muhuttaṃ tāva āgametha, yāvāhaṃ gacchāmi; appeva nāma ahampi sakkuṇeyyaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ imaṃ parisaṃ ānetu”nti.

26. Then, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wooden-bowl ascetic, having risen from his seat, spoke to that assembly thus: 'Well then, sirs, please wait for a moment while I go; perhaps I may be able to bring the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta to this assembly.'

“Atha [M 3.0018] kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ [T 3.0023] etadavoca – ‘abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkantaṃ te seyyo. Abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā – samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo…pe… taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmīti. Abhikkamasseva, kho āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ [V 3.0016] nisinno. Bhāsitā kho panesā, āvuso pāthikaputta, samaṇena gotamena parisati vācā – abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya. Sace pāyasmantānaṃ licchavīnaṃ evamassa – mayaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ varattāhi bandhitvā goyugehi āviñcheyyāmāti. Tā varattā chijjeyyuṃ pāthikaputto vā. Abhabbo pana acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ āgaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkamaneneva te jayaṃ karissāma, samaṇassa gotamassa parājaya’nti.

Then, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wooden-bowl ascetic, went to the Tindukakhāṇu wanderers' park, to where the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta was. Having approached, he spoke this word to the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta: ‘Come forth, friend Pāthikaputta; your coming forth would be better. The very well-known Licchavis have come forth, and the very well-known great brahmin magnates, wealthy householders, and various sectarian ascetics and brahmins have come forth. The ascetic Gotama is also seated in the venerable one's park for the day's abiding. And this speech was indeed uttered by you, friend Pāthikaputta, in the assembly at Vesālī: “The ascetic Gotama claims to have knowledge… I will perform a feat double that.” Come forth, friend Pāthikaputta, even halfway. The ascetic Gotama, having come first of all, is seated in the venerable one's park for the day's abiding. And this speech was indeed uttered by the ascetic Gotama in the assembly, friend Pāthikaputta: “The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it should occur to him: ‘Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view, I shall go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,’ his head would also be severed. And if it should occur to the venerable Licchavis: ‘Let us bind the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta with leather straps and drag him with pairs of oxen,’ those leather straps would break, or Pāthikaputta himself would be torn apart. The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view. If it should occur to him: ‘Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, and without relinquishing that view, I shall come into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,’ his head would also be severed.” Come forth, friend Pāthikaputta; by your very coming forth we shall bring about your victory and the ascetic Gotama’s defeat.’

“Evaṃ [P 3.0023] vutte, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto [T 3.0024] ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ. Atha kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃ su nāma te, āvuso pāthikaputta, pāvaḷā su nāma te pīṭhakasmiṃ allīnā, pīṭhakaṃ su nāma te pāvaḷāsu allīnaṃ? Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva [M 3.0019] saṃsappasi, na sakkosi āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evampi kho, bhaggava, vuccamāno acelo pāthikaputto “āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso”ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātunti.

When this was said, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, saying, ‘I am coming, friend, I am coming,’ sank down right there and was unable even to rise from his seat. Then, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wooden-bowl ascetic, spoke to the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta thus: ‘What is the matter with you, friend Pāthikaputta? Are your buttocks stuck to the stool, or is the stool stuck to your buttocks? Saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming,” you sink down right there and are unable even to rise from your seat.’ Even when spoken to thus, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, saying, ‘I am coming, friend, I am coming,’ sank down right there and was unable even to rise from his seat.

27. “Yadā kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī aññāsi – ‘parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti, atha naṃ etadavoca –

27. When, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wooden-bowl ascetic, knew: ‘This naked ascetic Pāthikaputta has the appearance of one defeated; saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming,” he sinks down right there and is unable even to rise from his seat,’ he then spoke to him thus:

‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sīhassa migarañño etadahosi – yaṃnūnāhaṃ aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyaṃ. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhameyyaṃ, āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambheyyaṃ, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokeyyaṃ, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadeyyaṃ, tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkameyyaṃ. So varaṃ varaṃ migasaṃghe migasaṃghaṃ (syā. ka.) vadhitvā mudumaṃsāni mudumaṃsāni bhakkhayitvā tameva āsayaṃ ajjhupeyya’nti.

‘Formerly, friend Pāthikaputta, this thought occurred to the lion, the king of beasts: “What if I were to establish a dwelling, relying on a certain forest thicket? Having established a dwelling there, in the evening time I would emerge from my dwelling. Having emerged from my dwelling, I would stretch. Having stretched, I would survey the four directions all around. Having surveyed the four directions all around, I would utter a lion’s roar three times. Having uttered a lion’s roar three times, I would set out for prey. Having killed the best of the best among the herds of beasts and eaten the tenderest of meats, I would then approach that very dwelling.”’

‘Atha [V 3.0017] kho, āvuso, so sīho migarājā aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappesi. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ [T 3.0025] āsayā nikkhami, āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambhi, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokesi, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadi, tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkāmi. So varaṃ varaṃ migasaṅghe vadhitvā mudumaṃsāni mudumaṃsāni bhakkhayitvā tameva āsayaṃ ajjhupesi.

‘Then, friend, that lion, the king of beasts, relying on a certain forest thicket, established a dwelling. Having established a dwelling there, in the evening time he emerged from his dwelling. Having emerged from his dwelling, he stretched. Having stretched, he surveyed the four directions all around. Having surveyed the four directions all around, he uttered a lion’s roar three times. Having uttered a lion’s roar three times, he set out for prey. Having killed the best of the best among the herds of beasts and eaten the tenderest of meats, he then approached that very dwelling.

28. ‘Tasseva [P 3.0024] kho, āvuso pāthikaputta, sīhassa migarañño vighāsasaṃvaḍḍho jarasiṅgālo jarasigālo (sī. syā. pī.) ditto ceva balavā ca. Atha kho, āvuso, tassa jarasiṅgālassa etadahosi – ko cāhaṃ, ko sīho migarājā. Yaṃnūnāhampi aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyaṃ. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhameyyaṃ, āsayā [M 3.0020] nikkhamitvā vijambheyyaṃ, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokeyyaṃ, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadeyyaṃ, tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkameyyaṃ. So varaṃ varaṃ migasaṅghe vadhitvā mudumaṃsāni mudumaṃsāni bhakkhayitvā tameva āsayaṃ ajjhupeyya’nti.

28. Now, friend Pāthikaputta, there was an old jackal, grown corpulent and strong by eating the leftovers of that very lion, the king of beasts. Then, friend, this thought occurred to that old jackal: ‘Who am I, and who is the lion, the king of beasts? What if I too were to establish a dwelling, relying on a certain forest thicket? Having established a dwelling there, in the evening time I would emerge from my dwelling. Having emerged from my dwelling, I would stretch. Having stretched, I would survey the four directions all around. Having surveyed the four directions all around, I would utter a lion’s roar three times. Having uttered a lion’s roar three times, I would set out for prey. Having killed the best of the best among the herds of beasts and eaten the tenderest of meats, I would then return to that very dwelling.’

‘Atha kho so, āvuso, jarasiṅgālo aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappesi. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhami, āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambhi, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokesi, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadissāmīti siṅgālakaṃyeva anadi bheraṇḍakaṃyeva bhedaṇḍakaṃyeva (ka.) anadi, ke ca chave siṅgāle, ke pana sīhanādeti sīhanāde (?).

Then, friend, that old jackal, relying on a certain forest thicket, established a dwelling. Having established a dwelling there, in the evening time he emerged from his dwelling. Having emerged from his dwelling, he stretched. Having stretched, he surveyed the four directions all around. Having surveyed the four directions all around, thinking, ‘I will utter a lion’s roar three times,’ he uttered only a jackal’s cry, he uttered only a wretched sound: ‘What is a wretched jackal, and what, then, is a lion’s roar?’

‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno tathāgate [T 3.0026] arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.

In just the same way, friend Pāthikaputta, while making your living in the dispensation of the Sugata and eating the leftovers of the Sugata, you think it fit to assail the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. What is the wretched Pāthikaputta, and what is the assailing of the Tathāgatas, the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones?

29. “Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī iminā opammena neva asakkhi acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha naṃ etadavoca –

29. When, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wandering ascetic with the wooden bowl, was unable with this simile to make the unclothed ascetic Pāthikaputta move from that seat, he then said this to him:

‘Sīhoti [P 3.0025] attānaṃ samekkhiyāna,

Amaññi kotthu migarājāhamasmi;
