Tatheva tameva (syā.) so siṅgālakaṃ anadi,

Ke ca chave siṅgāle ke pana sīhanāde’ti.

‘Having considered himself a lion, the jackal thought, “I am the king of beasts.” Yet just so, he uttered a jackal’s cry. What is a wretched jackal, and what, then, is a lion’s roar?’

‘Evameva [V 3.0018] kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.

In just the same way, friend Pāthikaputta, while making your living in the dispensation of the Sugata and eating the leftovers of the Sugata, you think it fit to assail the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. What is the wretched Pāthikaputta, and what is the assailing of the Tathāgatas, the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones?

30. “Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī imināpi opammena neva asakkhi acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha naṃ etadavoca –

30. When, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wandering ascetic with the wooden bowl, was unable even with this simile to make the unclothed ascetic Pāthikaputta move from that seat, he then said this to him:

‘Aññaṃ [M 3.0021] anucaṅkamanaṃ, attānaṃ vighāse samekkhiya;

Yāva attānaṃ na passati, kotthu tāva byagghoti maññati.

‘Following after another, seeing his own self grown stout on leftovers, as long as he does not see himself as he truly is, for so long the jackal thinks, “I am a tiger.”’

Tatheva [T 3.0027] so siṅgālakaṃ anadi;

Ke ca chave siṅgāle ke pana sīhanāde’ti.

‘Yet just so, he uttered a jackal’s cry. What is a wretched jackal, and what, then, is a lion’s roar?’

‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.

In just the same way, friend Pāthikaputta, while making your living in the dispensation of the Sugata and eating the leftovers of the Sugata, you think it fit to assail the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. What is the wretched Pāthikaputta, and what is the assailing of the Tathāgatas, the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones?

31. “Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī imināpi [P 3.0026] opammena neva asakkhi acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha naṃ etadavoca –

31. When, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wandering ascetic with the wooden bowl, was unable even with this simile to make the unclothed ascetic Pāthikaputta move from that seat, he then said this to him:

‘Bhutvāna bheke bhiṅge (ka.) khalamūsikāyo,

Kaṭasīsu khittāni ca koṇapāni kūṇapāni (syā.);

Mahāvane suññavane vivaḍḍho,

Amaññi kotthu migarājāhamasmi.

‘Having eaten frogs and threshing-floor mice, and corpses thrown in the charnel grounds, grown large in the great, lonely forest, the jackal thought, “I am the king of beasts.”’

Tatheva so siṅgālakaṃ anadi;

Ke ca chave siṅgāle ke pana sīhanāde’ti.

‘Yet just so, he uttered a jackal’s cry. What is a wretched jackal, and what, then, is a lion’s roar?’

‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno [V 3.0019] tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.

In just the same way, friend Pāthikaputta, while making your living in the dispensation of the Sugata and eating the leftovers of the Sugata, you think it fit to assail the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. What is the wretched Pāthikaputta, and what is the assailing of the Tathāgatas, the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones?

32. “Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī imināpi opammena neva asakkhi [T 3.0028] acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha taṃ parisaṃ āgantvā evamārocesi – ‘parābhūtarūpo, bho, acelo pāthikaputto āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti.

32. When, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the disciple of the wandering ascetic with the wooden bowl, was unable even with this simile to make the unclothed ascetic Pāthikaputta move from that seat, he then went to that assembly and announced: ‘Sirs, the unclothed ascetic Pāthikaputta is defeated! Saying, “I am coming, friend, I am coming, friend,” he just crawls about right there and is not able even to rise from his seat.’

33. “Evaṃ [M 3.0022] vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, āvuso, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya. Sacepāyasmantānaṃ licchavīnaṃ evamassa – mayaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ varattāhi bandhitvā nāgehi goyugehi (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā passitabbā āviñcheyyāmāti[P 3.0027]. Tā varattā chijjeyyuṃ pāthikaputto vā. Abhabbo pana acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

33. When this was said, Bhaggava, I addressed that assembly thus: ‘It is impossible, friends, for the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, to come into my presence. If it were to occur to him, “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, that thought, or that view,” his head would split apart. If the venerable Licchavis were to think, “Let us bind the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta with leather thongs and drag him with elephants,” those leather thongs would break, or Pāthikaputta would break. But it is impossible for the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, to come into my presence. If it were to occur to him, “I will go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that speech, that thought, or that view,” his head would split apart.’

34. “Atha khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesiṃ samādapesiṃ samuttejesiṃ sampahaṃsesiṃ, taṃ parisaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā mahābandhanā mokkhaṃ karitvā caturāsītipāṇasahassāni mahāviduggā uddharitvā tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā sattatālaṃ vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā aññaṃ sattatālampi acciṃ aggiṃ (syā.) abhinimminitvā pajjalitvā dhūmāyitvā [T 3.0029] dhūpāyitvā (sī. pī.) mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ paccuṭṭhāsiṃ.

34. Then, Bhaggava, I instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened that assembly with a Dhamma talk. Having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened that assembly with a Dhamma talk, having made them free from the great bondage, and having uplifted eighty-four thousand beings from the great, hard-to-cross flood, I attained the fire element. Rising seven palm-trees high into the air, and having created another flame seven palm-trees high, blazing and smoking, I reappeared in the great forest in the hall with a gabled roof.

35. “Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yatheva te ahaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ ārabbha byākāsiṃ, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ aññathā vā’ti? ‘Yatheva me, bhante, bhagavā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ ārabbha byākāsi, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, no aññathā’ti.

35. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi’s son approached me; having approached, he paid homage to me and sat down to one side. To Sunakkhatta the Licchavi’s son sitting to one side, Bhaggava, I said this: ‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Was the result just as I declared to you concerning the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, or was it otherwise?’ ‘Venerable sir, just as the Blessed One declared to me concerning the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, so was the result, not otherwise.’

‘Taṃ [V 3.0020] kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yadi evaṃ sante kataṃ vā hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, akataṃ vā’ti? ‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, no akata’nti. ‘Evampi kho [M 3.0023] maṃ tvaṃ, moghapurisa, uttarimanussadhammā [P 3.0028] iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karontaṃ evaṃ vadesi – na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotīti. Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddhaṃ’ti.

‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? If that is so, was a miracle of psychic power beyond ordinary human states performed or not performed?’ ‘Surely, venerable sir, if that is so, a miracle of psychic power beyond ordinary human states was performed, not unperformed.’ ‘Even so, foolish man, while I am performing a miracle of psychic power beyond ordinary human states, you speak thus of me: “Venerable sir, the Blessed One does not perform for me a miracle of psychic power beyond ordinary human states.” See, foolish man, how great this transgression of yours is.’

“Evampi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

Even when being spoken to thus by me, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi’s son indeed departed from this Dhamma and Discipline, just as one destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell.

Aggaññapaññattikathā

The Discourse on the Proclamation of the Foremost

36. “Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi. Tañca pajānāmi “tañcapajānāmī”ti idaṃ syāpotthakenatthi, tato ca uttaritaraṃ pajānāmi, tañca pajānaṃ pajānanaṃ (syā. ka.) aṭṭhakathāsaṃvaṇṇanā passitabbā na parāmasāmi, aparāmasato ca me paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā, yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati[T 3.0030].

36. Bhaggava, I distinctly know what is known as the foremost. I know that, and I distinctly know what is even beyond that. And knowing that, I do not grasp it. For me, who does not grasp, the quenching of defilements is known for myself alone. Directly knowing this, the Tathāgata does not fall into misfortune.

37. “Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā, ‘āmo’ti āmāti (syā.) paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana kathaṃ vihitakaṃno pana (ka.) tumhe āyasmanto issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti. Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi –

37. Bhaggava, there are some ascetics and brahmins who proclaim what is made by a Lord, what is created by Brahmā, and the word of a teacher as the foremost. I approach them and say thus: ‘Is it true, venerables, that you proclaim what is made by a Lord, what is created by Brahmā, and the word of a teacher as the foremost?’ When asked thus by me, they acknowledge, ‘Yes.’ I say to them thus: ‘But in what way, venerables, do you proclaim what is made by a Lord, what is created by Brahmā, and the word of a teacher as the foremost?’ When asked by me, they cannot fully answer, and being unable to fully answer, they question me in return. Being questioned, I explain to them:

38. ‘Hoti kho so, āvuso, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko saṃvaṭṭati. Saṃvaṭṭamāne loke yebhuyyena sattā ābhassarasaṃvattanikā honti. Te tattha honti manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.

38. ‘Friends, there is a time when, sooner or later, after the passing of a long period, this world contracts. When the world is contracting, beings are, for the most part, reborn in the Ābhassara realm. There they are mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-luminous, moving through the sky, abiding in glory, and they remain for a long, long time.

‘Hoti kho so, āvuso, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko vivaṭṭati. Vivaṭṭamāne loke suññaṃ brahmavimānaṃ pātubhavati. Atha kho atha (sī. syā. pī.) aññataro [P 3.0029] satto āyukkhayā vā puññakkhayā vā ābhassarakāyā cavitvā suññaṃ brahmavimānaṃ upapajjati[V 3.0021]. So [M 3.0024] tattha hoti manomayo pītibhakkho sayaṃpabho antalikkhacaro subhaṭṭhāyī, ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhati.

‘Friends, there is a time when, sooner or later, after the passing of a long period, this world expands. When the world is expanding, an empty Brahmā palace appears. Then a certain being, due to the exhaustion of lifespan or the exhaustion of merit, having passed away from the Ābhassara host, is reborn in the empty Brahmā palace. There, that being is mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-luminous, moving through the sky, abiding in glory, and remains for a long, long time.

‘Tassa tattha ekakassa dīgharattaṃ nivusitattā anabhirati paritassanā uppajjati – aho vata aññepi sattā itthattaṃ āgaccheyyunti. Atha aññepi sattā āyukkhayā vā puññakkhayā vā [T 3.0031] ābhassarakāyā cavitvā brahmavimānaṃ upapajjanti tassa sattassa sahabyataṃ. Tepi tattha honti manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino, ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.

‘For that being, having dwelt there alone for a long time, discontent and longing arise: ‘Oh, if only other beings would come to this state of existence!’ Then other beings, due to the exhaustion of lifespan or the exhaustion of merit, having passed away from the Ābhassara host, are reborn in the Brahmā palace into the companionship of that being. They too are there mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-luminous, moving through the sky, abiding in glory, and they remain for a long, long time.

39. ‘Tatrāvuso, yo so satto paṭhamaṃ upapanno, tassa evaṃ hoti – ahamasmi brahmā mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī issaro kattā nimmātā seṭṭho sajitā sañjitā (sī. pī.), sajjitā (syā. kaṃ.) vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānaṃ, mayā ime sattā nimmitā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Mamañhi pubbe etadahosi – aho vata aññepi sattā itthattaṃ āgaccheyyunti; iti mama ca manopaṇidhi. Ime ca sattā itthattaṃ āgatāti.

39. ‘Friends, among them, it occurs thus to that being who was reborn first: ‘I am Brahmā, the Great Brahmā, the Conqueror, the Unconquered, the All-Seeing, the Wielder of Power, the Lord, the Maker, the Creator, the Best, the Ordainer, the Controller, the Father of what has been and what is to be. These beings were created by me. For what reason? Because previously it occurred to me: ‘Oh, if only other beings would come to this state of existence!’ Thus, it is due to my mental aspiration that these beings have come to this state of existence.’

‘Yepi te sattā pacchā upapannā, tesampi evaṃ hoti – ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ brahmā mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī issaro kattā nimmātā seṭṭho sajitā vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānaṃ; iminā mayaṃ bhotā brahmunā nimmitā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imañhi mayaṃ addasāma idha paṭhamaṃ upapannaṃ; mayaṃ panāmha pacchā upapannāti.

‘And for those beings who were reborn later, it also occurs to them thus: ‘This venerable Brahmā is indeed the Great Brahmā, the Conqueror, the Unconquered, the All-Seeing, the Wielder of Power, the Lord, the Maker, the Creator, the Best, the Ordainer, the Controller, the Father of what has been and what is to be. We were created by this venerable Brahmā. For what reason? Because we saw him here, reborn first, whereas we were reborn later.’

40. ‘Tatrāvuso[P 3.0030], yo so satto paṭhamaṃ upapanno, so dīghāyukataro ca hoti vaṇṇavantataro ca mahesakkhataro ca. Ye pana te sattā pacchā upapannā, te appāyukatarā ca honti dubbaṇṇatarā ca appesakkhatarā ca.

40. ‘Friends, among them, the being who was reborn first is longer-lived, more beautiful, and more powerful. But those beings who were reborn later are shorter-lived, less beautiful, and less powerful.

‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati. Itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno [M 3.0025] ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya [T 3.0032] anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati; tato paraṃ nānussarati.

Friends, it is possible that a certain being, having passed away from that company, comes to this state of existence. Having come to this state of existence, he goes forth from the home life into homelessness. Having gone forth from the home life into homelessness, on account of ardor, exertion, application, diligence, and right attention, he attains such a concentration of mind that, when his mind is thus concentrated, he recollects that former state of existence, but he does not recollect beyond that.

‘So [V 3.0022] evamāha – yo kho so bhavaṃ brahmā mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī issaro kattā nimmātā seṭṭho sajitā vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānaṃ, yena mayaṃ bhotā brahmunā nimmitā. So nicco dhuvo sassato dīghāyuko (syā. ka.) sassato avipariṇāmadhammo sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassati. Ye pana mayaṃ ahumhā tena bhotā brahmunā nimmitā, te mayaṃ aniccā addhuvā addhuvā asassatā (syā. ka.) appāyukā cavanadhammā itthattaṃ āgatā’ti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no tumhe āyasmanto issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethāti. ‘Te evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ, yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. “Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi. Tañca pajānāmi, tato ca uttaritaraṃ pajānāmi, tañca pajānaṃ na parāmasāmi, aparāmasato ca me paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā. Yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

He says thus: ‘That venerable Brahmā—the Great Brahmā, the Conqueror, the Unconquered, the All-Seeing, the Wielder of Power, the Lord, the Maker, the Creator, the Best, the Ordainer, the Controller, the Father of what has been and what is to be—by whom we were created, he is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change; he will remain just so forever. But we, who were created by that venerable Brahmā, are impermanent, unstable, short-lived, subject to passing away, and have come to this state of existence.’ Venerables, is it in this manner that you declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning creation by a Lord, creation by Brahmā? They said thus: ‘Indeed, friend Gotama, we have heard it just as the venerable Gotama says.’ Bhaggava, I know the primeval account. I know that, and I know what is even beyond that. And knowing that, I do not grasp at it. Not grasping, the quenching has been known by me for myself. Directly knowing this, the Tathāgata does not fall into misfortune.

41. “Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā ‘āmo’ti paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ [P 3.0031] evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti, tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi [T 3.0033] –

41. Bhaggava, there are some ascetics and brahmins who declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning those corrupted by amusement. I approach them and say this: ‘Is it true, venerable sirs, that you declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning those corrupted by amusement?’ When asked this by me, they admit, ‘Yes.’ I say to them this: ‘In what manner, venerable sirs, do you declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning those corrupted by amusement?’ When questioned by me, they are unable to answer; being unable to answer, they question me in return. I, being questioned, explain to them:

42. ‘Santāvuso, khiḍḍāpadosikā nāma devā. Te ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā hasakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā (ka.) viharanti. Tesaṃ ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannānaṃ viharataṃ sati sammussati, satiyā sammosā satiyā sammosāya (syā.) te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti.

42. Friends, there are gods named the Khiḍḍāpadosikā. They dwell excessively absorbed in laughter, play, and delight. For those who dwell excessively absorbed in laughter, play, and delight, mindfulness is lost. Due to the loss of mindfulness, those gods pass away from that company.

‘Ṭhānaṃ [M 3.0026] kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati, itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati; tato paraṃ nānussarati.

Friends, it is possible that a certain being, having passed away from that company, comes to this state of existence. Having come to this state of existence, he goes forth from the home life into homelessness. Having gone forth from the home life into homelessness, on account of ardor, exertion, application, diligence, and right attention, he attains such a concentration of mind that, when his mind is thus concentrated, he recollects that former state of existence, but he does not recollect beyond that.

‘So evamāha – ye kho te bhonto devā na khiḍḍāpadosikā te na ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā viharanti. Tesaṃ nātivelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannānaṃ viharataṃ sati na sammussati, satiyā asammosā te devā tamhā kāyā na cavanti, niccā dhuvā sassatā [V 3.0023] avipariṇāmadhammā sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassanti. Ye pana mayaṃ ahumhā khiḍḍāpadosikā te mayaṃ ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā viharimhā, tesaṃ no ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannānaṃ viharataṃ sati sammussati, satiyā sammosā evaṃ sammosā eva (sī. pī.) sammosā te (syā. ka.) mayaṃ tamhā kāyā cutā, aniccā addhuvā appāyukā cavanadhammā itthattaṃ āgatāti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no [P 3.0032] tumhe āyasmanto khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti. ‘Te [T 3.0034] evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ, yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. “Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi…pe… yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

He says thus: ‘Those venerable gods who are not the Khiḍḍāpadosikā do not dwell excessively absorbed in laughter, play, and delight. For them, not dwelling excessively absorbed in these things, mindfulness is not lost. Due to mindfulness not being lost, those gods do not pass away from that company; they are permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change, and will remain just so forever. But we who were the Khiḍḍāpadosikā dwelt excessively absorbed in laughter, play, and delight. For us, dwelling excessively absorbed in these things, mindfulness was lost. Due to the loss of mindfulness, we thus passed away from that company, being impermanent, unstable, short-lived, and subject to passing away, and have come to this state of existence.’ Venerable sirs, is it in this manner that you declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning those corrupted by amusement? They said thus: ‘Indeed, friend Gotama, we have heard it just as the venerable Gotama says.’ Bhaggava, I know the primeval account... and directly knowing this, the Tathāgata does not fall into misfortune.

43. “Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā ‘āmo’ti paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti. Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi –

43. Bhaggava, there are some ascetics and brahmins who declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning those corrupted by mind. I approach them and say this: ‘Is it true, venerable sirs, that you declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning those corrupted by mind?’ When asked this by me, they admit, ‘Yes.’ I say to them this: ‘In what manner, venerable sirs, do you declare the primeval account, the teaching of a master, concerning those corrupted by mind?’ When questioned by me, they are unable to answer; being unable to answer, they question me in return. I, being questioned, explain to them:

44. ‘Santāvuso, manopadosikā nāma devā. Te ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyanti. Te ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyantā aññamaññamhi cittāni [M 3.0027] padūsenti. Te aññamaññaṃ paduṭṭhacittā kilantakāyā kilantacittā. Te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti.

44. Friends, there are gods named the Manopadosikā. They gaze intently at one another excessively. As they gaze intently at one another excessively, they corrupt their minds towards one another. With minds corrupted towards one another, they become weary in body and weary in mind. Those gods pass away from that company.

‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati. Itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, tato paraṃ nānussarati.

‘Friends, this case indeed exists: a certain being, having passed away from that company, comes to this state of existence. Having come to this state, he goes forth from the household life into the homeless life. Having gone forth from the household life into the homeless life, by means of ardor, exertion, application, diligence, and right attention, he attains such a concentration of mind that, with his mind so concentrated, he recollects that former existence, but nothing beyond that.

‘So evamāha – ye kho te bhonto devā na manopadosikā te nātivelaṃ [T 3.0035] aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyanti. Te nātivelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyantā aññamaññamhi cittāni nappadūsenti. Te aññamaññaṃ appaduṭṭhacittā akilantakāyā akilantacittā. Te devā tamhā [P 3.0033] akilantacittā tamhā (ka.) kāyā [V 3.0024] na cavanti, niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammā sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassanti. Ye pana mayaṃ ahumhā manopadosikā, te mayaṃ ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyimhā. Te mayaṃ ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyantā aññamaññamhi cittāni padūsimhā padosiyimhā (syā.), padūsayimhā (?). Te mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ paduṭṭhacittā kilantakāyā kilantacittā. Evaṃ mayaṃ kilantacittāeva mayaṃ (sī. pī.), kilantacittā (ka.) tamhā kāyā cutā, aniccā addhuvā appāyukā cavanadhammā itthattaṃ āgatāti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no tumhe āyasmanto manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti. ‘Te evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ, yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. “Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi…pe… yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

‘He says thus: “Those venerable devas who are not corrupted by mind do not gaze intently at one another for too long. As they do not gaze intently at one another for too long, they do not corrupt their minds towards one another. With their minds uncorrupted towards one another, unweary in body and unweary in mind, those devas do not pass away from that company; they are permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change, and will remain just so forever. But we who were corrupted by mind gazed intently at one another for too long. As we gazed intently at one another for too long, we corrupted our minds towards one another. With our minds corrupted towards one another, weary in body and weary in mind, we passed away from that company, being impermanent, unstable, short-lived, and subject to passing away, and have come to this state of existence.” Do you, venerable sirs, proclaim a primeval account of this kind, a teacher’s doctrine concerning those corrupted by mind?’ ‘They said thus: “Indeed, friend Gotama, we have heard it just as the venerable Gotama says.”’ ‘Bhaggava, I understand the primeval account… and directly knowing which, the Tathāgata does not fall into misfortune.’

45. “Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā ‘āmo’ti paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te [M 3.0028] mayā puṭṭhā na [T 3.0036] sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti. Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi –

45. ‘Bhaggava, there are some ascetics and brahmins who proclaim a primeval account, a teacher’s doctrine of fortuitous origination. I approach them and say: “Is it true, venerable sirs, that you proclaim a primeval account, a teacher’s doctrine of fortuitous origination?” When I ask them this, they acknowledge, “Yes.” I then say to them: “But of what kind do you, venerable sirs, proclaim a primeval account, a teacher’s doctrine of fortuitous origination?” When asked by me, they cannot explain; and being unable to explain, they question me in return. When I am questioned, I answer them:

46. ‘Santāvuso, asaññasattā nāma devā. Saññuppādā ca pana te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti.

46. ‘Friends, there are devas called non-percipient beings. And those devas, on account of the arising of perception, pass away from that company.

‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati. Yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati. Itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ idaṃ padaṃ brahmajālasutte na dissati. evaṃ (pī. ka.) saññuppādaṃ anussarati, tato paraṃ nānussarati.

‘Friends, this case indeed exists: a certain being, having passed away from that company, comes to this state of existence. Having come to this state, he goes forth from the household life into the homeless life. Having gone forth from the household life into the homeless life, by means of ardor, exertion, application, diligence, and right attention, he attains such a concentration of mind that, with his mind so concentrated, he recollects that arising of perception, but nothing beyond that.

‘So evamāha – adhiccasamuppanno attā ca loko ca. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ahañhi [P 3.0034] pubbe nāhosiṃ, somhi etarahi ahutvā santatāya sattakāya (sī. pī.), sattāya (ka. sī.) pariṇatoti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no tumhe āyasmanto adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? ‘Te evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. “Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi tañca [V 3.0025] pajānāmi, tato ca uttaritaraṃ pajānāmi, tañca pajānaṃ na parāmasāmi, aparāmasato ca me paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā. Yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

‘He says thus: “The self and the world have arisen fortuitously. For what reason? Because formerly I was not; now, not having been, I have been transformed into a being.” Do you, venerable sirs, proclaim a primeval account of this kind, a teacher’s doctrine of fortuitous origination?’ ‘They said thus: “Indeed, friend Gotama, we have heard it just as the venerable Gotama says.”’ ‘Bhaggava, I understand the primeval account, and I understand that, and I understand what is even beyond that. And understanding that, I do not misapprehend it. And for me, not misapprehending, the quenching has been known for myself. Directly knowing which, the Tathāgata does not fall into misfortune.’

47. “Evaṃvādiṃ kho maṃ, bhaggava, evamakkhāyiṃ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhanti – ‘viparīto samaṇo gotamo bhikkhavo ca. Samaṇo gotamo evamāha – yasmiṃ samaye subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharati, sabbaṃ tasmiṃ samaye asubhantveva asubhanteva (sī. syā. pī.) pajānātī’ti sañjānātīti (sī. pī.). Na [T 3.0037] kho panāhaṃ, bhaggava, evaṃ vadāmi – ‘yasmiṃ samaye subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharati, sabbaṃ tasmiṃ samaye asubhantveva pajānātī’ti. Evañca khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, vadāmi – ‘yasmiṃ samaye subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharati, subhantveva tasmiṃ samaye pajānātī’ti.

47. ‘Bhaggava, some ascetics and brahmins, when I speak and explain thus, falsely, emptily, untruly, and groundlessly misrepresent me, saying: “The ascetic Gotama is perverse, and so are the monks. The ascetic Gotama says: ‘When one enters and dwells in the beautiful liberation, at that time one perceives everything as ugly.’” But, Bhaggava, I do not say: “When one enters and dwells in the beautiful liberation, at that time one perceives everything as ugly.” Rather, Bhaggava, I say: “When one enters and dwells in the beautiful liberation, at that time one perceives it as beautiful.”’

“Te [M 3.0029] ca, bhante, viparītā, ye bhagavantaṃ viparītato dahanti bhikkhavo ca. Evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati. Pahoti [P 3.0035] me bhagavā tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathā ahaṃ subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja vihareyya”nti.

‘Venerable sir, they are the ones who are perverse, those who perversely misrepresent the Blessed One and the monks. I have such confidence in the Blessed One, venerable sir. The Blessed One is able to teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might attain and abide in the beautiful liberation.’

48. “Dukkaraṃ kho etaṃ, bhaggava, tayā aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrāyogena aññatrācariyakena subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharituṃ. Iṅgha tvaṃ, bhaggava, yo ca te ayaṃ mayi pasādo, tameva tvaṃ sādhukamanurakkhā”ti. “Sace taṃ, bhante, mayā dukkaraṃ aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrāyogena aññatrācariyakena subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharituṃ. Yo ca me ayaṃ, bhante, bhagavati pasādo, tamevāhaṃ sādhukamanurakkhissāmī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano bhaggavagotto paribbājako bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

48. ‘It is difficult, Bhaggava, for you—with other views, other persuasions, other preferences, a different practice, and a different teacher—to attain and abide in the beautiful liberation. Come now, Bhaggava, just guard well that confidence you have in me.’ ‘Venerable sir, if it is difficult for me—with other views, other persuasions, other preferences, a different practice, and a different teacher—to attain and abide in the beautiful liberation, then I will indeed guard well the confidence I have in the Blessed One.’ This the Blessed One said. Pleased, the wanderer of the Bhaggava clan rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Pāthikasuttaṃ pāṭikasuttantaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The first Pāthika Sutta is concluded.

2. Udumbarikasuttaṃ

2. 2. The Udumbarika Sutta

Nigrodhaparibbājakavatthu

The Story of the Wanderer Nigrodha

49. Evaṃ [M 3.0030][P 3.0036][V 3.0026][T 3.0038] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena nigrodho paribbājako udumbarikāya paribbājakārāme paṭivasati mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ tiṃsamattehi paribbājakasatehi. Atha kho sandhāno gahapati divā divassa divādivasseva (sī. syā. pī.) rājagahā nikkhami bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Atha kho sandhānassa gahapatissa etadahosi – “akālo kho bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Paṭisallīno bhagavā. Manobhāvanīyānampi bhikkhūnaṃ asamayo dassanāya. Paṭisallīnā manobhāvanīyā bhikkhū. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena udumbarikāya paribbājakārāmo, yena nigrodho paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya”nti. Atha kho sandhāno gahapati yena udumbarikāya paribbājakārāmo, tenupasaṅkami.

49. Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Vulture Peak Mountain. Now at that time the wanderer Nigrodha was residing in Queen Udumbarikā's wanderers' park, together with a large assembly of wanderers, with three thousand wanderers. Then, Sandhāna the householder left Rājagaha in the afternoon to see the Blessed One. Then it occurred to Sandhāna the householder: 'It is not the right time to see the Blessed One; the Blessed One is in seclusion. And it is not the right time to see the monks who develop the mind; the monks who develop the mind are in seclusion. What if I were to go to Queen Udumbarikā's wanderers' park, to where the wanderer Nigrodha is?' So Sandhāna the householder went to Queen Udumbarikā's wanderers' park.

50. Tena kho pana samayena nigrodho paribbājako mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ nisinno hoti unnādiniyā uccāsaddamahāsaddāya anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentiyā. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ [P 3.0037] mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ [T 3.0039] iti vā.

50. Now at that time the wanderer Nigrodha was seated with a large assembly of wanderers, making a loud and raucous noise, engaged in various kinds of worldly talk. That is: talk of kings, talk of thieves, talk of great ministers, talk of armies, talk of dangers, talk of battles, talk of food, talk of drink, talk of clothes, talk of beds, talk of garlands, talk of perfumes, talk of relatives, talk of vehicles, talk of villages, talk of market towns, talk of cities, talk of countries, talk of women, talk of heroes, talk at the crossroads, talk at the watering place, talk of the departed, diverse talk, speculation about the world, speculation about the ocean, and talk about becoming and non-becoming.

51. Addasā kho nigrodho paribbājako sandhānaṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvā sakaṃ parisaṃ saṇṭhāpesi – “appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha. Ayaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako āgacchati sandhāno gahapati. Yāvatā kho pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā rājagahe paṭivasanti, ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataro sandhāno gahapati. Appasaddakāmā [V 3.0027] kho panete āyasmanto appasaddavinītā[M 3.0031], appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino. Appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ.

51. The wanderer Nigrodha saw the householder Sandhāna coming from afar. Seeing him, he quieted his own assembly: 'Be quiet, good sirs, do not make a noise. This is the householder Sandhāna coming, a disciple of the ascetic Gotama. Of all the lay disciples of the ascetic Gotama, dressed in white, who reside in Rājagaha, this householder Sandhāna is one of them. These venerable ones are fond of quiet, trained in quiet, and speak in praise of quiet. Perhaps, knowing the assembly to be quiet, he might consider it fit to approach.' When this was said, those wanderers became silent.

52. Atha kho sandhāno gahapati yena nigrodho paribbājako tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā nigrodhena paribbājakena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sandhāno gahapati nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – “aññathā kho ime bhonto aññatitthiyā paribbājakā saṅgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ [P 3.0038] tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Aññathā kho ca (sī. pī.) pana so bhagavā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppānī”ti.

52. Then the householder Sandhāna approached the wanderer Nigrodha. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the wanderer Nigrodha. Having concluded his courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Sandhāna said this to the wanderer Nigrodha: 'Differently, indeed, venerable sirs, do these wanderers of other doctrines, having gathered and assembled, dwell noisy, with high and loud voices, devoted to various kinds of worldly talk, that is: talk of kings... and talk about becoming and non-becoming. But that Blessed One, differently, resorts to lodgings in forest groves that are remote, with little sound, little clamor, free from the drafts of people, fit for human seclusion, and suitable for solitary retreat.'

53. Evaṃ vutte nigrodho paribbājako sandhānaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “yagghe [T 3.0040] gahapati, jāneyyāsi, kena samaṇo gotamo saddhiṃ sallapati, kena sākacchaṃ samāpajjati, kena paññāveyyattiyaṃ samāpajjati? Suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo nālaṃ sallāpāya. So antamantāneva sevati antapantāneva (syā.). Seyyathāpi nāma gokāṇā pariyantacārinī antamantāneva sevati. Evameva suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā; aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo; nālaṃ sallāpāya. So antamantāneva sevati. Iṅgha, gahapati, samaṇo gotamo imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādeyyāma saṃhareyyāma (ka.), tucchakumbhīva naṃ maññe orodheyyāmā”ti.

53. When this was said, the wanderer Nigrodha said this to the householder Sandhāna: 'Listen now, householder, you should know with whom the ascetic Gotama converses, with whom he engages in discussion, with whom he attains to lucidity of wisdom. The ascetic Gotama’s wisdom is ruined by solitary dwellings; the ascetic Gotama does not frequent assemblies; he is not capable of conversation. He resorts only to the fringes. Just as a one-eyed cow, keeping to the edge of the herd, resorts only to the fringes, so too is the ascetic Gotama’s wisdom ruined by solitary dwellings; the ascetic Gotama does not frequent assemblies; he is not capable of conversation. He resorts only to the fringes. Come now, householder, if the ascetic Gotama were to come to this assembly, with a single question we would make him founder, and I think we would pin him down like an empty pot.'

54. Assosi kho bhagavā dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya sandhānassa gahapatissa nigrodhena paribbājakena saddhiṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohitvā yena sumāgadhāya [P 3.0039] tīre moranivāpo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [M 3.0032] sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkami. Addasā kho nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkamantaṃ. Disvāna sakaṃ parisaṃ saṇṭhāpesi – “appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha, ayaṃ samaṇo gotamo sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkamati. Appasaddakāmo kho pana so āyasmā, appasaddassa vaṇṇavādī. Appeva [T 3.0041] nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyya. Sace samaṇo gotamo [V 3.0028] imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, imaṃ taṃ pañhaṃ puccheyyāma – ‘ko nāma so, bhante, bhagavato dhammo, yena bhagavā sāvake vineti, yena bhagavatā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya’nti? Evaṃ vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ.

54. The Blessed One heard this conversation between the householder Sandhāna and the wanderer Nigrodha with his divine ear element, which is purified and surpasses the human. Then the Blessed One, descending from Vulture Peak Mountain, approached the peacocks' feeding ground on the bank of the Sumāgadhā Pond. Having approached, he walked back and forth in the open at the peacocks' feeding ground on the bank of the Sumāgadhā Pond. The wanderer Nigrodha saw the Blessed One walking back and forth in the open at the peacocks' feeding ground on the bank of the Sumāgadhā Pond. Having seen him, he quieted his assembly: 'Be quiet, sirs, do not make a sound. The ascetic Gotama is walking back and forth in the open at the peacocks' feeding ground on the bank of the Sumāgadhā Pond. That venerable one is fond of quiet and is a speaker in praise of quiet. Perhaps, knowing the assembly to be quiet, he might consider it fit to approach. If the ascetic Gotama comes to this assembly, we will ask him this question: “What, venerable sir, is that Dhamma of the Blessed One by which the Blessed One trains his disciples, and by which his disciples, thus trained, having reached assurance, profess their ultimate reliance, the primal holy life?”' When this was said, those wanderers became silent.

Tapojigucchāvādo

The Discourse on Asceticism and Revulsion

55. Atha kho bhagavā yena nigrodho paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “etu kho, bhante, bhagavā, svāgataṃ, bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā, idamāsanaṃ paññatta”nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nigrodhopi kho paribbājako aññataraṃ nīcāsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kāya nuttha, nigrodha, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti? Evaṃ vutte, nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca, “idha mayaṃ, bhante, addasāma bhagavantaṃ sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkamantaṃ, disvāna evaṃ [P 3.0040] avocumhā – ‘sace samaṇo gotamo imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, imaṃ taṃ pañhaṃ puccheyyāma – ko nāma so, bhante, bhagavato dhammo, yena bhagavā sāvake vineti, yena bhagavatā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā [T 3.0042] paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya’nti? Ayaṃ kho no, bhante, antarākathā vippakatā; atha bhagavā anuppatto”ti.

55. Then the Blessed One approached the wanderer Nigrodha. Then the wanderer Nigrodha said to the Blessed One: “Come, venerable sir, may the Blessed One come! Welcome, venerable sir, is the Blessed One's arrival. It has been a long time, venerable sir, since the Blessed One has made this occasion to come here. May the Blessed One be seated, venerable sir; this seat is prepared.” The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. The wanderer Nigrodha also took a low seat and sat to one side. To the wanderer Nigrodha sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this: “For what discussion are you now assembled, Nigrodha? And what was your conversation that was left unfinished?” When this was said, the wanderer Nigrodha said to the Blessed One: “Here, venerable sir, we saw the Blessed One walking in the open at the peacocks’ feeding sanctuary on the bank of the Sumāgadhā pond. Having seen him, we said this: ‘If the ascetic Gotama were to come to this assembly, we would ask him this question: What, venerable sir, is that Dhamma of the Blessed One by which he trains his disciples, and by which the disciples, trained by the Blessed One, having attained assurance, profess the noble disposition that is the foundation of the holy life?’ This, venerable sir, was our unfinished conversation; and then the Blessed One arrived.”

56. “Dujjānaṃ kho etaṃ, nigrodha, tayā aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrāyogena aññatrācariyakena, yenāhaṃ sāvake vinemi[M 3.0033], yena mayā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ. Iṅgha tvaṃ maṃ, nigrodha, sake ācariyake adhijegucche pañhaṃ puccha – ‘kathaṃ santā nu kho, bhante, tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā hoti, kathaṃ aparipuṇṇā’ti? Evaṃ vutte te paribbājakā unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā ahesuṃ – “acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, samaṇassa gotamassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāma sakavādaṃ ṭhapessati, paravādena pavāressatī”ti.

56. “It is difficult for you, Nigrodha, with your different view, different conviction, different preference, different practice, and different teacher, to know that Dhamma by which I train my disciples, and by which my disciples, trained by me, having attained assurance, profess the noble disposition that is the foundation of the holy life. Come now, Nigrodha, ask me a question concerning your own teacher's doctrine on intense scrupulousness: ‘How, venerable sir, is abhorrence through asceticism complete, and how is it incomplete?’” When this was said, those wanderers became tumultuous, with loud and great sounds, saying: “It is wonderful, sirs! It is marvelous, sirs! How great is the psychic power and majesty of the ascetic Gotama, that he would set aside his own doctrine and invite discussion on the doctrine of another!”

57. Atha kho nigrodho paribbājako te paribbājake appasadde katvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mayaṃ kho, bhante, tapojigucchāvādā tarojigucchaṃsārodā (ka.) tapojigucchāsārā tapojigucchāallīnā viharāma[V 3.0029]. Kathaṃ santā nu kho, bhante, tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā hoti, kathaṃ aparipuṇṇā”ti?

57. Then the wanderer Nigrodha, having quieted those wanderers, said this to the Blessed One: “We, venerable sir, are proponents of abhorrence through asceticism, we hold abhorrence through asceticism as the essence, and we dwell clinging to abhorrence through asceticism. How, venerable sir, is abhorrence through asceticism complete, and how is it incomplete?”

“Idha, nigrodha, tapassī acelako hoti muttācāro, hatthāpalekhano hatthāvalekhano (syā.), na ehibhaddantiko, na tiṭṭhabhaddantiko, nābhihaṭaṃ[P 3.0041], na uddissakataṃ, na nimantanaṃ sādiyati, so na kumbhimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na kaḷopimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na eḷakamantaraṃ, na daṇḍamantaraṃ, na musalamantaraṃ, na dvinnaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ, na gabbhiniyā, na pāyamānāya, na [T 3.0043] purisantaragatāya, na saṅkittīsu, na yattha sā upaṭṭhito hoti, na yattha makkhikā saṇḍasaṇḍacārinī, na macchaṃ, na maṃsaṃ, na suraṃ, na merayaṃ, na thusodakaṃ pivati, so ekāgāriko vā hoti ekālopiko, dvāgāriko vā hoti dvālopiko, sattāgāriko vā hoti sattālopiko, ekissāpi dattiyā yāpeti, dvīhipi dattīhi yāpeti, sattahipi dattīhi yāpeti; ekāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti, dvīhikampi dvāhikaṃpi (sī. syā.) āhāraṃ āhāreti, sattāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti, iti evarūpaṃ addhamāsikampi pariyāyabhattabhojanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. So sākabhakkho vā hoti, sāmākabhakkho vā hoti, nīvārabhakkho vā hoti, daddulabhakkho vā hoti, haṭabhakkho vā hoti, kaṇabhakkho vā hoti, ācāmabhakkho vā hoti, piññākabhakkho vā hoti, tiṇabhakkho vā hoti, gomayabhakkho vā hoti; vanamūlaphalāhāro yāpeti pavattaphalabhojī. So sāṇānipi dhāreti[M 3.0034], masāṇānipi dhāreti, chavadussānipi dhāreti, paṃsukūlānipi dhāreti, tirīṭānipi dhāreti, ajinampi dhāreti, ajinakkhipampi dhāreti, kusacīrampi dhāreti, vākacīrampi dhāreti, phalakacīrampi dhāreti, kesakambalampi dhāreti, vāḷakambalampi dhāreti, ulūkapakkhampi dhāreti, kesamassulocakopi hoti kesamassulocanānuyogamanuyutto[P 3.0042], ubbhaṭṭhakopi ubhaṭṭhakopi (syā.), ubbhaṭṭhikopi (ka.) hoti āsanapaṭikkhitto, ukkuṭikopi hoti ukkuṭikappadhānamanuyutto, kaṇṭakāpassayikopi hoti kaṇṭakāpassaye seyyaṃ kappeti, phalakaseyyampi kappeti, thaṇḍilaseyyampi kappeti, ekapassayikopi hoti rajojalladharo, abbhokāsikopi [T 3.0044] hoti yathāsanthatiko, vekaṭikopi hoti vikaṭabhojanānuyogamanuyutto, apānakopi hoti apānakattamanuyutto, sāyatatiyakampi udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā vā hoti aparipuṇṇā vā”ti? “Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā hoti, no aparipuṇṇā”ti. “Evaṃ paripuṇṇāyapi kho ahaṃ, nigrodha, tapojigucchāya anekavihite upakkilese vadāmī”ti.

“Here, Nigrodha, an ascetic is unclothed, of unrestrained habits, and cleanses with his hand. He does not accept food from one who says, ‘Come, venerable sir!’ nor from one who says, ‘Wait, venerable sir!’ He does not consent to food that is brought forward, specially prepared, or from an invitation. He does not accept food from the mouth of a pot or from the mouth of a basket. He does not accept food placed across a threshold, across a stick, or across a pestle. He does not accept from one of two people eating together, from a pregnant woman, from a nursing woman, from a woman who is with a man, from a collection, where a dog is waiting, or where flies are swarming. He does not eat fish or meat; he does not drink liquor, wine, or fermented rice-water. He is one who takes food from only one house, and only one morsel; or from two houses, and two morsels; up to seven houses, and seven morsels. He subsists on one small bowl, on two small bowls, up to seven small bowls. He eats once a day, once every two days, up to once every seven days. Thus he dwells committed to the practice of eating at intervals, up to half a month. He is an eater of vegetables, of millet, of wild rice, of daddula, of water-plants, of rice-powder, of rice-scum, of sesame flour, of grass, or of cow-dung. He subsists on forest roots and fruits; he eats what has fallen. He wears hemp, coarse hemp, shrouds, rags from a refuse-heap, tree-bark fiber, antelope hide, strips of antelope hide, kusa-grass fiber, bark-strips, a garment of wooden planks, a blanket of human hair, a blanket of horse-hair, or a garment of owl's wings. He is a plucker-out of hair and beard, committed to the practice of plucking out hair and beard. He is one who stands continuously, rejecting seats. He is a squatter, committed to the practice of squatting. He is a thorn-bed-user, making his bed on thorns. He makes his bed on a plank or on the bare ground. He is one who sleeps on one side, a wearer of dust and dirt, one who lives in the open air, one who accepts whatever place is offered. He is an eater of filth, committed to the practice of eating filth. He is a non-drinker, committed to the practice of not drinking water. He dwells committed to the practice of descending into water three times a day, including in the evening. What do you think, Nigrodha? When this is the case, is abhorrence through asceticism complete or incomplete?” “Surely, venerable sir, when this is the case, abhorrence through asceticism is complete, not incomplete.” “Even when abhorrence through asceticism is thus complete, Nigrodha, I declare that it has many kinds of stains.”

Upakkileso

The Stains

58. “Yathā [V 3.0030] kathaṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā evaṃ paripuṇṇāya tapojigucchāya anekavihite upakkilese vadatī”ti? “Idha, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

58. “For what reason, venerable sir, does the Blessed One speak of defilements of many kinds in such a complete revulsion for evil through exertion?” “Here, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice. By that ascetic practice, he is pleased and has his resolve fulfilled. In that, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice, and by that ascetic practice is pleased and has his resolve fulfilled—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice. By that ascetic practice, he exalts himself and disparages others. In that, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice, and by that ascetic practice exalts himself and disparages others—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā majjati mucchati pamādamāpajjati madamāpajjati (syā.). Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so [M 3.0035] tena tapasā majjati mucchati [P 3.0043] pamādamāpajjati. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice. By that ascetic practice, he becomes intoxicated, becomes infatuated, and falls into heedlessness. In that, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice, and by that ascetic practice becomes intoxicated, becomes infatuated, and falls into heedlessness—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

59. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ [T 3.0045] abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

59. “Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice. By that ascetic practice, he generates gain, honor, and renown. By that gain, honor, and renown, he is pleased and has his resolve fulfilled. In that, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice, and by that ascetic practice generates gain, honor, and renown, and by that gain, honor, and renown is pleased and has his resolve fulfilled—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice. By that ascetic practice, he generates gain, honor, and renown. By that gain, honor, and renown, he exalts himself and disparages others. In that, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice, and by that ascetic practice generates gain, honor, and renown, and by that gain, honor, and renown exalts himself and disparages others—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena majjati mucchati pamādamāpajjati. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena [V 3.0031] lābhasakkārasilokena majjati mucchati pamādamāpajjati. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice. By that ascetic practice, he generates gain, honor, and renown. By that gain, honor, and renown, he becomes intoxicated, becomes infatuated, and falls into heedlessness. In that, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice, and by that ascetic practice generates gain, honor, and renown, and by that gain, honor, and renown becomes intoxicated, becomes infatuated, and falls into heedlessness—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

60. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī bhojanesu vodāsaṃ āpajjati – ‘idaṃ me khamati, idaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. So yañca yaṃ hi (sī. pī.) khvassa nakkhamati, taṃ sāpekkho pajahati. Yaṃ panassa khamati, taṃ gadhito gathito (sī. pī.) mucchito ajjhāpanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

60. “Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic becomes discriminating with regard to food, thinking: ‘This is agreeable to me; this is not agreeable to me.’ What is not agreeable to him, he abandons with longing. But what is agreeable to him, he consumes greedily, infatuated, attached, not seeing the danger, and without the wisdom of escape. This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna [P 3.0044][T 3.0046] caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati lābhasakkārasilokanikantihetu – ‘sakkarissanti maṃ rājāno rājamahāmattā khattiyā brāhmaṇā [M 3.0036] gahapatikā titthiyā’ti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an ascetic practice for the sake of craving for gain, honor, and renown, thinking: ‘Kings, royal ministers, nobles, brahmins, householders, and followers of other sects will honor me.’ This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

61. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā apasādetā apasāretā (ka.) hoti – ‘kiṃ panāyaṃ sambahulājīvo bahulājīvo (sī. pī.) sabbaṃ saṃbhakkheti. Seyyathidaṃ – mūlabījaṃ khandhabījaṃ phaḷubījaṃ aggabījaṃ bījabījameva pañcamaṃ, asanivicakkaṃ dantakūṭaṃ, samaṇappavādenā’ti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

61. “Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is one who disparages another recluse or brahmin, saying: ‘Why does this one with an abundant livelihood consume all kinds of seeds? That is to say: root-seeds, stem-seeds, joint-seeds, shoot-seeds, and seed-seeds as the fifth. He is a thunderbolt-wheel, a grinder of food, yet he goes by the name of “recluse”.’ This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī passati aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā kulesu sakkariyamānaṃ garukariyamānaṃ māniyamānaṃ pūjiyamānaṃ. Disvā tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘imañhi nāma sambahulājīvaṃ kulesu sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti. Maṃ pana tapassiṃ lūkhājīviṃ kulesu na sakkaronti na garuṃ karonti na mānenti na pūjentī’ti, iti so issāmacchariyaṃ kulesu uppādetā hoti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic sees another recluse or brahmin being honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated among families. Having seen this, it occurs to him: ‘Indeed, they honor, respect, esteem, and venerate this one with an abundant livelihood among families. But me, an ascetic with a rough livelihood, they do not honor, respect, esteem, or venerate among families.’ Thus, he is one who gives rise to envy and miserliness regarding families. This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

62. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī āpāthakanisādī hoti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

62. “Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is one who sits in a conspicuous place. This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī attānaṃ adassayamāno kulesu carati – ‘idampi me tapasmiṃ idampi me tapasmi’nti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic goes about among families displaying himself, thinking: ‘This, too, is part of my asceticism; this, too, is part of my asceticism.’ This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna [V 3.0032][P 3.0045] caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī kiñcideva paṭicchannaṃ sevati. So ‘khamati te ida’nti puṭṭho samāno akkhamamānaṃ āha – ‘khamatī’ti. Khamamānaṃ [T 3.0047] āha – ‘nakkhamatī’ti. Iti so sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic engages in some concealed act. Being asked, ‘Is this agreeable to you?’, though it is not agreeable, he says, ‘It is agreeable.’ Though it is agreeable, he says, ‘It is not agreeable.’ Thus, he is one who knowingly speaks a falsehood. This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā dhammaṃ desentassa santaṃyeva pariyāyaṃ anuññeyyaṃ nānujānāti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

“Furthermore, Nigrodha, when the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata is teaching the Dhamma, an ascetic does not approve of a point that is indeed valid and should be approved of. This, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

63. “Puna [M 3.0037] caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī kodhano hoti upanāhī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī kodhano hoti upanāhī. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

63. Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is wrathful and resentful. That an ascetic, Nigrodha, is wrathful and resentful—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī makkhī hoti paḷāsī palāsī (sī. syā. pī.) …pe… issukī hoti maccharī… saṭho hoti māyāvī… thaddho hoti atimānī… pāpiccho hoti pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato… sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is denigrating and rivalrous… envious and stingy… deceitful and crafty… stubborn and conceited… with evil desires, under the sway of evil desires… holding wrong view, endowed with a view that grasps at extremes… clinging to his own views, grasping them tightly, and abandoning them with difficulty. That an ascetic, Nigrodha, clings to his own views, grasps them tightly, and abandons them with difficulty—this, too, Nigrodha, is a defilement for the ascetic.

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadime tapojigucchā tapojigucchāya (?) upakkilesā vā anupakkilesā vā”ti? “Addhā kho ime, bhante, tapojigucchā tapojigucchāya (?) upakkilesā upakkilesā hoti (ka.), no anupakkilesā. Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhante, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco tapassī sabbeheva imehi upakkilesehi samannāgato assa; ko pana vādo aññataraññatarenā”ti.

What do you think, Nigrodha? These contemptible aspects of asceticism, are they defilements or non-defilements?" "Surely, venerable sir, these contemptible aspects of asceticism are defilements, not non-defilements. And it is possible, venerable sir, that some ascetic here might be endowed with all these defilements; what then to say of one or another?"

Parisuddhapapaṭikappattakathā

Discourse on Attaining the Purity of the Outer Bark

64. “Idha, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ [T 3.0048] samādiyati, so tena tapasā na attamano [P 3.0046] hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

64. Here, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an austerity practice. By that austerity practice, he is not pleased with himself, nor does he consider his purpose accomplished. In that, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an austerity practice and by that austerity practice is not pleased with himself nor considers his purpose accomplished, in this way he is purified in that respect.

“Puna [V 3.0033] caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā na attānukkaṃseti na paraṃ vambheti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an austerity practice, but by that austerity practice he neither extols himself nor disparages another... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā na majjati na mucchati na pamādamāpajjati…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an austerity practice, but by that austerity practice he is not intoxicated, not deluded, and does not fall into heedlessness... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

65. “Puna [M 3.0038] caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

65. Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an austerity practice, and by that austerity practice he produces gain, honor, and fame. But by that gain, honor, and fame, he is not pleased with himself, nor does he consider his purpose accomplished... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attānukkaṃseti na paraṃ vambheti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an austerity practice, and by that austerity practice he produces gain, honor, and fame. Yet, because of that gain, honor, and fame, he neither extols himself nor disparages another... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena na majjati na mucchati na pamādamāpajjati…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic undertakes an austerity practice, and by that austerity practice he produces gain, honor, and fame. Because of that gain, honor, and fame, he is not intoxicated, not deluded, and does not fall into heedlessness... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

66. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī bhojanesu na vodāsaṃ āpajjati – ‘idaṃ me khamati, idaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. So yañca khvassa nakkhamati, taṃ anapekkho pajahati. Yaṃ panassa khamati[T 3.0049], taṃ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

66. Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic does not make distinctions regarding foods, thinking, 'This is agreeable to me, this is not agreeable to me.' Whatever is not agreeable to him, he abandons without attachment. Whatever is agreeable to him, he partakes of it without greed, without delusion, without being absorbed in it, seeing the danger, and with the wisdom of escape... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na tapaṃ samādiyati lābhasakkārasilokanikantihetu – ‘sakkarissanti maṃ rājāno rājamahāmattā khattiyā brāhmaṇā gahapatikā titthiyā’ti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic does not undertake an austerity practice for the sake of craving gain, honor, and fame, thinking: 'Kings, royal ministers, nobles, brahmins, householders, or followers of other sects will honor me.'... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

67. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā nāpasādetā hoti – ‘kiṃ panāyaṃ sambahulājīvo [P 3.0047] sabbaṃ saṃbhakkheti. Seyyathidaṃ – mūlabījaṃ khandhabījaṃ phaḷubījaṃ [V 3.0034] aggabījaṃ bījabījameva pañcamaṃ, asanivicakkaṃ dantakūṭaṃ, samaṇappavādenā’ti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

67. Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is not one to disparage another ascetic or brahmin, saying: 'Why does this one with his abundant livelihood consume everything? That is: root-seeds, stem-seeds, joint-seeds, shoot-seeds, and seed-seeds as the fifth. He is a "tooth-hammer," like a thunderbolt-wheel, yet he goes by the name of "ascetic"!'... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī passati aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā kulesu sakkariyamānaṃ garu kariyamānaṃ māniyamānaṃ pūjiyamānaṃ. Disvā tassa na evaṃ [M 3.0039] hoti – ‘imañhi nāma sambahulājīvaṃ kulesu sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti. Maṃ pana tapassiṃ lūkhājīviṃ kulesu na sakkaronti na garuṃ karonti na mānenti na pūjentī’ti, iti so issāmacchariyaṃ kulesu nuppādetā hoti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic sees another ascetic or brahmin being honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated in families. Upon seeing this, it does not occur to him: 'This one, living an abundant life, is honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated in families. But I, an ascetic living an austere life, am not honored, not respected, not esteemed, or not venerated in families.' Thus, he is not one to generate envy and avarice regarding families... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

68. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na āpāthakanisādī hoti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

68. Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is not one who sits in a conspicuous place... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na attānaṃ adassayamāno kulesu carati – ‘idampi me tapasmiṃ, idampi me tapasmi’nti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic does not go about in families displaying himself, saying: 'This is part of my ascetic practice, this is part of my ascetic practice.'... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na [T 3.0050] kañcideva paṭicchannaṃ sevati, so – ‘khamati te ida’nti puṭṭho samāno akkhamamānaṃ āha – ‘nakkhamatī’ti. Khamamānaṃ āha – ‘khamatī’ti. Iti so sampajānamusā na bhāsitā hoti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic does not engage in any concealed fault. When asked, 'Is this agreeable to you?' if it is not agreeable, he says, 'It is not agreeable.' If it is agreeable, he says, 'It is agreeable.' Thus, he is not one who knowingly speaks falsehood... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā dhammaṃ desentassa santaṃyeva pariyāyaṃ anuññeyyaṃ anujānāti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, when the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata is teaching the Dhamma, the ascetic acknowledges a point that is truly so and worthy of approval... In this way, he is purified in that respect.

69. “Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī akkodhano hoti anupanāhī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī akkodhano hoti anupanāhī evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

69. Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is not given to anger and does not bear grudges. Insofar as, Nigrodha, the ascetic is not given to anger and does not bear grudges, in that respect he is purified.

“Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī…pe… anissukī hoti amaccharī… asaṭho hoti amāyāvī… atthaddho hoti anatimānī… [P 3.0048] na pāpiccho hoti na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato… na micchādiṭṭhiko hoti na antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato… na sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti na ādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī [V 3.0035] na sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti na ādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī. Evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, an ascetic is not denigrating, not spiteful… not envious, not stingy… not deceitful, not fraudulent… not stubborn, not arrogant… is not of evil wishes, not gone under the sway of evil wishes… is not of wrong view, not endowed with a view that grasps at extremes… is not one who perversely clings to his own view, not one who holds tenaciously to it, but is one who relinquishes it with ease. Insofar as, Nigrodha, the ascetic is not one who perversely clings to his own view, not one who holds tenaciously to it, but is one who relinquishes it with ease, in that respect he is purified.

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā”ti? “Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā [M 3.0040] hoti no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā”ti. “Na kho, nigrodha, ettāvatā tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca; api ca kho papaṭikappattā pappaṭikapattā (ka.) hotī”ti.

“What do you think, Nigrodha? This being so, is the practice of austerity purified or unpurified?” “Surely, venerable sir, this being so, the practice of austerity is purified, not unpurified; it has reached the highest and it has reached the essence.” “Not by this much, Nigrodha, has the practice of austerity reached the highest and reached the essence; rather, it has only reached the outer bark.”

Parisuddhatacappattakathā

The Discourse on Attaining the Purity of the Bark

70. “Kittāvatā [T 3.0051] pana, bhante, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tapojigucchāya aggaññeva pāpetu, sāraññeva pāpetū”ti. “Idha, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti. Kathañca, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti? Idha, nigrodha, tapassī na pāṇaṃ atipāteti atipāpeti (ka. sī. pī. ka.), na pāṇaṃ atipātayati, na pāṇamatipātayato samanuñño hoti[P 3.0049]. Na adinnaṃ ādiyati, na adinnaṃ ādiyāpeti, na adinnaṃ ādiyato samanuñño hoti. Na musā bhaṇati, na musā bhaṇāpeti, na musā bhaṇato samanuñño hoti. Na bhāvitamāsīsati na bhāvitamāsiṃ sati (sī. syā. pī.), na bhāvitamāsīsāpeti, na bhāvitamāsīsato samanuñño hoti. Evaṃ kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti.

70. “But to what extent, venerable sir, has the practice of austerity reached the highest and reached the essence? It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would lead me to the very highest of the practice of austerity, and to the very essence.” “Here, Nigrodha, an ascetic is restrained by the fourfold restraint. And how, Nigrodha, is an ascetic restrained by the fourfold restraint? Here, Nigrodha, an ascetic does not kill a living being, does not cause a living being to be killed, and does not approve of one who kills a living being. He does not take what is not given, does not cause what is not given to be taken, and does not approve of one who takes what is not given. He does not speak falsely, does not cause false speech to be spoken, and does not approve of one who speaks falsely. He does not long for sensual pleasures, does not cause others to long for sensual pleasures, and does not approve of one who longs for sensual pleasures. In this way, Nigrodha, an ascetic is restrained by the fourfold restraint.

“Yato kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti, aduṃ cassa hoti tapassitāya. So abhiharati no hīnāyāvattati. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. So pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodheti. Byāpādappadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādappadosā cittaṃ parisodheti. Thinamiddhaṃ thīnamiddhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodheti. Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ [T 3.0052] pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodheti. Vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodheti.

“When, Nigrodha, an ascetic is restrained by the fourfold restraint, this becomes a component of his asceticism. He develops it and does not revert to the inferior. He resorts to a secluded lodging: a forest, the root of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a jungle thicket, an open space, or a heap of straw. After his meal, having returned from his alms-round, he sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him. Having abandoned covetousness for the world, he dwells with a mind devoid of covetousness; he purifies his mind of covetousness. Having abandoned ill will and malevolence, he dwells with a mind devoid of ill will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; he purifies his mind of ill will and malevolence. Having abandoned sloth and torpor, he dwells free from sloth and torpor, percipient of light, mindful, and clearly comprehending; he purifies his mind of sloth and torpor. Having abandoned restlessness and remorse, he dwells unagitated, with a mind inwardly peaceful; he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse. Having abandoned doubt, he dwells having crossed over doubt, free from uncertainty about wholesome states; he purifies his mind of doubt.

71. “So [M 3.0041][V 3.0036] ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena [P 3.0050] appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

71. “Having abandoned these five hindrances—defilements of the mind and weakeners of wisdom—he dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness. Likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. With a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by appreciative joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, he dwells pervading one direction. Likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will.

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha.
