Yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā”ti? “Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā hoti no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā”ti. “Na kho, nigrodha, ettāvatā tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca; api ca kho tacappattā hotī”ti.

“What do you think, Nigrodha? This being so, is the practice of austerity purified or unpurified?” “Surely, venerable sir, this being so, the practice of austerity is purified, not unpurified; it has reached the highest and it has reached the essence.” “Not by this much, Nigrodha, has the practice of austerity reached the highest and reached the essence; rather, it has only reached the bark.”

Parisuddhaphegguppattakathā

The Discourse on Attaining the Purity of the Sapwood

72. “Kittāvatā pana, bhante, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tapojigucchāya aggaññeva [T 3.0053] pāpetu, sāraññeva pāpetū”ti. “Idha, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti. Kathañca, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti…pe… yato kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti, aduṃ cassa hoti tapassitāya. So abhiharati no hīnāyāvattati. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati…pe… so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā…pe… karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi [M 3.0042] jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi [P 3.0051] jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ, tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo [V 3.0037] evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati.

72. “But, venerable sir, to what extent has revulsion toward ascetic practices reached its peak and its essence? It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would lead me to the very peak and the very essence of revulsion toward ascetic practices.” “Here, Nigrodha, an ascetic is restrained by the fourfold restraint. And how, Nigrodha, is an ascetic restrained by the fourfold restraint? … When, Nigrodha, an ascetic is restrained by the fourfold restraint, this is a mark of his asceticism. He carries it forward and does not revert to a lower state. He resorts to a secluded lodging… Having abandoned these five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—he dwells pervading with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness… with a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will. He recollects his manifold past lives, that is: one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many eons of cosmic contraction, many eons of cosmic expansion, many eons of cosmic contraction and expansion: ‘In that existence, I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance, ate such food, experienced such pleasure and pain, and had such a lifespan. Passing away from there, I was reborn in another existence. There, too, I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance, ate such food, experienced such pleasure and pain, and had such a lifespan. Passing away from there, I have been reborn here.’ Thus, he recollects his manifold past lives with their aspects and details.

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā”ti? “Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā [T 3.0054] hoti, no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā”ti. “Na kho, nigrodha, ettāvatā tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca; api ca kho phegguppattā hotī”ti.

“What do you think, Nigrodha? When this is the case, is revulsion toward ascetic practices purified or unpurified?” “Certainly, venerable sir, when this is the case, revulsion toward ascetic practices is purified, not unpurified; it has reached the peak and it has reached the essence.” “Not so, Nigrodha. To this extent, revulsion toward ascetic practices has not reached the peak, nor has it reached the essence. Rather, it has only reached the sapwood.”

Parisuddhaaggappattasārappattakathā

Discourse on the Pure Attainment of the Peak and Essence

73. “Kittāvatā pana, bhante, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tapojigucchāya aggaññeva pāpetu, sāraññeva pāpetū”ti. “Idha, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti. Kathañca, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti…pe… yato kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti, aduṃ cassa hoti tapassitāya. So abhiharati no hīnāyāvattati. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati…pe… so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ [P 3.0052] anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate, yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena [M 3.0043] samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā [T 3.0055] paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate, yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.

73. “But, venerable sir, to what extent has revulsion toward ascetic practices reached its peak and its essence? It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would lead me to the very peak and the very essence of revulsion toward ascetic practices.” “Here, Nigrodha, an ascetic is restrained by the fourfold restraint. And how, Nigrodha, is an ascetic restrained by the fourfold restraint? … When, Nigrodha, an ascetic is restrained by the fourfold restraint, this is a mark of his asceticism. He carries it forward and does not revert to a lower state. He resorts to a secluded lodging… Having abandoned these five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—he dwells pervading with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness… with a mind accompanied by equanimity—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will. He recollects his manifold past lives… thus he recollects his manifold past lives with their aspects and details. With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and in bad destinations. He understands beings as they fare according to their kamma: ‘Indeed, these honorable beings were endowed with misconduct of body, speech, and mind; they were revilers of the noble ones, held wrong view, and undertook actions based on wrong view. With the breakup of the body, after death, they have been reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. Or indeed, these honorable beings were endowed with good conduct of body, speech, and mind; they were not revilers of the noble ones, held right view, and undertook actions based on right view. With the breakup of the body, after death, they have been reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world.’ Thus, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and in bad destinations. He understands beings as they fare according to their kamma.”

“Taṃ [V 3.0038] kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā”ti? “Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā hoti no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā”ti.

“What do you think, Nigrodha? When this is the case, is revulsion toward ascetic practices purified or unpurified?” “Certainly, venerable sir, when this is the case, revulsion toward ascetic practices is purified, not unpurified; it has reached the peak and it has reached the essence.”

74. “Ettāvatā kho, nigrodha, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca. Iti kho, nigrodha iti nigrodha (syā.), yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ avacāsi – ‘ko nāma so, bhante, bhagavato dhammo, yena bhagavā sāvake vineti, yena bhagavatā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya’nti. Iti kho taṃ, nigrodha, ṭhānaṃ uttaritarañca paṇītatarañca, yenāhaṃ sāvake vinemi, yena mayā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya”nti.

74. “To this extent, Nigrodha, revulsion toward ascetic practices has reached its peak and its essence. Now, Nigrodha, as to what you asked me: ‘Venerable sir, what is that Dhamma of the Blessed One by which the Blessed One trains his disciples, and by which his disciples, having been trained by the Blessed One, attain confidence and profess the goal of the foremost holy life?’ That very state by which I train my disciples, and by which my disciples, having been trained by me, attain confidence and profess the goal of the foremost holy life, is indeed higher and more sublime.”

Evaṃ vutte, te paribbājakā unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā ahesuṃ – “ettha mayaṃ anassāma sācariyakā, na mayaṃ ito bhiyyo uttaritaraṃ pajānāmā”ti.

When this was said, those wanderers became uproarious, making high and great sounds, saying: 'Here we are lost, together with our teacher; we do not know anything more excellent beyond this.'

Nigrodhassa pajjhāyanaṃ

Nigrodha's Brooding

75. Yadā [T 3.0056][P 3.0053] aññāsi sandhāno gahapati – “aññadatthu kho dānime aññatitthiyā paribbājakā bhagavato bhāsitaṃ sussūsanti, sotaṃ odahanti, aññācittaṃ upaṭṭhāpentī”ti. Atha atha naṃ (ka.) nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca [M 3.0044] – “iti kho, bhante nigrodha, yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ avacāsi – ‘yagghe, gahapati, jāneyyāsi, kena samaṇo gotamo saddhiṃ sallapati, kena sākacchaṃ samāpajjati, kena paññāveyyattiyaṃ samāpajjati, suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā, aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo nālaṃ sallāpāya, so antamantāneva sevati; seyyathāpi nāma gokāṇā pariyantacārinī antamantāneva sevati. Evameva suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā, aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo nālaṃ sallāpāya; so antamantāneva sevati; iṅgha, gahapati, samaṇo gotamo imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādeyyāma, tucchakumbhīva naṃ maññe orodheyyāmā’ti. Ayaṃ kho so, bhante, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho idhānuppatto, aparisāvacaraṃ pana naṃ karotha, gokāṇaṃ pariyantacāriniṃ karotha, ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādetha, tucchakumbhīva naṃ orodhethā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, nigrodho paribbājako tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto [V 3.0039] appaṭibhāno nisīdi.

75. When the householder Sandhāna realized—'Indeed, these wanderers of other sects are now eager to listen to the Blessed One’s teaching, they give ear, and set their minds on understanding'—he then addressed the wanderer Nigrodha: 'Now, Venerable Nigrodha, concerning what you said to me—‘Pray, householder, you should know with whom the ascetic Gotama converses, with whom he engages in discussion, with whom he attains expertise in wisdom. The ascetic Gotama’s wisdom is lost in empty places; he does not frequent assemblies and is unable to converse. He frequents only the fringes, just as a one-eyed cow that wanders along the edges frequents only the fringes. In the same way, the ascetic Gotama’s wisdom is lost in empty places; he does not frequent assemblies and is unable to converse. He frequents only the fringes. Come now, householder, if the ascetic Gotama were to come to this assembly, with just one question we would discomfit him. I think we could corner him like an empty pot.’ Well, Venerable Sir, this Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, has now arrived here. Make him one who does not frequent assemblies, make him like a one-eyed cow wandering the edges. With just one question, discomfit him; corner him like an empty pot!' When this was said, the wanderer Nigrodha sat silent, crestfallen, with drooping shoulders, downcast, brooding, and at a loss for a reply.

76. Atha kho bhagavā nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ maṅkubhūtaṃ pattakkhandhaṃ adhomukhaṃ pajjhāyantaṃ appaṭibhānaṃ viditvā nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ [T 3.0057] etadavoca – “saccaṃ kira, nigrodha, bhāsitā te esā vācā”ti? “Saccaṃ[P 3.0054], bhante, bhāsitā me esā vācā, yathābālena yathāmūḷhena yathāakusalenā”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha. Kinti te sutaṃ paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, evaṃ su te bhagavanto saṃgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Seyyathāpi tvaṃ etarahi sācariyako. Udāhu, evaṃ su te bhagavanto araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahī’ti.

76. Then the Blessed One, knowing that the wanderer Nigrodha was silent, crestfallen, with drooping shoulders, downcast, brooding, and at a loss for a reply, said to him: 'Is it true, Nigrodha, that these words were spoken by you?' 'It is true, Venerable Sir, that these words were spoken by me—as befits a fool, as befits one who is deluded, as befits one who is unskillful.' 'What do you think, Nigrodha? What have you heard from the wanderers who are old, senior, the teachers of teachers, as they were speaking: ‘Those who in the past were Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones, did those Blessed Ones gather and assemble together, being uproarious, with high and great sounds, and dwell devoted to various kinds of worldly talk—such as talk about kings, talk about robbers… and so on… talk about being and non-being—just as you now do with your teacher? Or did those Blessed Ones resort to remote forest and woodland lodgings, with little sound, little noise, free from the bustle of people, secluded from human contact, suitable for solitary retreat—just as I do now?'

“Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante. Paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā[M 3.0045], na evaṃ su nāssu (sī. pī.) te bhagavanto saṃgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahi sācariyako. Evaṃ su te bhagavanto araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, seyyathāpi bhagavā etarahī’”ti.

'I have heard this, Venerable Sir, from the wanderers who are old, senior, the teachers of teachers, as they were speaking: ‘Those who in the past were Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones, those Blessed Ones did not gather and assemble together, being uproarious, with high and great sounds, and dwell devoted to various kinds of worldly talk—such as talk about kings, talk about robbers… and so on… talk about being and non-being—just as I now do with my teacher. Rather, those Blessed Ones resorted to remote forest and woodland lodgings, with little sound, little noise, free from the bustle of people, secluded from human contact, suitable for solitary retreat—just as the Blessed One does now.’'

“Tassa te, nigrodha, viññussa sato mahallakassa na etadahosi – ‘buddho so bhagavā bodhāya [T 3.0058] dhammaṃ deseti, danto so bhagavā damathāya dhammaṃ deseti, santo so bhagavā samathāya dhammaṃ deseti, tiṇṇo so bhagavā taraṇāya [P 3.0055] dhammaṃ deseti, parinibbuto so bhagavā parinibbānāya dhammaṃ desetī’”ti?

'For you, Nigrodha, being a discerning and senior man, did this not occur to you: ‘That Blessed One is awakened and teaches the Dhamma for awakening; that Blessed One is tamed and teaches the Dhamma for taming; that Blessed One is peaceful and teaches the Dhamma for peace; that Blessed One has crossed over and teaches the Dhamma for crossing over; that Blessed One is fully extinguished and teaches the Dhamma for full extinguishment’?'

Brahmacariyapariyosānasacchikiriyā

Realization of the Consummation of the Holy Life

77. Evaṃ vutte, nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yvāhaṃ evaṃ bhagavantaṃ avacāsiṃ. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā”ti. “Taggha tvaṃ taṃ (sī. syā. pī.), nigrodha, accayo [V 3.0040] accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yo maṃ tvaṃ evaṃ avacāsi. Yato ca kho tvaṃ, nigrodha, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosi, taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuddhi hesā, nigrodha, ariyassa vinaye, yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Ahaṃ kho pana, nigrodha, evaṃ vadāmi –

77. When this was said, the wanderer Nigrodha said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, a transgression has overcome me—foolishly, deludedly, unskillfully—in that I spoke thus of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One, Venerable Sir, accept my transgression as a transgression, for the sake of future restraint.' 'Indeed, Nigrodha, a transgression has overcome you—foolishly, deludedly, unskillfully—in that you spoke thus of me. But since you see your transgression as a transgression and make amends according to the Dhamma, we accept it of you. For it is growth, Nigrodha, in the discipline of the Noble One, when one sees a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma, and undertakes restraint for the future. But I, Nigrodha, say this—

‘Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ (?) paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati sattavassāni. Tiṭṭhantu, nigrodha, satta vassāni. Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā [M 3.0046] sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ [T 3.0059] pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati cha vassāni. Pañca vassāni… cattāri vassāni… tīṇi vassāni… dve vassāni… ekaṃ vassaṃ. Tiṭṭhatu, nigrodha, ekaṃ vassaṃ. Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati satta māsāni. Tiṭṭhantu, nigrodha, satta māsāni… cha māsāni… pañca māsāni [P 3.0056]… cattāri māsāni… tīṇi māsāni… dve māsāni… ekaṃ māsaṃ… aḍḍhamāsaṃ. Tiṭṭhatu, nigrodha, aḍḍhamāso. Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati sattāhaṃ’.

‘Let a wise man come, one who is not deceitful, not fraudulent, and of a straightforward nature; I will instruct him, I will teach him the Dhamma. Practicing as instructed, he will, in this very life, realize for himself with higher knowledge the unsurpassed consummation of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, will dwell therein for seven years. Let alone seven years, Nigrodha. Let a wise man come, one who is not deceitful, not fraudulent, and of a straightforward nature; I will instruct him, I will teach him the Dhamma. Practicing as instructed, he will, in this very life, realize for himself with higher knowledge the unsurpassed consummation of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, will dwell therein for six years. Five years… four years… three years… two years… one year. Let alone one year, Nigrodha. Let a wise man come, one who is not deceitful, not fraudulent, and of a straightforward nature; I will instruct him, I will teach him the Dhamma. Practicing as instructed, he will, in this very life, realize for himself with higher knowledge the unsurpassed consummation of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, will dwell therein for seven months. Let alone seven months, Nigrodha… six months… five months… four months… three months… two months… one month… half a month. Let alone half a month, Nigrodha. Let a wise man come, one who is not deceitful, not fraudulent, and of a straightforward nature; I will instruct him, I will teach him the Dhamma. Practicing as instructed, he will, in this very life, realize for himself with higher knowledge the unsurpassed consummation of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, will dwell therein for seven days.’

Paribbājakānaṃ pajjhāyanaṃ

The Wanderers’ Brooding

78. “Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘antevāsikamyatā no samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo eva vo te (sī. syā.) ācariyo, so eva vo ācariyo hotu. Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘uddesā no cāvetukāmo samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha[T 3.0060], evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo eva vo uddeso so eva vo uddeso hotu. Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘ājīvā no cāvetukāmo [V 3.0041] samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo eva vo ājīvo, so eva vo ājīvo hotu. Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘ye no dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tesu patiṭṭhāpetukāmo samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Akusalā ceva vo te dhammā vodhammā (ka.), te dhammā (syā.) hontu akusalasaṅkhātā ca sācariyakānaṃ. Siyā kho pana te[M 3.0047], nigrodha, evamassa – ‘ye no dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tehi vivecetukāmo samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kusalā ceva vo te dhammā hontu kusalasaṅkhātā ca sācariyakānaṃ. Iti khvāhaṃ, nigrodha, neva antevāsikamyatā evaṃ vadāmi, napi uddesā cāvetukāmo evaṃ [P 3.0057] vadāmi, napi ājīvā cāvetukāmo evaṃ vadāmi, napi ye vo dhammā napi ye kho dhammā (sī.), napi ye te dhammā (syā.), napi ye ca vo dhammā (ka.) akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tesu patiṭṭhāpetukāmo evaṃ vadāmi, napi ye vo dhammā napi ye kho dhammā (sī.), napi ye te dhammā (syā.), napi ye ca vo dhammā (ka.) kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tehi vivecetukāmo evaṃ vadāmi. Santi ca kho, nigrodha, akusalā dhammā appahīnā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā ponobhavikā (ka.) sadarā saddarā (pī. ka.), sadarathā (syā. ka.) dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā, yesāhaṃ pahānāya dhammaṃ desemi. Yathāpaṭipannānaṃ vo saṃkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodānīyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṃ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme [T 3.0061] sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā”ti.

78. “Nigrodha, you might think: ‘The ascetic Gotama says this because he wants us as his pupils.’ But you should not see it that way. Let him who is your teacher remain your teacher. Nigrodha, you might think: ‘The ascetic Gotama says this because he wants to divert us from our recitation.’ But you should not see it that way. Let your recitation remain as it is. Nigrodha, you might think: ‘The ascetic Gotama says this because he wants to divert us from our way of life.’ But you should not see it that way. Let your way of life remain as it is. Nigrodha, you might think: ‘The ascetic Gotama says this because he wants to establish us in those things that are considered unwholesome among you and your teachers.’ But you should not see it that way. Let those things remain unwholesome as they are considered among you and your teachers. Nigrodha, you might think: ‘The ascetic Gotama says this because he wants to detach us from those things that are considered wholesome among you and your teachers.’ But you should not see it that way. Let those things remain wholesome as they are considered among you and your teachers. Thus, Nigrodha, I do not speak out of a desire for pupils, nor to divert you from your recitation, nor to divert you from your way of life, nor to establish you in things considered unwholesome among you and your teachers, nor to detach you from things considered wholesome among you and your teachers. But, Nigrodha, there are unwholesome states, not yet abandoned, that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fraught with distress, resulting in suffering, and leading to future birth, aging, and death. It is for the abandonment of these that I teach the Dhamma. For those of you who practice accordingly, these defiling states will be abandoned, and purifying states will increase. You will, in this very life, realize for yourselves with higher knowledge the fulfillment and abundance of wisdom, and having attained it, you will dwell therein.”

79. Evaṃ vutte, te paribbājakā tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā appaṭibhānā nisīdiṃsu yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacittā. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “sabbe pime moghapurisā phuṭṭhā pāpimatā. Yatra hi nāma ekassapi na evaṃ bhavissati – ‘handa mayaṃ aññāṇatthampi samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ carāma, kiṃ karissati sattāho’”ti? Atha kho bhagavā udumbarikāya paribbājakārāme sīhanādaṃ naditvā vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā gijjhakūṭe pabbate paccupaṭṭhāsi paccuṭṭhāsi (sī. syā. pī.). Sandhāno pana gahapati tāvadeva rājagahaṃ pāvisīti.

79. When this was said, those wanderers sat silent, dismayed, with shoulders drooping, heads down, brooding, and unable to reply, just as those whose minds are oppressed by Māra. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: ‘All these foolish men have been afflicted by the Evil One. For it does not occur to even one of them: “Come, let us live the holy life under the ascetic Gotama, even for the sake of final knowledge. What can seven days do?”’ Then the Blessed One, having roared a lion’s roar in the wanderers’ park at Udumbarikā, rose into the air and appeared on the Vulture Peak mountain. The householder Sandhāna, for his part, had just entered Rājagaha.

Udumbarikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The Second Udumbarika Sutta is concluded.

3. Cakkavattisuttaṃ

3. The Cakkavatti Sutta

Attadīpasaraṇatā

Being One's Own Island and Refuge

80. Evaṃ [M 3.0048][P 3.0058][V 3.0042][T 3.0062] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā magadhesu viharati mātulāyaṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhaddante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – “attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī…pe… citte cittānupassī…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo.

80. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans at Mātulā. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks!" "Venerable sir," those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: "Dwell, monks, as islands unto yourselves, as your own refuge, with no other refuge; dwell with the Dhamma as your island, with the Dhamma as your refuge, with no other refuge. And how, monks, does a monk dwell as an island unto himself, as his own refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, with no other refuge? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. It is in this way, monks, that a monk dwells as an island unto himself, as his own refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, with no other refuge.

“Gocare, bhikkhave, caratha sake pettike visaye. Gocare, bhikkhave, carataṃ sake pettike visaye na lacchati māro otāraṃ, na lacchati māro ārammaṇaṃ āramaṇaṃ (?). Kusalānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ samādānahetu evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati.

“Dwell, monks, in your own pasture, your own paternal domain. For those dwelling in their own pasture, their own paternal domain, Māra will not find an opportunity, Māra will not find a support. Monks, it is through the undertaking of wholesome qualities that this merit increases.”

Daḷhanemicakkavattirājā

King Daḷhanemi, the Wheel-Turning Monarch

81. “Bhūtapubbaṃ[P 3.0059], bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi nāma ahosi cakkavattī cakkavatti (syā. pī.) dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni [V 3.0043] ahesuṃ seyyathidaṃ – cakkaratanaṃu [T 3.0063] hatthiratanaṃ assaratanaṃ maṇiratanaṃ itthiratanaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā ahesuṃ sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena dhammena samena (syā. ka.) abhivijiya ajjhāvasi.

81. “Once, monks, there was a king named Daḷhanemi, a wheel-turning monarch, righteous, a king of righteousness, ruler of the four quarters, victorious, having attained stability in his country, and endowed with the seven treasures. He possessed these seven treasures, namely: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the adviser-treasure as the seventh. He had over a thousand sons who were brave, heroic in form, and crushers of others’ armies. Having conquered this earth bounded by the ocean without rod, without weapon, by righteousness, he ruled and dwelt therein.”

82. “Atha [M 3.0049] kho, bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘yadā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, passeyyāsi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ, atha me āroceyyāsī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño daḷhanemissa paccassosi. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, so puriso bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ, disvāna yena rājā daḷhanemi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ daḷhanemiṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ te cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cuta’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ āmantāpetvā āmantetvā (syā. ka.) etadavoca – ‘dibbaṃ kira me, tāta kumāra, cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ – yassa rañño cakkavattissa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkati ṭhānā cavati, na dāni tena raññā ciraṃ jīvitabbaṃ hotīti. Bhuttā kho pana [P 3.0060] me mānusakā kāmā, samayo dāni me dibbe kāme pariyesituṃ. Ehi tvaṃ, tāta kumāra, imaṃ samuddapariyantaṃ pathaviṃ paṭipajja. Ahaṃ pana kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā [T 3.0064] agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmī’ti.

82. “Then, monks, after the passing of many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, King Daḷhanemi addressed a certain man: ‘When you, good man, see that the divine wheel-treasure has receded, has shifted from its position, then you should inform me.’ ‘Very well, Your Majesty,’ that man replied to King Daḷhanemi. Monks, after the passing of many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, that man saw that the divine wheel-treasure had receded, had shifted from its position. Having seen this, he approached King Daḷhanemi and said: ‘May Your Majesty know that your divine wheel-treasure has receded, has shifted from its position.’ Then, monks, King Daḷhanemi, having summoned his eldest son, the prince, said this: ‘Dear prince, it seems my divine wheel-treasure has receded, has shifted from its position. And this, indeed, has been heard by me: “When the divine wheel-treasure of a wheel-turning monarch recedes, when it shifts from its position, that king does not have long to live.” Human sensual pleasures have been enjoyed by me; now is the time for me to seek divine sensual pleasures. Come, dear prince, take up this earth bounded by the ocean. As for me, having shaved off my hair and beard and having put on the ochre robes, I will go forth from the household life into homelessness.’”

83. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ sādhukaṃ rajje samanusāsitvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Sattāhapabbajite kho pana, bhikkhave, rājisimhi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antaradhāyi.

83. “Then, monks, King Daḷhanemi, having well instructed his eldest son, the prince, in the kingdom, shaved off his hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness. Monks, seven days after the royal sage had gone forth, the divine wheel-treasure disappeared.”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro puriso yena rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto muddhāvasitto (sī. syā. pī.) evamuparipi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ muddhābhisittaṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antarahita’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto dibbe cakkaratane antarahite anattamano ahosi, anattamanatañca paṭisaṃvedesi. So yena rājisi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājisiṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antarahita’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājisi rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ [V 3.0044] muddhābhisittaṃ etadavoca – ‘mā kho tvaṃ, tāta, dibbe [M 3.0050] cakkaratane antarahite anattamano ahosi, mā anattamanatañca paṭisaṃvedesi, na hi te, tāta, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pettikaṃ dāyajjaṃ. Iṅgha tvaṃ, tāta, ariye cakkavattivatte vattāhi. Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ te ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānassa tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa sīsaṃ nahātassa (sī. pī.), sīsanhātassa (syā.) uposathikassa uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pātubhavissati sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūra’nti.

“Then, monks, a certain man approached the anointed Khattiya king and said: ‘May Your Majesty know that the divine wheel-treasure has disappeared.’ Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king, upon the disappearance of the divine wheel-treasure, was displeased and expressed his displeasure. He approached the royal sage and said: ‘May Your Majesty know that the divine wheel-treasure has disappeared.’ When this was said, monks, the royal sage said to the anointed Khattiya king: ‘Do not be displeased, dear son, at the disappearance of the divine wheel-treasure, nor express your displeasure. For the divine wheel-treasure, dear son, is not your paternal inheritance. Come now, dear son, conduct yourself in the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch. This condition exists, that for you, while conducting yourself in the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch, on the fifteenth Uposatha day, having bathed your head and observing the Uposatha, having gone to the upper terrace of the excellent palace, the divine wheel-treasure will manifest, with a thousand spokes, with its rim, with its hub, complete in all its aspects.’”

Cakkavattiariyavattaṃ

The Noble Duty of a Wheel-Turning Monarch

84. “‘Katamaṃ [P 3.0061] pana taṃ, deva, ariyaṃ cakkavattivatta’nti[T 3.0065]? ‘Tena hi tvaṃ, tāta, dhammaṃyeva nissāya dhammaṃ sakkaronto dhammaṃ garuṃ karonto garukaronto (sī. syā. pī.) dhammaṃ mānento dhammaṃ pūjento dhammaṃ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṃ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidahassu antojanasmiṃ balakāyasmiṃ khattiyesu anuyantesu anuyuttesu (sī. pī.) brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamajānapadesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu migapakkhīsu. Mā ca te, tāta, vijite adhammakāro pavattittha. Ye ca te, tāta, vijite adhanā assu, tesañca dhanamanuppadeyyāsi dhanamanuppadajjeyyāsi (sī. syā. pī.). Ye ca te, tāta, vijite samaṇabrāhmaṇā madappamādā paṭiviratā khantisoracce niviṭṭhā ekamattānaṃ damenti, ekamattānaṃ samenti, ekamattānaṃ parinibbāpenti, te kālena kālaṃ upasaṅkamitvā paripuccheyyāsi pariggaṇheyyāsi – “kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusalaṃ, kiṃ sāvajjaṃ, kiṃ anavajjaṃ, kiṃ sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ na sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya assa, kiṃ vā pana me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya assā”ti? Tesaṃ sutvā yaṃ akusalaṃ taṃ abhinivajjeyyāsi, yaṃ kusalaṃ taṃ samādāya vatteyyāsi. Idaṃ kho, tāta, taṃ ariyaṃ cakkavattivatta’nti.

84. “But what, Your Majesty, is that noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch?” “Then, dear son, relying only on the Dhamma, honoring the Dhamma, respecting the Dhamma, revering the Dhamma, venerating the Dhamma, paying homage to the Dhamma, with the Dhamma as your banner, the Dhamma as your standard, the Dhamma as your supreme authority, you should establish righteous protection, shelter, and guard for your household, your troops, your attendant nobles, for brahmins and householders, for town and country folk, for ascetics and brahmins, and for beasts and birds. And, dear son, let no unrighteous action prevail in your realm. And to those in your realm who are without wealth, you should give wealth. And those in your realm who are ascetics and brahmins, abstaining from intoxication and heedlessness, established in patience and gentleness, who tame themselves, calm themselves, and bring themselves to the quenching of defilements—approach them from time to time to question and investigate: ‘What, venerable sirs, is wholesome, and what is unwholesome? What is blameworthy, and what is blameless? What should be practiced, and what should not be practiced? What, when done by me, would lead to my harm and suffering for a long time? Or what, when done by me, would lead to my welfare and happiness for a long time?’ Having heard them, you should avoid what is unwholesome, and having undertaken what is wholesome, you should practice it. This, dear son, is that noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.”

Cakkaratanapātubhāvo

The Appearance of the Wheel-Gem

85. “‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto rājisissa paṭissutvā ariye cakkavattivatte ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ (ka.) vatti. Tassa ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānassa tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa uposathikassa [M 3.0051] uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pāturahosi sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ. Disvāna [T 3.0066] rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa etadahosi – ‘sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ – yassa rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa tadahuposathe [V 3.0045] pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa uposathikassa uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pātubhavati sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ[P 3.0062], so hoti rājā cakkavattī’ti. Assaṃ nu kho ahaṃ rājā cakkavattīti.

85. “Yes, Your Majesty.” So, monks, the anointed Khattiya king, having assented to the royal sage, practiced the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch. For him, while practicing the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch, on that Uposatha day, the fifteenth, having bathed his head and observed the Uposatha, while on the best upper palace, a divine wheel-gem appeared—with a thousand spokes, with its rim, with its hub, complete in all aspects. Having seen it, it occurred to the anointed Khattiya king: ‘I have indeed heard this: “To whichever anointed Khattiya king, on the Uposatha day, the fifteenth, having bathed his head and observed the Uposatha, while on the best upper palace, a divine wheel-gem appears—with a thousand spokes, with its rim, with its hub, complete in all aspects—he becomes a wheel-turning monarch.” Could I be a wheel-turning monarch?’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ utarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vāmena hatthena bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvā dakkhiṇena hatthena cakkaratanaṃ abbhukkiri – ‘pavattatu bhavaṃ cakkaratanaṃ, abhivijinātu bhavaṃ cakkaratana’nti.

Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king, having risen from his seat, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having taken a water pitcher in his left hand, sprinkled the wheel-gem with his right hand, saying: ‘May the noble wheel-gem roll forth! May the noble wheel-gem conquer!’

“Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ puratthimaṃ disaṃ pavatti, anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Yasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, padese cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāsi, tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, puratthimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ehi kho, mahārāja, svāgataṃ te sāgataṃ (sī. pī.) mahārāja, sakaṃ te, mahārāja, anusāsa, mahārājā’ti. Rājā cakkavattī evamāha – ‘pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ, kāmesumicchā na caritabbā, musā na bhāsitabbā, majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ, yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti. Ye [T 3.0067] kho pana, bhikkhave, puratthimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā anuyuttā (sī. pī.) ahesuṃ.

Then, monks, that wheel-gem rolled forth towards the eastern direction, and the wheel-turning monarch followed right after it with his fourfold army. In whatever region, monks, the wheel-gem stopped, there the wheel-turning monarch took up residence with his fourfold army. The rival kings in the eastern direction then approached the wheel-turning monarch and said: ‘Come, great king. Welcome, great king. It is yours, great king. Instruct us, great king.’ The wheel-turning monarch said: ‘Living beings are not to be killed. What is not given is not to be taken. Sexual misconduct is not to be committed. False speech is not to be spoken. Intoxicants are not to be consumed. And enjoy your revenue as before.’ And so, monks, the rival kings of the eastern direction became followers of the wheel-turning monarch.

86. “Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ puratthimaṃ samuddaṃ ajjhogāhetvā ajjhogahetvā (sī. syā. pī.) paccuttaritvā dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ pavatti…pe… dakkhiṇaṃ samuddaṃ ajjhogāhetvā paccuttaritvā pacchimaṃ disaṃ pavatti, anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Yasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, padese cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāsi, tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, pacchimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ehi kho, mahārāja, svāgataṃ te, mahārāja, sakaṃ te, mahārāja, anusāsa, mahārājā’ti. Rājā cakkavattī [M 3.0052] evamāha – ‘pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ, kāmesumicchā na caritabbā, musā na bhāsitabbā, majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ, yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, pacchimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā [P 3.0063] ahesuṃ.

86. Then, monks, that wheel-gem, having plunged into the eastern ocean and re-emerged, rolled forth to the southern direction… it plunged into the southern ocean and re-emerged, rolling forth to the western direction, and the wheel-turning monarch followed right after it with his fourfold army. In whatever region, monks, the wheel-gem stopped, there the wheel-turning monarch took up residence with his fourfold army. The rival kings of the western direction approached the wheel-turning monarch and said: ‘Come, great king. Welcome, great king. It is yours, great king. Instruct us, great king.’ The wheel-turning monarch said: ‘Living beings are not to be killed. What is not given is not to be taken. Sexual misconduct is not to be committed. False speech is not to be spoken. Intoxicants are not to be consumed. And enjoy your revenue as before.’ And so, monks, the rival kings of the western direction became followers of the wheel-turning monarch.

87. “Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ pacchimaṃ samuddaṃ ajjhogāhetvā paccuttaritvā uttaraṃ disaṃ pavatti, anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Yasmiṃ [V 3.0046] kho pana, bhikkhave, padese cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāsi, tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, uttarāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ehi kho, mahārāja, svāgataṃ te, mahārāja[T 3.0068], sakaṃ te, mahārāja, anusāsa, mahārājā’ti. Rājā cakkavattī evamāha – ‘pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ, kāmesumicchā na caritabbā, musā na bhāsitabbā, majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ, yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, uttarāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā ahesuṃ.

87. Then, monks, that wheel-gem plunged into the western ocean and re-emerged, rolling forth to the northern direction. The Wheel-turning Monarch followed right after, along with his fourfold army. In whatever region, monks, the wheel-gem stood, there the Wheel-turning Monarch took up residence along with his fourfold army. Those other kings of the northern direction approached the Wheel-turning Monarch and said: ‘Come, great king; welcome, great king. It is your own, great king; instruct us, great king.’ The Wheel-turning Monarch said: ‘A living being is not to be killed, what is not given is not to be taken, sexual misconduct is not to be engaged in, what is false is not to be spoken, intoxicants are not to be drunk, and enjoy your revenues as before.’ And so, monks, those other kings of the northern direction became followers of the Wheel-turning Monarch.

“Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ samuddapariyantaṃ pathaviṃ abhivijinitvā tameva rājadhāniṃ paccāgantvā rañño cakkavattissa antepuradvāre atthakaraṇapamukhe aḍḍakaraṇapamukhe (ka.) akkhāhataṃ maññe aṭṭhāsi rañño cakkavattissa antepuraṃ upasobhayamānaṃ.

Then, monks, that wheel-gem, having conquered the earth up to its ocean boundary, returned to that very capital and stood at the entrance to the inner palace of the Wheel-turning Monarch, at the forefront of the hall of justice, as if fixed to the axle, adorning the inner palace of the Wheel-turning Monarch.

Dutiyādicakkavattikathā

The Story of the Second and Subsequent Wheel-Turning Monarchs

88. “Dutiyopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī…pe… tatiyopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… catutthopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… pañcamopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… chaṭṭhopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… sattamopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘yadā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, passeyyāsi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ, atha me āroceyyāsī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño cakkavattissa paccassosi. Addasā kho[M 3.0053], bhikkhave, so puriso bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ [T 3.0069] ṭhānā cutaṃ. Disvāna yena rājā cakkavattī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe[P 3.0064], deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ te cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cuta’nti?

88. Monks, the second wheel-turning monarch… the third wheel-turning monarch… the fourth wheel-turning monarch… the fifth wheel-turning monarch… the sixth wheel-turning monarch… the seventh wheel-turning monarch, after the passing of many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, addressed a certain man: ‘Good man, when you see that the divine wheel-gem has receded, has shifted from its place, then you should inform me.’ ‘Yes, lord,’ that man replied to the wheel-turning monarch. After the passing of many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, that man saw that the divine wheel-gem had receded, had shifted from its place. Having seen this, he approached the wheel-turning monarch and said to him: ‘Pray, lord, know that your divine wheel-gem has receded, has shifted from its place.’

89. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ āmantāpetvā etadavoca – ‘dibbaṃ kira me, tāta kumāra, cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ, ṭhānā cutaṃ, sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ – yassa rañño cakkavattissa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkati, ṭhānā cavati, na dāni tena raññā ciraṃ jīvitabbaṃ hotīti. Bhuttā kho pana me mānusakā kāmā, samayo dāni me dibbe kāme pariyesituṃ, ehi tvaṃ, tāta kumāra, imaṃ samuddapariyantaṃ pathaviṃ paṭipajja[V 3.0047]. Ahaṃ pana kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmī’ti.

89. Then, monks, the wheel-turning monarch had his eldest son, the prince, summoned and said this: ‘My dear prince, it is said my divine wheel-gem has receded, has shifted from its place. And I have heard it said: “For whichever wheel-turning monarch the divine wheel-gem recedes and shifts from its place, that king does not have long to live.” I have enjoyed human sensual pleasures; now is the time for me to seek divine sensual pleasures. Come, my dear prince, you must govern this earth bounded by the ocean. As for me, having shaved off my hair and beard and put on the ochre-dyed robes, I shall go forth from the household life into homelessness.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ sādhukaṃ rajje samanusāsitvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Sattāhapabbajite kho pana, bhikkhave, rājisimhi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antaradhāyi.

Then, monks, the wheel-turning monarch, having properly instructed his eldest son, the prince, in kingship, shaved off his hair and beard, put on the ochre-dyed robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness. And, monks, seven days after the royal sage had gone forth, the divine wheel-gem vanished.

90. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro puriso yena rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ muddhābhisittaṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antarahita’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto dibbe cakkaratane antarahite anattamano ahosi. Anattamanatañca paṭisaṃvedesi; no ca kho rājisiṃ upasaṅkamitvā ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ pucchi. So samateneva sudaṃ janapadaṃ pasāsati. Tassa samatena janapadaṃ pasāsato pubbenāparaṃ [T 3.0070] janapadā na pabbanti, yathā taṃ pubbakānaṃ rājūnaṃ ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānānaṃ.

90. Then, monks, a certain man approached the anointed khattiya king and said, ‘Pray, lord, know that the divine wheel-gem has disappeared.’ Then, monks, when the divine wheel-gem had disappeared, the anointed khattiya king became displeased and experienced displeasure; but he did not approach the royal sage to ask about the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch. He governed the country by his own ideas. As he governed the country by his own ideas, the districts did not prosper as they had for the previous kings who acted in accordance with the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, amaccā pārisajjā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā mantassājīvino sannipatitvā rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ muddhābhisittaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘na [P 3.0065] kho te, deva, samatena (sudaṃ) janapadaṃ pasāsato pubbenāparaṃ [M 3.0054] janapadā pabbanti, yathā taṃ pubbakānaṃ rājūnaṃ ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānānaṃ. Saṃvijjanti kho te, deva, vijite amaccā pārisajjā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā mantassājīvino mayañceva aññe ca aññe ca paṇḍite samaṇabrāhmaṇe puccheyyāsi (ka.) ye mayaṃ ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ dhārema. Iṅgha tvaṃ, deva, amhe ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ puccha. Tassa te mayaṃ ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ puṭṭhā byākarissāmā’ti.

Then, monks, the ministers, councilors, chief accountants, army commanders, doorkeepers, and those who live by counsel, gathered and said to the anointed khattiya king: ‘Lord, as you govern the country by your own ideas, the districts do not prosper as they had for the previous kings who acted in accordance with the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch. In your kingdom, lord, there exist ministers, councilors, chief accountants, army commanders, doorkeepers, and those who live by counsel—both we and others—who uphold the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch. Come now, lord, ask us about the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch. When asked by you, we will explain the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.’

Āyuvaṇṇādipariyānikathā

The Story of the Decline of Lifespan, Beauty, and So On

91. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto amacce pārisajje gaṇakamahāmatte anīkaṭṭhe dovārike mantassājīvino sannipātetvā ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ pucchi. Tassa te ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ puṭṭhā byākariṃsu. Tesaṃ sutvā dhammikañhi kho rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidahi, no ca kho adhanānaṃ dhanamanuppadāsi. Adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ [V 3.0048] theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto [T 3.0071] taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti ādiyasīti (syā.)? ‘Saccaṃ, devā’ti. ‘Kiṃ kāraṇā’ti? ‘Na hi, deva, jīvāmī’ti. Atha [P 3.0066] kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto tassa purisassa dhanamanuppadāsi – ‘iminā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, dhanena attanā ca jīvāhi, mātāpitaro ca posehi, puttadārañca posehi, kammante ca payojehi, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu samaṇesu brāhmaṇesu (bahūsu) uddhaggikaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpehi sovaggikaṃ sukhavipākaṃ saggasaṃvattanika’nti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa paccassosi.

91. Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king assembled his ministers, courtiers, chief ministers skilled in accounting, military experts, gatekeepers, and advisors, and inquired about the noble duty of a Wheel-Turning Monarch. When asked, they explained the noble duty of a Wheel-Turning Monarch to him. Having heard their words, he established righteous protection, guarding, and security, but he did not provide wealth to the destitute. When wealth was not provided to the destitute, poverty became widespread. With poverty widespread, a certain man took what was not given, which is designated as theft. They arrested that man. Having arrested him, they presented him to the anointed Khattiya king, saying: ‘Your Majesty, this man took what was not given, which is designated as theft.’ When this was said, monks, the anointed Khattiya king said this to that man: ‘Is it true, good man, that you took what was not given, which is designated as theft?’ ‘It is true, Your Majesty.’ ‘For what reason?’ ‘Because, Your Majesty, I cannot make a living.’ Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king provided wealth to that man, saying: ‘With this wealth, good man, make a living for yourself, support your mother and father, support your wife and children, engage in work, and establish for ascetics and brahmins a donation that leads to higher realms, results in a good destination, has a pleasant outcome, and is conducive to heaven.’ ‘So be it, Your Majesty,’ that man, monks, replied to the anointed Khattiya king.

“Aññataropi kho, bhikkhave, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ [M 3.0055] kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti? ‘Saccaṃ, devā’ti. ‘Kiṃ kāraṇā’ti? ‘Na hi, deva, jīvāmī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto tassa purisassa dhanamanuppadāsi – ‘iminā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, dhanena attanā ca jīvāhi, mātāpitaro ca posehi, puttadārañca posehi, kammante ca payojehi, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu uddhaggikaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpehi sovaggikaṃ sukhavipākaṃ saggasaṃvattanika’nti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa paccassosi[T 3.0072].

Then, monks, another man also took what was not given, which is designated as theft. They arrested that man. Having arrested him, they presented him to the anointed Khattiya king, saying: ‘Your Majesty, this man took what was not given, which is designated as theft.’ When this was said, monks, the anointed Khattiya king said this to that man: ‘Is it true, good man, that you took what was not given, which is designated as theft?’ ‘It is true, Your Majesty.’ ‘For what reason?’ ‘Because, Your Majesty, I cannot make a living.’ Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king provided wealth to that man, saying: ‘With this wealth, good man, make a living for yourself, support your mother and father, support your wife and children, engage in work, and establish for ascetics and brahmins a donation that leads to higher realms, results in a good destination, has a pleasant outcome, and is conducive to heaven.’ ‘So be it, Your Majesty,’ that man, monks, replied to the anointed Khattiya king.

92. “Assosuṃ kho, bhikkhave, manussā – ‘ye kira, bho, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyanti, tesaṃ rājā dhanamanuppadetī’ti. Sutvāna tesaṃ etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūna mayampi paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyeyyāmā’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ [P 3.0067] vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti? ‘Saccaṃ, devā’ti. ‘Kiṃ kāraṇā’ti? ‘Na hi, deva, jīvāmī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa etadahosi – ‘sace kho ahaṃ yo yo paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyissati, tassa tassa dhanamanuppadassāmi, evamidaṃ [V 3.0049] adinnādānaṃ pavaḍḍhissati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ purisaṃ sunisedhaṃ nisedheyyaṃ, mūlaghaccaṃ mūlaghacchaṃ (syā.), mūlachejja (ka.) kareyyaṃ, sīsamassa chindeyya’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto purise āṇāpesi – ‘tena hi, bhaṇe, imaṃ purisaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ pacchābāhuṃ (syā.) gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhamitvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sunisedhaṃ nisedhetha, mūlaghaccaṃ karotha, sīsamassa chindathā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti [T 3.0073] kho, bhikkhave, te purisā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa paṭissutvā taṃ purisaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā [M 3.0056] dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhamitvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sunisedhaṃ nisedhesuṃ, mūlaghaccaṃ akaṃsu, sīsamassa chindiṃsu.

92. The people heard, monks: ‘It is said, sirs, that the king provides wealth to those who take what is not given, which is designated as theft.’ Having heard this, the thought occurred to them: ‘What if we too were to take what is not given, which is designated as theft?’ Then, monks, a certain man took what was not given, which is designated as theft. They arrested that man. Having arrested him, they presented him to the anointed Khattiya king, saying: ‘Your Majesty, this man took what was not given, which is designated as theft.’ When this was said, monks, the anointed Khattiya king said this to that man: ‘Is it true, good man, that you took what was not given, which is designated as theft?’ ‘It is true, Your Majesty.’ ‘For what reason?’ ‘Because, Your Majesty, I cannot make a living.’ Then, monks, this thought occurred to the anointed Khattiya king: ‘If I provide wealth to everyone who takes what is not given, which is designated as theft, this taking of what is not given will increase. What if I were to severely punish this man, to uproot him, to cut off his head?’ Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king ordered his men: ‘Well then, sirs, bind this man’s arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope, shave his head, and with a harsh-sounding drum lead him from street to street and from crossroad to crossroad. Having led him out through the southern gate, to the south of the city, severely punish him, uproot him, and cut off his head.’ ‘So be it, Your Majesty,’ those men, monks, replied to the anointed Khattiya king. They bound that man’s arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope, shaved his head, and with a harsh-sounding drum led him from street to street and from crossroad to crossroad. Having led him out through the southern gate, to the south of the city, they severely punished him, uprooted him, and cut off his head.

93. “Assosuṃ kho, bhikkhave, manussā – ‘ye kira, bho, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyanti, te rājā sunisedhaṃ nisedheti, mūlaghaccaṃ karoti, sīsāni tesaṃ chindatī’ti. Sutvāna tesaṃ etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūna mayampi tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpessāma kārāpeyyāma (syā. pī.) kārāpeyyāmāti (ka. sī.), tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpetvā yesaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyissāma, te sunisedhaṃ [P 3.0068] nisedhessāma, mūlaghaccaṃ karissāma, sīsāni tesaṃ chindissāmā’ti. Te tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpesuṃ, tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpetvā gāmaghātampi upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ, nigamaghātampi upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ, nagaraghātampi upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ, panthaduhanampi panthadūhanaṃpi (sī. syā. pī.) upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ. Yesaṃ te adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyanti, te sunisedhaṃ nisedhenti, mūlaghaccaṃ karonti, sīsāni tesaṃ chindanti.

93. Bhikkhus, people heard: ‘Sirs, it is said that for those who take what is not given, designated as theft, the king severely prohibits them, uproots them, and cuts off their heads.’ Having heard this, it occurred to them: ‘What if we too have sharp weapons made? Having had sharp weapons made, we shall severely prohibit, uproot, and cut off the heads of those from whom we shall take what is not given, designated as theft.’ They had sharp weapons made, and having had sharp weapons made, they began to commit village-plundering, they began to commit town-plundering, they began to commit city-plundering, and they began to commit highway robbery. They severely prohibit, uproot, and cut off the heads of those from whom they take what is not given, designated as theft.

94. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi, dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi, adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi, satthe [T 3.0074] vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi, pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ asītivassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārīsavassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

94. Thus, bhikkhus, when wealth was not provided to the destitute, poverty became widespread. With poverty having become widespread, taking what is not given became widespread. With taking what is not given having become widespread, weapons became widespread. With weapons having become widespread, the destruction of life became widespread. With the destruction of life having become widespread, the lifespan of those beings declined, and their complexion declined. For those who were declining in lifespan and complexion, the children of humans with a lifespan of eighty thousand years had a lifespan of forty thousand years.

“Cattārīsavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo [V 3.0050] muddhābhisitto taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti? ‘Na hi, devā’ti sampajānamusā abhāsi.

Bhikkhus, among humans with a lifespan of forty thousand years, a certain man took what was not given, designated as theft. They seized him. Having seized him, they presented him to the anointed Khattiya king, saying: ‘Your Majesty, this man took what was not given, designated as theft.’ When this was said, bhikkhus, the anointed Khattiya king said this to the man: ‘Is it true, good man, that you took what was not given, designated as theft?’ ‘It is not so, Your Majesty,’ he said, knowingly speaking a falsehood.

95. “Iti [M 3.0057] kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi, adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Satthe vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi, pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate musāvādo vepullamagamāsi[P 3.0069], musāvāde vepullaṃ gate tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ cattārīsavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsativassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

95. Thus, bhikkhus, when wealth was not provided to the destitute, poverty became widespread. With poverty having become widespread, taking what is not given became widespread. With taking what is not given having become widespread, weapons became widespread. With weapons having become widespread, the destruction of life became widespread. With the destruction of life having become widespread, false speech became widespread. With false speech having become widespread, the lifespan of those beings declined, and their complexion declined. For those who were declining in lifespan and complexion, the children of humans with a lifespan of forty thousand years had a lifespan of twenty thousand years.

“Vīsativassasahassāyukesu[T 3.0075], bhikkhave, manussesu aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aññataro puriso rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa ārocesi – ‘itthannāmo, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti pesuññamakāsi.

Bhikkhus, among humans with a lifespan of twenty thousand years, a certain man took what was not given, designated as theft. Another man reported him to the anointed Khattiya king, saying: ‘Your Majesty, the man named so-and-so took what was not given, designated as theft.’ He engaged in slanderous speech.

96. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi, adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi, satthe vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi, pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate musāvādo vepullamagamāsi, musāvāde vepullaṃ gate pisuṇā vācā vepullamagamāsi, pisuṇāya vācāya vepullaṃ gatāya tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ vīsativassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ dasavassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

96. Thus, bhikkhus, when wealth was not provided to the destitute, poverty became widespread. With poverty having become widespread, taking what is not given became widespread. With taking what is not given having become widespread, weapons became widespread. With weapons having become widespread, the destruction of life became widespread. With the destruction of life having become widespread, false speech became widespread. With false speech having become widespread, slanderous speech became widespread. With slanderous speech having become widespread, the lifespan of those beings declined, and their complexion declined. For those who were declining in lifespan and complexion, the children of humans with a lifespan of twenty thousand years had a lifespan of ten thousand years.

“Dasavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ekidaṃ sattā vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā dubbaṇṇā, te vaṇṇavante satte abhijjhāyantā paresaṃ dāresu cārittaṃ āpajjiṃsu.

Bhikkhus, among humans with a lifespan of ten thousand years, some beings were beautiful, and some beings were ugly. Therein, those beings who were ugly, coveting the beautiful beings, fell into transgression with the wives of others.

97. “Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate…pe… kāmesumicchācāro vepullamagamāsi, kāmesumicchācāre vepullaṃ gate tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi [V 3.0051] parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi [M 3.0058] parihāyamānānaṃ dasavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ pañcavassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

97. Thus, bhikkhus, when wealth was not provided to the destitute, poverty became widespread. With poverty having become widespread… and so on… sexual misconduct became widespread. With sexual misconduct having become widespread, the lifespan of those beings declined, and their complexion declined. For those who were declining in lifespan and complexion, the children of humans with a lifespan of ten thousand years had a lifespan of five thousand years.

98. “Pañcavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave[T 3.0076], manussesu dve dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu – pharusāvācā samphappalāpo ca. Dvīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ pañcavassasahassāyukānaṃ [P 3.0070] manussānaṃ appekacce aḍḍhateyyavassasahassāyukā, appekacce dvevassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

98. Bhikkhus, among humans with a lifespan of five thousand years, two things became widespread: harsh speech and frivolous talk. With these two things having become widespread, the lifespan of those beings declined, and their complexion declined. For those who were declining in lifespan and complexion, among the children of humans with a lifespan of five thousand years, some had a lifespan of two thousand five hundred years, and some had a lifespan of two thousand years.

99. “Aḍḍhateyyavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu abhijjhābyāpādā vepullamagamaṃsu. Abhijjhābyāpādesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ aḍḍhateyyavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

99. Monks, among humans with a lifespan of two thousand five hundred years, covetousness and ill will became widespread. As covetousness and ill will became widespread, the lifespan and complexion of those beings declined. As their lifespan and complexion declined, the humans with a lifespan of two thousand five hundred years had children with a lifespan of a thousand years.

100. “Vassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu micchādiṭṭhi vepullamagamāsi. Micchādiṭṭhiyā vepullaṃ gatāya tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ vassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ pañcavassasatāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

100. Monks, among humans with a lifespan of a thousand years, wrong view became widespread. As wrong view became widespread, the lifespan and complexion of those beings declined. As their lifespan and complexion declined, the humans with a lifespan of a thousand years had children with a lifespan of five hundred years.

101. “Pañcavassasatāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu tayo dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu. Adhammarāgo visamalobho micchādhammo. Tīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ pañcavassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ appekacce aḍḍhateyyavassasatāyukā, appekacce dvevassasatāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

101. Monks, among humans with a lifespan of five hundred years, three things became widespread: unrighteous lust, excessive greed, and wrong practice. As these three things became widespread, the lifespan and complexion of those beings declined. As their lifespan and complexion declined, the humans with a lifespan of five hundred years had children, some with a lifespan of two hundred and fifty years, and some with a lifespan of two hundred years.

“Aḍḍhateyyavassasatāyukesu, bhikkhave[T 3.0077], manussesu ime dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu. Amatteyyatā apetteyyatā asāmaññatā abrahmaññatā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā.

Monks, among humans with a lifespan of two hundred and fifty years, these things became widespread: lack of good conduct towards mothers, lack of good conduct towards fathers, lack of good conduct towards ascetics, lack of good conduct towards brahmins, and not honoring the elders of the family.

102. “Iti [M 3.0059] kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate [V 3.0052] satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Satthe vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi. Pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate musāvādo vepullamagamāsi. Musāvāde vepullaṃ gate pisuṇā vācā vepullamagamāsi. Pisuṇāya vācāya vepullaṃ gatāya kāmesumicchācāro vepullamagamāsi. Kāmesumicchācāre vepullaṃ gate [P 3.0071] dve dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu, pharusā vācā samphappalāpo ca. Dvīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu abhijjhābyāpādā vepullamagamaṃsu. Abhijjhābyāpādesu vepullaṃ gatesu micchādiṭṭhi vepullamagamāsi. Micchādiṭṭhiyā vepullaṃ gatāya tayo dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu, adhammarāgo visamalobho micchādhammo. Tīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu ime dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu, amatteyyatā apetteyyatā asāmaññatā abrahmaññatā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā. Imesu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ aḍḍhateyyavassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vassasatāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

102. Thus, monks, when wealth was not given to the poor, poverty became widespread. As poverty became widespread, taking what is not given became widespread. As taking what is not given became widespread, weapons became widespread. As weapons became widespread, killing living beings became widespread. As killing living beings became widespread, false speech became widespread. As false speech became widespread, slanderous speech became widespread. As slanderous speech became widespread, sexual misconduct became widespread. As sexual misconduct became widespread, two things became widespread: harsh speech and frivolous talk. As these two things became widespread, covetousness and ill will became widespread. As covetousness and ill will became widespread, wrong view became widespread. As wrong view became widespread, three things became widespread: unrighteous lust, excessive greed, and wrong practice. As these three things became widespread, these things became widespread: lack of good conduct towards mothers, lack of good conduct towards fathers, lack of good conduct towards ascetics, lack of good conduct towards brahmins, and not honoring the elders of the family. As these things became widespread, the lifespan and complexion of those beings declined. As their lifespan and complexion declined, the humans with a lifespan of two hundred and fifty years had children with a lifespan of one hundred years.

Dasavassāyukasamayo

The Era of Ten-Year Lifespans

103. “Bhavissati[T 3.0078], bhikkhave, so samayo, yaṃ imesaṃ manussānaṃ dasavassāyukā puttā bhavissanti. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu pañcavassikā pañcamāsikā (ka. sī.) kumārikā alaṃpateyyā bhavissanti. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu imāni rasāni antaradhāyissanti, seyyathidaṃ, sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ loṇaṃ. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu kudrūsako aggaṃ bhojanānaṃ aggabhojanaṃ (syā.) bhavissati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, etarahi sālimaṃsodano aggaṃ bhojanānaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dasavassāyukesu manussesu kudrūsako aggaṃ bhojanānaṃ bhavissati.

103. Monks, there will be a time when the offspring of these humans will have a lifespan of ten years. Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, five-year-old girls will be suitable for marriage. Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, these flavors will disappear, namely: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, molasses, and salt. Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, coarse grain will be the foremost of foods. Just as now, monks, fine rice with meat is the foremost of foods, so too, monks, among humans with a ten-year lifespan, coarse grain will be the foremost of foods.

“Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu dasa kusalakammapathā sabbena sabbaṃ antaradhāyissanti, dasa akusalakammapathā atibyādippissanti ativiya dippissanti (syā. pī.), ativyādippissanti (sī.). Dasavassāyukesu[M 3.0060], bhikkhave, manussesu kusalantipi na bhavissati, kuto pana kusalassa kārako. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ye te bhavissanti amatteyyā [P 3.0072] apetteyyā asāmaññā abrahmaññā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, te pujjā ca bhavissanti pāsaṃsā ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, etarahi matteyyā petteyyā sāmaññā brahmaññā kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino pujjā ca pāsaṃsā ca; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dasavassāyukesu manussesu ye te bhavissanti amatteyyā apetteyyā asāmaññā abrahmaññā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, te pujjā ca bhavissanti pāsaṃsā ca.

Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, the ten wholesome courses of action will completely disappear, and the ten unwholesome courses of action will become exceedingly prominent. Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, even the word ‘wholesome’ will not exist, so how then could there be one who does what is wholesome? Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, those who do not treat their mothers well, do not treat their fathers well, do not treat ascetics well, do not treat brahmins well, and do not honor the elders of their family—they will be the ones who are venerated and praised. Just as now, monks, those who treat their mothers well, treat their fathers well, treat ascetics well, treat brahmins well, and honor the elders of their family are venerated and praised; even so, monks, among humans with a ten-year lifespan, those who do not treat their mothers well, do not treat their fathers well, do not treat ascetics well, do not treat brahmins well, and do not honor the elders of their family—they will be the ones who are venerated and praised.

“Dasavassāyukesu[V 3.0053], bhikkhave, manussesu na bhavissati mātāti [T 3.0079] vā mātucchāti vā mātulānīti vā ācariyabhariyāti vā garūnaṃ dārāti vā. Sambhedaṃ loko gamissati yathā ajeḷakā kukkuṭasūkarā soṇasiṅgālā soṇasigālā (sī. pī.).

Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, there will be no designation of ‘mother,’ nor ‘maternal aunt,’ nor ‘maternal uncle’s wife,’ nor ‘teacher’s wife,’ nor ‘wives of respected elders.’ The world will fall into promiscuity, just like goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, dogs and jackals.

“Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ aññamaññamhi tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ. Mātupi puttamhi puttassapi mātari; pitupi puttamhi puttassapi pitari; bhātupi bhaginiyā bhaginiyāpi bhātari tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, māgavikassa migaṃ disvā tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito hoti tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dasavassāyukesu manussesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ aññamaññamhi tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ. Mātupi puttamhi puttassapi mātari; pitupi puttamhi puttassapi pitari; bhātupi bhaginiyā bhaginiyāpi bhātari tibbo āghāto [P 3.0073] paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ.
