“Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, there will arise among those beings intense hatred for one another, intense ill will, intense malevolence, and intense murderous intent. A mother will have this for her son, and a son for his mother; a father for his son, and a son for his father; a brother for his sister, and a sister for her brother. There will arise intense hatred, intense ill will, intense malevolence, and intense murderous intent. Just as, monks, a hunter, upon seeing a deer, feels intense hatred, intense ill will, intense malevolence, and intense murderous intent; even so, monks, among humans with a ten-year lifespan, there will arise among those beings intense hatred for one another, intense ill will, intense malevolence, and intense murderous intent. A mother will have this for her son, and a son for his mother; a father for his son, and a son for his father; a brother for his sister, and a sister for her brother. There will arise intense hatred, intense ill will, intense malevolence, and intense murderous intent.”

104. “Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu sattāhaṃ satthantarakappo bhavissati. Te aññamaññamhi migasaññaṃ paṭilabhissanti. Tesaṃ tiṇhāni [T 3.0080] satthāni [M 3.0061] hatthesu pātubhavissanti. Te tiṇhena satthena ‘esa migo esa migo’ti aññamaññaṃ jīvitā voropessanti.

104. “Among humans with a ten-year lifespan, monks, there will be a sword-interval calamity lasting for seven days. They will perceive one another as wild beasts. Sharp weapons will appear in their hands. With these sharp weapons, thinking, ‘This is a wild beast! This is a wild beast!’, they will deprive one another of life.”

“Atha kho tesaṃ, bhikkhave, sattānaṃ ekaccānaṃ evaṃ bhavissati – ‘mā ca mayaṃ kañci kiñci (ka.), mā ca amhe koci, yaṃnūna mayaṃ tiṇagahanaṃ vā vanagahanaṃ vā rukkhagahanaṃ vā nadīviduggaṃ vā pabbatavisamaṃ vā pavisitvā vanamūlaphalāhārā yāpeyyāmā’ti. Te tiṇagahanaṃ vā vanagahanaṃ vā rukkhagahanaṃ vā nadīviduggaṃ vā pabbatavisamaṃ vā te tiṇagahanaṃ vanagahanaṃ rukkhagahanaṃ nadīviduggaṃ pabbatavisamaṃ (sī. pī.) pavisitvā sattāhaṃ vanamūlaphalāhārā yāpessanti. Te tassa sattāhassa accayena tiṇagahanā vanagahanā rukkhagahanā nadīviduggā pabbatavisamā nikkhamitvā aññamaññaṃ āliṅgitvā sabhāgāyissanti samassāsissanti – ‘diṭṭhā, bho, sattā jīvasi, diṭṭhā, bho, sattā jīvasī’ti.

“Then, monks, this thought will occur to some of those beings: ‘Let us not kill anyone, and let no one kill us. What if we were to enter a grass thicket, a forest thicket, a thicket of trees, an impassable river region, or a rugged mountain area, and sustain ourselves on forest roots and fruits?’ They will enter a grass thicket, a forest thicket, a thicket of trees, an impassable river region, or a rugged mountain area, and for seven days they will sustain themselves on forest roots and fruits. After the passing of those seven days, they will emerge from those grass thickets, forest thickets, thickets of trees, impassable river regions, and rugged mountain areas, embrace one another, and rejoice together, consoling one another, saying: ‘It is a blessing to see you, friend! You are alive! It is a blessing to see you, friend! You are alive!’”

Āyuvaṇṇādivaḍḍhanakathā

The Discourse on the Increase of Lifespan, Beauty, and Other Qualities

105. “Atha [V 3.0054] kho tesaṃ, bhikkhave, sattānaṃ evaṃ bhavissati – ‘mayaṃ kho akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu evarūpaṃ āyataṃ ñātikkhayaṃ pattā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ kusalaṃ kareyyāma. Kiṃ kusalaṃ kareyyāma? Yaṃnūna mayaṃ pāṇātipātā virameyyāma, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vatteyyāmā’ti. Te pāṇātipātā viramissanti, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vattissanti. Te kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu āyunāpi vaḍḍhissanti, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissanti[P 3.0074]. Tesaṃ āyunāpi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ dasavassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsativassāyukā puttā bhavissanti.

105. “Then, monks, this thought will arise in those beings: ‘It is because we undertook unwholesome qualities that we have come to such a great destruction of our kin. Let us now do what is wholesome. What wholesome deed should we do? Let us abstain from the destruction of life; let us undertake and live by this wholesome quality.’ They will abstain from the destruction of life; they will undertake and live by this wholesome quality. Because they have undertaken wholesome qualities, they will increase in lifespan and in beauty. For those who are increasing in lifespan and beauty, the children of humans with a ten-year lifespan will have a lifespan of twenty years.”

“Atha kho tesaṃ, bhikkhave, sattānaṃ evaṃ bhavissati – ‘mayaṃ kho kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ [T 3.0081] samādānahetu āyunāpi vaḍḍhāma, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhāma. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ bhiyyosomattāya kusalaṃ kareyyāma. Kiṃ kusalaṃ kareyyāma? Yaṃnūna mayaṃ adinnādānā virameyyāma… kāmesumicchācārā virameyyāma… musāvādā virameyyāma… pisuṇāya vācāya virameyyāma… pharusāya vācāya virameyyāma… samphappalāpā virameyyāma… abhijjhaṃ pajaheyyāma… byāpādaṃ pajaheyyāma… micchādiṭṭhiṃ pajaheyyāma… tayo dhamme pajaheyyāma – adhammarāgaṃ visamalobhaṃ micchādhammaṃ… yaṃnūna mayaṃ matteyyā assāma petteyyā sāmaññā brahmaññā kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vatteyyāmā’ti. Te matteyyā bhavissanti petteyyā sāmaññā [M 3.0062] brahmaññā kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vattissanti.

“Then, monks, this thought will arise in those beings: ‘It is because we undertook wholesome qualities that we are increasing in lifespan and in beauty. Let us now do even more wholesome deeds. What wholesome deeds should we do? Let us abstain from taking what is not given… from sexual misconduct… from false speech… from divisive speech… from harsh speech… from idle chatter… let us abandon covetousness… ill will… and wrong view… let us abandon these three things: unrighteous lust, wrongful greed, and wrong practice… Let us be dutiful to our mothers, dutiful to our fathers, dutiful to ascetics, dutiful to brahmins, and honor the elders of the family. Let us undertake and live by this wholesome quality.’ They will be dutiful to their mothers, dutiful to their fathers, dutiful to ascetics, dutiful to brahmins, and will honor the elders of the family; they will undertake and live by this wholesome quality.”

“Te kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu āyunāpi vaḍḍhissanti, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissanti. Tesaṃ āyunāpi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ vīsativassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārīsavassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… cattārīsavassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ asītivassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… asītivassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ saṭṭhivassasatāyukā puttā bhavissanti… saṭṭhivassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsatitivassasatāyukā puttā bhavissanti… vīsatitivassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārīsachabbassasatāyukā puttā bhavissanti. Cattārīsachabbassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ dvevassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… dvevassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārivassasahassāyukā [T 3.0082] puttā bhavissanti… cattārivassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ aṭṭhavassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… aṭṭhavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsativassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… vīsativassasahassāyukānaṃ [V 3.0055] manussānaṃ cattārīsavassasahassāyukā [P 3.0075] puttā bhavissanti… cattārīsavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ asītivassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu pañcavassasatikā kumārikā alaṃpateyyā bhavissanti.

Because they have undertaken wholesome qualities, they will increase in lifespan and in beauty. For those who are increasing in lifespan and beauty, the children of humans with a twenty-year lifespan will have a lifespan of forty years… the children of humans with a forty-year lifespan will have a lifespan of eighty years… the children of humans with an eighty-year lifespan will have a lifespan of one hundred and sixty years… the children of humans with a one hundred and sixty-year lifespan will have a lifespan of three hundred and twenty years… the children of humans with a three hundred and twenty-year lifespan will have a lifespan of six hundred and forty years… the children of humans with a six hundred and forty-year lifespan will have a lifespan of two thousand years… the children of humans with a two-thousand-year lifespan will have a lifespan of four thousand years… the children of humans with a four-thousand-year lifespan will have a lifespan of eight thousand years… the children of humans with an eight-thousand-year lifespan will have a lifespan of twenty thousand years… the children of humans with a twenty-thousand-year lifespan will have a lifespan of forty thousand years… the children of humans with a forty-thousand-year lifespan will have a lifespan of eighty thousand years… Monks, among humans with an eighty-thousand-year lifespan, girls will become marriageable at the age of five hundred.

Saṅkharājauppatti

The Arising of King Saṅkha

106. “Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu tayo ābādhā bhavissanti, icchā, anasanaṃ, jarā. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ayaṃ jambudīpo iddho ceva bhavissati phīto ca, kukkuṭasampātikā gāmanigamarājadhāniyo gāmanigamajanapadā rājadhāniyo (ka.). Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ayaṃ jambudīpo avīci maññe phuṭo bhavissati manussehi, seyyathāpi naḷavanaṃ vā saravanaṃ sāravanaṃ (syā.) vā. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ayaṃ bārāṇasī ketumatī nāma rājadhānī bhavissati iddhā ceva phītā ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu [M 3.0063] imasmiṃ jambudīpe caturāsītinagarasahassāni bhavissanti ketumatīrājadhānīpamukhāni. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ketumatiyā rājadhāniyā saṅkho nāma rājā uppajjissati cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto [T 3.0083] vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavissanti, seyyathidaṃ, cakkaratanaṃ hatthiratanaṃ assaratanaṃ maṇiratanaṃ itthiratanaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavissanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena abhivijiya ajjhāvasissati.

106. “Monks, when humans live for eighty thousand years, there will be three afflictions: desire, hunger, and old age. Monks, when humans live for eighty thousand years, this Jambudīpa will be prosperous and flourishing, with villages, towns, and royal capitals as close together as a chicken might fly between. Monks, when humans live for eighty thousand years, this Jambudīpa will be so crowded with people that it will seem like the Avīci hell, like a forest of reeds or a forest of sara-grass. Monks, when humans live for eighty thousand years, this city of Bārāṇasī will be the royal capital named Ketumatī—prosperous, flourishing, populous, teeming with people, and abundant in food. Monks, when humans live for eighty thousand years, there will be eighty-four thousand cities in this Jambudīpa, with the royal capital Ketumatī as the foremost. Monks, when humans live for eighty thousand years, a king named Saṅkha will arise in the royal capital of Ketumatī—a wheel-turning monarch, a righteous king of the Dhamma, conqueror of the four quarters, who has attained stability in his country, endowed with the seven treasures. These will be his seven treasures: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh. He will have over a thousand sons—heroic, of powerful form, and capable of crushing foreign armies. He will conquer and rule this earth bounded by the ocean without rod or weapon, by means of the Dhamma.”

Metteyyabuddhuppādo

The Arising of the Buddha Metteyya

107. “Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu metteyyo [P 3.0076] nāma bhagavā loke uppajjissati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. Seyyathāpāhametarahi loke uppanno arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ [V 3.0056] samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedessati, seyyathāpāhametarahi imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedemi. So dhammaṃ desessati ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsessati; seyyathāpāhametarahi dhammaṃ desemi ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. So anekasahassaṃ anekasatasahassaṃ (ka.) bhikkhusaṃghaṃ [T 3.0084] pariharissati, seyyathāpāhametarahi anekasataṃ bhikkhusaṃghaṃ pariharāmi.

107. “Monks, when human beings live for eighty thousand years, the Blessed One named Metteyya will arise in the world—an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Sublime One, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. Just as I have now arisen in the world as an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Sublime One, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. He will realize this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its recluses and brahmins, gods and humans, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, and will make it known, just as I now realize and make known this world. He will teach the Dhamma—excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, excellent in the end, with its meaning and phrasing—and he will reveal the holy life, utterly complete and pure, just as I now teach the Dhamma and reveal the holy life. He will guide a monastic community of many thousands, just as I now guide a community of many hundreds.”

108. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, saṅkho nāma rājā yo so yūpo raññā mahāpanādena kārāpito. Taṃ yūpaṃ ussāpetvā ajjhāvasitvā taṃ datvā [M 3.0064] vissajjitvā samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavaṇibbakayācakānaṃ dānaṃ datvā metteyyassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā [P 3.0077] anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati.

108. “Then, monks, King Saṅkha will raise up the palace that was built by King Mahāpanāda. Having dwelt in it, he will give it away and relinquish it; and having given alms to recluses and brahmins, the poor, travelers, and beggars, he will go forth from the household life into homelessness in the presence of the Blessed One Metteyya, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, after shaving off his hair and beard and donning the saffron robes. Having gone forth thus, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, before long he will realize for himself with direct knowledge in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, he will dwell therein.”

109. “Attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī…pe… citte cittānupassī…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ [T 3.0085] kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo.

109. “Dwell, monks, as islands unto yourselves, as your own refuge, with no other refuge; dwell with the Dhamma as your island, with the Dhamma as your refuge, with no other refuge. And how, monks, does a monk dwell as an island unto himself, as his own refuge, with no other refuge, with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, with no other refuge? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… mind in mind… phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. Thus, monks, does a monk dwell as an island unto himself, as his own refuge, with no other refuge, with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, with no other refuge.”

Bhikkhunoāyuvaṇṇādivaḍḍhanakathā

A Discourse on the Increase of a Monk’s Longevity, Beauty, and So On

110. “Gocare, bhikkhave, caratha sake pettike visaye. Gocare, bhikkhave, carantā sake pettike visaye āyunāpi vaḍḍhissatha, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissatha, sukhenapi vaḍḍhissatha, bhogenapi vaḍḍhissatha, balenapi vaḍḍhissatha.

110. “Monks, you should roam in your own pasture, your own ancestral domain. Monks, by roaming in your own pasture, your own ancestral domain, you will increase in longevity, you will increase in beauty, you will increase in happiness, you will increase in prosperity, and you will increase in strength.”

“Kiñca[V 3.0057], bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āyusmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. So imesaṃ catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āyusmiṃ.

“And what, monks, is the cause of a monk's longevity? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to zeal and formations of striving. He develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to energy and formations of striving. He develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to consciousness and formations of striving. He develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to investigation and formations of striving. Having developed and cultivated these four bases of spiritual power, if he wishes, he might remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon. This, monks, is the cause of a monk's longevity.”

“Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vaṇṇasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto [P 3.0078] viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu [M 3.0065] bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vaṇṇasmiṃ.

“And what, monks, is the cause of a monk's beauty? Here, monks, a monk is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha, possessed of right conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults. Having undertaken them, he trains in the training rules. This, monks, is the cause of a monk's beauty.”

“Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sukhasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno, sukhasmiṃ.

“And what, monks, is the cause of a monk's happiness? Here, monks, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a monk enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial thought and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of initial thought and sustained thought… he enters and dwells in the second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna. This, monks, is the cause of a monk's happiness.”

“Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhogasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā [T 3.0086] viharati tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhogasmiṃ.

“And what, monks, is the cause of a monk's prosperity? Here, monks, a monk dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all as with oneself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will. With a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by appreciative joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, he pervades one direction, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all as with oneself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity that is vast, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will. This, monks, is the cause of a monk's prosperity.”

“Kiñca[V 3.0058], bhikkhave, bhikkhuno balasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno balasmiṃ.

“And what, monks, is the cause of a monk's strength? Here, monks, through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life he enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. This, monks, is the cause of a monk's strength.”

“Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekabalampi samanupassāmi yaṃ evaṃ duppasahaṃ, yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, mārabalaṃ. Kusalānaṃ[P 3.0079], bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ samādānahetu evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

“Monks, I do not see any other single power that is so difficult to overcome as this power of Māra. Monks, it is because of undertaking wholesome qualities that this merit increases.” This is what the Blessed One said. The monks, delighted, rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words.

Cakkavattisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.

The Cakkavatti Sutta, the third, is concluded.

4. Aggaññasuttaṃ

4. The Aggañña Sutta

Vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā

Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja

111. Evaṃ [P 3.0080][M 3.0066][V 3.0059][T 3.0087] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Tena kho pana samayena vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā bhikkhūsu parivasanti bhikkhubhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito pāsādā orohitvā pāsādapacchāyāyaṃ pāsādacchāyāyaṃ (ka.) abbhokāse caṅkamati.

111. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, at the Eastern Park, in the mansion of Migāra's mother. Now at that time, Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja were living among the monks, desiring the state of a monk. Then, in the evening, the Blessed One, having arisen from seclusion, descended from the mansion and was walking back and forth in the open air, in the shade behind the mansion.

112. Addasā kho vāseṭṭho bhagavantaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitaṃ pāsādā orohitvā pāsādapacchāyāyaṃ abbhokāse caṅkamantaṃ. Disvāna bhāradvājaṃ āmantesi – “ayaṃ, āvuso bhāradvāja, bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito pāsādā orohitvā pāsādapacchāyāyaṃ abbhokāse caṅkamati. Āyāmāvuso bhāradvāja, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; appeva nāma labheyyāma bhagavato santikā sammukhā (syā. ka.) dhammiṃ kathaṃ savanāyā”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho bhāradvājo vāseṭṭhassa paccassosi.

112. Vāseṭṭha saw the Blessed One in the evening, who, having arisen from seclusion, had descended from the mansion and was walking back and forth in the open air, in the shade behind the mansion. Having seen him, he addressed Bhāradvāja: 'Friend Bhāradvāja, the Blessed One, having arisen from seclusion in the evening, has descended from the mansion and is walking back and forth in the open air, in the shade behind the mansion. Come, friend Bhāradvāja, let us approach the place where the Blessed One is. Perhaps we might get to hear a talk on the Dhamma in the Blessed One's presence.' 'Yes, friend,' Bhāradvāja assented to Vāseṭṭha.

113. Atha kho vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā bhagavantaṃ caṅkamantaṃ anucaṅkamiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā vāseṭṭhaṃ āmantesi – “tumhe [P 3.0081] khvattha, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇajaccā brāhmaṇakulīnā brāhmaṇakulā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, kacci vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā na akkosanti na paribhāsantī”ti? “Taggha no, bhante, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsanti attarūpāya paribhāsāya [T 3.0088] paripuṇṇāya, no aparipuṇṇāyā”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ pana vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsanti attarūpāya paribhāsāya paripuṇṇāya, no aparipuṇṇāyā”ti? “Brāhmaṇā, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā hīno añño vaṇṇo (sī. pī. ma. ni. 2 madhurasutta). Brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo[M 3.0067], kaṇhā [V 3.0060] aññe vaṇṇā kaṇho añño vaṇṇo (sī. pī. ma. ni. 2 madhurasutta). Brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā. Brāhmaṇāva brāhmaṇā (syā.) brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā. Te tumhe seṭṭhaṃ vaṇṇaṃ hitvā hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā, yadidaṃ muṇḍake samaṇake ibbhe kaṇhe bandhupādāpacce. Tayidaṃ na sādhu, tayidaṃ nappatirūpaṃ, yaṃ tumhe seṭṭhaṃ vaṇṇaṃ hitvā hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā yadidaṃ muṇḍake samaṇake ibbhe kaṇhe bandhupādāpacce’ti. Evaṃ kho no, bhante, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsanti attarūpāya paribhāsāya paripuṇṇāya, no aparipuṇṇāyā”ti.

113. Then Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and followed the Blessed One as he was walking back and forth. Then the Blessed One addressed Vāseṭṭha: 'Vāseṭṭha, you are of brahmin birth, from a high brahmin family, having gone forth from a brahmin clan, from the household life into homelessness. Surely, Vāseṭṭha, the brahmins do not revile or abuse you?' 'Indeed, venerable sir, the brahmins revile and abuse us with fitting and complete abuse, not with incomplete abuse.' 'But in what way, Vāseṭṭha, do the brahmins revile and abuse you with fitting and complete abuse, not with incomplete abuse?' 'Venerable sir, the brahmins say this: “Only the brahmin class is superior; other classes are inferior. Only the brahmin class is fair; other classes are dark. Only brahmins are pure, not non-brahmins. Brahmins alone are the legitimate sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā. You, having abandoned the superior class, have associated with an inferior class, that is, with these shavelings, ascetics, menials, dark ones, born from the feet of our kinsman. That is not good, that is not proper, that you, having abandoned the superior class, have associated with an inferior class, that is, with these shavelings, ascetics, menials, dark ones, born from the feet of our kinsman.” In this way, venerable sir, the brahmins revile and abuse us with fitting and complete abuse, not with incomplete abuse.'

114. “Taggha vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ assarantā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇhā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Dissanti kho pana, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇānaṃ brāhmaṇiyo utuniyopi gabbhiniyopi vijāyamānāpi [P 3.0082] pāyamānāpi. Te ca brāhmaṇā yonijāva samānā evamāhaṃsu [T 3.0089] – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇhā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Te te ca (syā. ka.) brahmānañceva abbhācikkhanti, musā ca bhāsanti, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavanti.

114. Indeed, Vāseṭṭha, those brahmins, not remembering the ancient tradition, say this: ‘Only the brahmin class is superior; other classes are inferior. Only the brahmin class is fair; other classes are dark. Only brahmins are pure, not non-brahmins. Brahmins alone are the legitimate sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’ But, Vāseṭṭha, brahmin women are seen menstruating, becoming pregnant, giving birth, and breastfeeding. And those brahmins, being born from a womb, say this: ‘Only the brahmin class is superior; other classes are inferior. Only the brahmin class is fair; other classes are dark. Only brahmins are pure, not non-brahmins. Brahmins alone are the legitimate sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’ They both misrepresent Brahmā and speak falsely, and they generate much demerit.

Catuvaṇṇasuddhi

The Purity of the Four Classes

115. “Cattārome, vāseṭṭha, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco pāṇātipātī hoti adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā sāvajjā sāvajjasaṅkhātā asevitabbā asevitabbasaṅkhātā naalamariyā naalamariyasaṅkhātā kaṇhā kaṇhavipākā viññugarahitā, khattiyepi te kho vāseṭṭha (ka.) idhekacce sandissanti. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco [M 3.0068] pāṇātipātī hoti adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā…pe… kaṇhā kaṇhavipākā viññugarahitā; suddepi te idhekacce sandissanti.

115. Vāseṭṭha, there are these four classes: the noble class, the brahmin class, the merchant class, and the servant class. Vāseṭṭha, here in this world, some of the noble class are takers of life, takers of what is not given, they engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsehood, speak divisively, speak harshly, engage in frivolous chatter, are covetous, have minds of ill will, and hold wrong view. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, whatever qualities are unwholesome, reckoned as unwholesome, blameworthy, reckoned as blameworthy, not to be cultivated, reckoned as not to be cultivated, not befitting the noble ones, reckoned as not befitting the noble ones, dark, with dark results, and censured by the wise—these unwholesome qualities are found here in some of the noble class. Vāseṭṭha, some of the brahmin class also… Vāseṭṭha, some of the merchant class also… Vāseṭṭha, here in this world, some of the servant class are takers of life, takers of what is not given… and hold wrong view. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, whatever qualities are unwholesome, reckoned as unwholesome… dark, with dark results, and censured by the wise—these unwholesome qualities are found here in some of the servant class.

“Khattiyopi [V 3.0061] kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato, musāvādā paṭivirato, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato, samphappalāpā paṭivirato, anabhijjhālu abyāpannacitto, sammādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā anavajjā [T 3.0090] anavajjasaṅkhātā sevitabbā sevitabbasaṅkhātā alamariyā alamariyasaṅkhātā sukkā sukkavipākā viññuppasatthā, khattiyepi te idhekacce sandissanti. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… anabhijjhālu[P 3.0083], abyāpannacitto, sammādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā anavajjā anavajjasaṅkhātā sevitabbā sevitabbasaṅkhātā alamariyā alamariyasaṅkhātā sukkā sukkavipākā viññuppasatthā; suddepi te idhekacce sandissanti.

Vāseṭṭha, here in this world, some of the noble class refrain from taking life, refrain from taking what is not given, refrain from sexual misconduct, refrain from false speech, refrain from divisive speech, refrain from harsh speech, refrain from frivolous chatter, are not covetous, have minds without ill will, and hold right view. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, whatever qualities are wholesome, reckoned as wholesome, blameless, reckoned as blameless, to be cultivated, reckoned as to be cultivated, befitting the noble ones, reckoned as befitting the noble ones, bright, with bright results, and praised by the wise—these wholesome qualities are found here in some of the noble class. Vāseṭṭha, some of the brahmin class also… Vāseṭṭha, some of the merchant class also… Vāseṭṭha, here in this world, some of the servant class refrain from taking life… are not covetous, have minds without ill will, and hold right view. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, whatever qualities are wholesome, reckoned as wholesome, blameless, reckoned as blameless… befitting the noble ones, reckoned as befitting the noble ones, bright, with bright results, and praised by the wise—these wholesome qualities are found here in some of the servant class.

116. “Imesu kho, vāseṭṭha, catūsu vaṇṇesu evaṃ ubhayavokiṇṇesu vattamānesu kaṇhasukkesu dhammesu viññugarahitesu ceva viññuppasatthesu ca yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇhā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Taṃ tesaṃ viññū nānujānanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imesañhi, vāseṭṭha, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ yo hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto, so nesaṃ aggamakkhāyati dhammeneva, no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca[T 3.0091].

116. Vāseṭṭha, among these four classes, wherein both dark and white qualities—those censured by the wise and those praised by the wise—are found intermingled, the brāhmaṇas declare: ‘Only the brāhmaṇa class is the highest; the other classes are inferior. Only the brāhmaṇa class is white; the other classes are dark. Only brāhmaṇas are purified, not non-brāhmaṇas. Only brāhmaṇas are the sons of Brahmā, born from his breast, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, the heirs of Brahmā.’ The wise do not assent to this statement of theirs. For what reason? Vāseṭṭha, from among these four classes, whoever is a bhikkhu who is an Arahant, whose cankers are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, has done what was to be done, has laid down the burden, has attained his own welfare, whose fetter of existence is completely destroyed, and who is liberated through right and perfect knowledge—he is declared the foremost among them in accordance with Dhamma, not contrary to it. For, Vāseṭṭha, Dhamma is the highest among this populace, both in the present life and in the life to come.

117. “Tadamināpetaṃ, vāseṭṭha, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ, yathā dhammova seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

117. Vāseṭṭha, it should be understood by this exposition also how Dhamma is the highest among this populace, both in the present life and in the life to come.

“Jānāti [M 3.0069] kho kho pana (ka.), vāseṭṭha, rājā pasenadi kosalo – ‘samaṇo gotamo anantarā anuttaro (bahūsu) sakyakulā pabbajito’ti. Sakyā kho pana, vāseṭṭha, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa anuyuttā anantarā anuyantā (syā.), anantarā anuyuttā (ka.) bhavanti. Karonti kho, vāseṭṭha, sakyā raññe pasenadimhi kosale nipaccakāraṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yaṃ karonti sakyā raññe pasenadimhi kosale nipaccakāraṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ, karoti [P 3.0084] taṃ [V 3.0062] rājā pasenadi kosalo tathāgate nipaccakāraṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ, na naṃ nanu (bahūsu) ‘sujāto samaṇo gotamo, dujjātohamasmi. Balavā samaṇo gotamo, dubbalohamasmi. Pāsādiko samaṇo gotamo, dubbaṇṇohamasmi. Mahesakkho samaṇo gotamo, appesakkhohamasmī’ti. Atha kho naṃ dhammaṃyeva sakkaronto dhammaṃ garuṃ karonto dhammaṃ mānento dhammaṃ pūjento dhammaṃ apacāyamāno evaṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo tathāgate nipaccakāraṃ karoti, abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ. Imināpi kho etaṃ, vāseṭṭha, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ, yathā dhammova seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

Vāseṭṭha, King Pasenadi of Kosala knows: ‘The ascetic Gotama has gone forth from the Sakyan clan.’ Vāseṭṭha, the Sakyans are vassals of King Pasenadi of Kosala. The Sakyans, Vāseṭṭha, perform for King Pasenadi of Kosala acts of deference: paying homage, rising in respect, making the añjali gesture, and showing proper respect. Vāseṭṭha, whatever acts of deference the Sakyans perform for King Pasenadi of Kosala—paying homage, rising in respect, making the añjali gesture, and showing proper respect—King Pasenadi of Kosala performs those same acts for the Tathāgata. It is not that he does so thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is well-born, whereas I am ill-born. The ascetic Gotama is powerful, whereas I am weak. The ascetic Gotama is inspiring to see, whereas I am unattractive. The ascetic Gotama is of great majesty, whereas I am of little majesty.’ Rather, it is by honoring the Dhamma itself, holding the Dhamma in high esteem, revering the Dhamma, venerating the Dhamma, and paying homage to the Dhamma itself that King Pasenadi of Kosala performs these acts of deference for the Tathāgata: paying homage, rising in respect, making the añjali gesture, and showing proper respect. Vāseṭṭha, by this exposition also, it should be understood how Dhamma is the highest among this populace, both in the present life and in the life to come.

118. “Tumhe khvattha, vāseṭṭha, nānājaccā nānānāmā nānāgottā nānākulā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā. ‘Ke tumhe’ti – puṭṭhā [T 3.0092] samānā ‘samaṇā sakyaputtiyāmhā’ti – paṭijānātha. Yassa kho panassa, vāseṭṭha, tathāgate saddhā niviṭṭhā mūlajātā patiṭṭhitā daḷhā asaṃhāriyā samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ, tassetaṃ kallaṃ vacanāya – ‘bhagavatomhi putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāgatassa hetaṃ, vāseṭṭha, adhivacanaṃ ‘dhammakāyo’ itipi, ‘brahmakāyo’ itipi, ‘dhammabhūto’ itipi, ‘brahmabhūto’ itipi.

118. Vāseṭṭha, you are of various castes, various names, various clans, and various families, who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness. When asked, ‘Who are you?’ you declare, ‘We are ascetics, sons of the Sakyan Sage.’ Indeed, Vāseṭṭha, for any person whose faith in the Tathāgata is settled, rooted, established, firm, and unshakable by any ascetic or brahmin, by a deva, by Māra, by Brahmā, or by anyone in the world, it is fitting for that person to declare: ‘I am the Blessed One’s legitimate son, born from his mouth, born of the Dhamma, created by the Dhamma, an heir of the Dhamma.’ For what reason? Because, Vāseṭṭha, these are designations of the Tathāgata: ‘Dhamma-body,’ as well as ‘Brahmā-body,’ ‘Dhamma-become,’ as well as ‘Brahmā-become.’

119. “Hoti kho so, vāseṭṭha, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko saṃvaṭṭati. Saṃvaṭṭamāne loke yebhuyyena sattā ābhassarasaṃvattanikā honti. Te tattha honti [M 3.0070] manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.

119. There comes a time, Vāseṭṭha, when, after a long period, this world dissolves. As the world dissolves, most beings are reborn in the Ābhassara realm. There they dwell, mind-made, feeding on joy, self-luminous, moving through the sky, abiding in glory for a long, long time.

“Hoti kho so, vāseṭṭha, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko vivaṭṭati. Vivaṭṭamāne loke yebhuyyena sattā ābhassarakāyā [P 3.0085] cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchanti. Tedha honti manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.

There comes a time, Vāseṭṭha, when after a long period this world evolves. As the world evolves, most beings, having passed away from the Ābhassara realm, come to this state. Here they are mind-made, feeding on joy, self-luminous, moving through the sky, abiding splendidly, and they remain for a long, long time.

Rasapathavipātubhāvo

The Appearance of the Savory Earth

120. “Ekodakībhūtaṃ kho pana, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena hoti andhakāro andhakāratimisā[V 3.0063]. Na candimasūriyā paññāyanti, na nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni paññāyanti, na rattindivā paññāyanti, na māsaḍḍhamāsā paññāyanti, na utusaṃvaccharā paññāyanti[T 3.0093], na itthipumā paññāyanti, sattā sattātveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti. Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena rasapathavī udakasmiṃ samatani samatāni (bahūsu); seyyathāpi nāma payaso tattassa payatattassa (syā.) nibbāyamānassa upari santānakaṃ hoti, evameva pāturahosi. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā, seyyathāpi nāma sampannaṃ vā sappi sampannaṃ vā navanītaṃ evaṃvaṇṇā ahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma khuddamadhuṃ khuddaṃ madhuṃ (ka. sī.) aneḷakaṃ anelakaṃ (sī. pī.), evamassādā ahosi. Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto lolajātiko – ‘ambho, kimevidaṃ bhavissatī’ti rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyi. Tassa rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyato acchādesi, taṇhā cassa okkami. Aññepi kho, vāseṭṭha, sattā tassa sattassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamānā rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyiṃsu. Tesaṃ rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyataṃ acchādesi, taṇhā ca tesaṃ okkami.

120. At that time, Vāseṭṭha, there was a single mass of water, and it was dark, a blinding darkness. Neither the moon nor the sun was discerned, nor were the constellations or star-forms discerned, nor were night and day discerned, nor months and half-months, nor seasons and years. Male and female were not discerned; beings were reckoned simply as ‘beings.’ Then, Vāseṭṭha, for those beings, after a long, long period had passed, a savory earth spread out upon the water, just as a skin forms on the surface of hot milk-rice as it cools. It was endowed with color, fragrance, and taste. Its color was like that of fine ghee or fine fresh butter, and its taste was like that of pure wild honey. Then, Vāseṭṭha, a certain being of a greedy nature thought, ‘Oh, what could this be?’ and tasted the savory earth with a finger. As he tasted the savory earth with his finger, it suffused him, and craving arose in him. Other beings, Vāseṭṭha, following the example of that being, also tasted the savory earth with their fingers. As they tasted the savory earth with their fingers, it suffused them, and craving arose in them.

Candimasūriyādipātubhāvo

The Appearance of the Moon, the Sun, and So Forth

121. “Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Yato kho [P 3.0086] te yato kho (sī. syā. pī.), vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ [M 3.0071] hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Atha tesaṃ sattānaṃ sayaṃpabhā antaradhāyi. Sayaṃpabhāya antarahitāya candimasūriyā pāturahesuṃ. Candimasūriyesu pātubhūtesu nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni pāturahesuṃ. Nakkhattesu tārakarūpesu pātubhūtesu rattindivā paññāyiṃsu. Rattindivesu paññāyamānesu māsaḍḍhamāsā paññāyiṃsu. Māsaḍḍhamāsesu paññāyamānesu utusaṃvaccharā paññāyiṃsu. Ettāvatā kho[T 3.0094], vāseṭṭha, ayaṃ loko puna vivaṭṭo hoti.

121. Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings began to consume the savory earth with their hands, making it into lumps. When those beings, Vāseṭṭha, began to consume the savory earth with their hands, making it into lumps, their own radiance disappeared. When their own radiance had disappeared, the moon and sun appeared. When the moon and sun had appeared, the constellations and star-forms appeared. When the constellations and star-forms had appeared, night and day became discernible. When night and day became discernible, months and half-months became discernible. When months and half-months became discernible, seasons and years became discernible. To this extent, Vāseṭṭha, this world was established once more.

122. “Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tabbhakkhā (syā.) tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ (rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantānaṃ) ( ) sī. syā. pī. potthakesu natthi kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā vaṇṇavevajjatā (ṭīkā) ca paññāyittha. Ekidaṃ sattā vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā vaṇṇavanto, te dubbaṇṇe satte atimaññanti – ‘mayametehi vaṇṇavantatarā, amhehete dubbaṇṇatarā’ti. Tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayā mānātimānajātikānaṃ rasapathavī antaradhāyi. Rasāya pathaviyā antarahitāya sannipatiṃsu. Sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘aho rasaṃ, aho rasa’nti! Tadetarahipi [V 3.0064] manussā kañcideva surasaṃ sādhurasaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) labhitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘aho rasaṃ, aho rasa’nti! Tadeva porāṇaṃ aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ anusaranti, na tvevassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

122. Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings, consuming the savory earth, having it as their food, having it as their nourishment, subsisted for a long, long time. In whatsoever manner, Vāseṭṭha, those beings, consuming the savory earth, having it as their food, having it as their nourishment, subsisted for a long, long time, in that same manner, coarseness arose in their bodies, and a difference in their appearance became manifest. Some beings were beautiful, while others were ugly. Therein, those beings who were beautiful despised the ugly beings, thinking, ‘We are more beautiful than they; they are uglier than we.’ On account of their pride in their appearance, for those beings who were by nature proud and excessively proud, the savory earth disappeared. When the savory earth had disappeared, they gathered together. Having gathered, they lamented, ‘Oh, the savor! Oh, the savor!’ Even now, when people obtain something of fine taste, they say thus: ‘Oh, the savor! Oh, the savor!’ They are following that ancient, primordial expression, but they do not know its meaning.

Bhūmipappaṭakapātubhāvo

The Appearance of the Earth-Crust

123. “Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ rasāya pathaviyā [P 3.0087] antarahitāya bhūmipappaṭako pāturahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma ahicchattako, evameva pāturahosi. So ahosi vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno, seyyathāpi nāma sampannaṃ vā sappi sampannaṃ vā navanītaṃ evaṃvaṇṇo ahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma khuddamadhuṃ aneḷakaṃ, evamassādo [T 3.0095] ahosi.

123. Then, Vāseṭṭha, for those beings, when the savory earth had disappeared, an earth-crust appeared. It appeared just like a mushroom bud. It was endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, and endowed with taste. Its color was like that of fine ghee or fine fresh butter, and its taste was like that of pure wild honey.

“Atha [M 3.0072] kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā bhūmipappaṭakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Te taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā bhūmipappaṭakaṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ bhiyyoso mattāya kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā ca paññāyittha. Ekidaṃ sattā vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā vaṇṇavanto, te dubbaṇṇe satte atimaññanti – ‘mayametehi vaṇṇavantatarā, amhehete dubbaṇṇatarā’ti. Tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayā mānātimānajātikānaṃ bhūmipappaṭako antaradhāyi.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings began to consume the earth-crust. Consuming it, having it as their food, having it as their nourishment, they subsisted for a long, long time. In whatsoever manner, Vāseṭṭha, those beings, consuming the earth-crust, having it as their food, having it as their nourishment, subsisted for a long, long time, in that same manner, coarseness arose in their bodies to an exceedingly great degree, and a difference in their appearance became manifest. Some beings were beautiful, while others were ugly. Therein, those beings who were beautiful despised the ugly beings, thinking, ‘We are more beautiful than they; they are uglier than we.’ On account of their pride in their appearance, for those beings who were by nature proud and excessively proud, the earth-crust disappeared.

Padālatāpātubhāvo

The Appearance of the Sweet-Creeping Plant

124. “Bhūmipappaṭake antarahite padālatā saddālatā (sī.) pāturahosi, seyyathāpi nāma kalambukā kalambakā (syā.), evameva pāturahosi. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā, seyyathāpi nāma sampannaṃ vā sappi sampannaṃ vā navanītaṃ evaṃvaṇṇā ahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma khuddamadhuṃ aneḷakaṃ, evamassādā ahosi.

124. When the earth-crust had disappeared, the sweet-creeping plant appeared. Just as the kalambukā plant might appear, even so did it appear. It was endowed with color, fragrance, and taste. Its color was like that of fine ghee or fine fresh butter, and its taste was like that of pure wild honey.

“Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā padālataṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Te taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā padālataṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ bhiyyosomattāya kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā ca paññāyittha. Ekidaṃ [P 3.0088] sattā [T 3.0096] vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā vaṇṇavanto, te dubbaṇṇe satte [V 3.0065] atimaññanti – ‘mayametehi vaṇṇavantatarā, amhehete dubbaṇṇatarā’ti. Tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayā mānātimānajātikānaṃ padālatā antaradhāyi.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings began to consume the sweet-creeping plant. Consuming it, having it as their food and nourishment, they subsisted for a very long, long time. And as those beings, Vāseṭṭha, continued to consume the sweet-creeping plant, having it as their food and nourishment, and subsisting for a very long, long time, a greater coarseness appeared in their bodies, and differences in their appearance became manifest. Some beings were beautiful, while others were ugly. Thereupon, those beings who were beautiful despised the ugly ones, thinking: ‘We are more beautiful than they are; they are uglier than we are.’ For them, who had become proud and arrogant, because of this conceit based on appearance, the sweet-creeping plant disappeared.

“Padālatāya antarahitāya sannipatiṃsu. Sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘ahu vata no, ahāyi vata no padālatā’ti! Tadetarahipi manussā kenaci kenacideva (sī. syā. pī.) dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ahu vata no, ahāyi [M 3.0073] vata no’ti! Tadeva porāṇaṃ aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ anusaranti, na tvevassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

When the sweet-creeping plant had disappeared, they assembled together. Having assembled, they lamented, ‘Alas, we had it! Alas, our sweet-creeping plant is lost!’ To this day, when people are afflicted by some painful state, they say the same: ‘Alas, we had it! Alas, it is lost to us!’ They are just recalling that same ancient, primordial saying, but they do not understand its meaning.

Akaṭṭhapākasālipātubhāvo

The Manifestation of Uncultivated Rice

125. “Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ padālatāya antarahitāya akaṭṭhapāko sāli pāturahosi akaṇo athuso suddho sugandho taṇḍulapphalo. Yaṃ taṃ sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya āharanti, pāto taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ pāto pātarāsāya āharanti, sāyaṃ taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ; nāpadānaṃ paññāyati. Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā akaṭṭhapākaṃ sāliṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu.

125. Then, Vāseṭṭha, for those beings, when the sweet-creeping plant had disappeared, uncultivated rice appeared. It was without broken grains, without chaff, pure, fragrant, and consisting of only the rice grain. That which they would bring in the evening for the evening meal, in the morning would be ripe and grown back. That which they would bring in the morning for the morning meal, in the evening would be ripe and grown back. No sign of reaping was apparent. Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings, consuming that uncultivated rice, having it as their food and nourishment, subsisted for a very long, long time.

Itthipurisaliṅgapātubhāvo

The Manifestation of Female and Male Characteristics

126. “Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā akaṭṭhapākaṃ sāliṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ bhiyyosomattāya kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā ca paññāyittha, itthiyā ca itthiliṅgaṃ pāturahosi purisassa ca purisaliṅgaṃ. Itthī [T 3.0097] ca purisaṃ ativelaṃ upanijjhāyati puriso ca itthiṃ. Tesaṃ ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyataṃ sārāgo udapādi, pariḷāho kāyasmiṃ okkami. Te pariḷāhapaccayā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseviṃsu.

126. Vāseṭṭha, as those beings continued for a long, long time, feeding on that uncultivated rice, having it as their food and nourishment, so in just that way, more and more coarseness descended upon their bodies, and a difference in their appearance became manifest. The female sexual organ appeared in the female, and the male sexual organ appeared in the male. And the female gazed intently and excessively at the male, and the male at the female. As they gazed intently and excessively at one another, strong passion arose in them, and a burning descended upon their bodies. Due to that burning, they engaged in the act of sexual intercourse.

“Ye kho pana te, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena sattā passanti methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevante, aññe paṃsuṃ khipanti, aññe seṭṭhiṃ khipanti[P 3.0089], aññe gomayaṃ khipanti – ‘nassa asuci vasali (syā.), vasalī (ka.), nassa asucī’ti. ‘Kathañhi nāma satto sattassa evarūpaṃ karissatī’ti! Tadetarahipi manussā ekaccesu janapadesu vadhuyā nibbuyhamānāya nivayhamānāya, niggayhamānāya (ka.) aññe paṃsuṃ khipanti, aññe seṭṭhiṃ khipanti, aññe [V 3.0066] gomayaṃ khipanti. Tadeva porāṇaṃ aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ anusaranti, na tvevassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

Vāseṭṭha, those beings at that time who saw others engaging in the act of sexual intercourse threw dust at them, others threw ashes, and others threw cow-dung, saying: ‘Perish, impure one! Perish, impure one!’ and ‘How indeed can one being do such a thing to another being?’ Even now, in some regions, when a bride is being led forth, some people throw dust, some throw ashes, and some throw cow-dung. They are following that same ancient, primordial tradition, but they do not know its meaning.

Methunadhammasamācāro

The Practice of Sexual Intercourse

127. “Adhammasammataṃ [M 3.0074] kho pana adhammasammataṃ taṃ kho pana (syā.), adhammasammataṃ kho pana taṃ (?), vāseṭṭha, tena samayena hoti, tadetarahi dhammasammataṃ. Ye kho pana, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena sattā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanti, te māsampi dvemāsampi na labhanti gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā pavisituṃ. Yato kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā tasmiṃ asaddhamme ativelaṃ pātabyataṃ āpajjiṃsu. Atha agārāni upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ tasseva asaddhammassa paṭicchādanatthaṃ. Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññatarassa sattassa alasajātikassa etadahosi – ‘ambho, kimevāhaṃ vihaññāmi sāliṃ āharanto sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya! Yaṃnūnāhaṃ sāliṃ āhareyyaṃ sakiṃdeva sakiṃdeva (ka.) sāyapātarāsāyā’ti[T 3.0098]!

127. Vāseṭṭha, what was considered unrighteous at that time is now considered righteous. Vāseṭṭha, those beings who engaged in the act of sexual intercourse at that time were not allowed to enter a village or a town for a month or even two months. Vāseṭṭha, when those beings became excessively engaged in that unrighteous practice, they then began to make houses for the purpose of concealing that very unrighteousness. Then, Vāseṭṭha, to a certain being of a lazy nature this thought occurred: ‘Indeed, why should I weary myself bringing rice in the evening for the evening meal and in the morning for the morning meal? What if I were to bring rice just once for both the evening and morning meals!’

“Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto sāliṃ āhāsi sakiṃdeva sāyapātarāsāya. Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto yena so satto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ sattaṃ etadavoca – ‘ehi, bho satta, sālāhāraṃ gamissāmā’ti. ‘Alaṃ, bho satta, āhato āhaṭo (syā.) me sāli sakiṃdeva sāyapātarāsāyā’ti. Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto tassa sattassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno sāliṃ āhāsi sakiṃdeva dvīhāya. ‘Evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, that being brought rice just once for the evening and morning meals. Then, Vāseṭṭha, another being approached that being; having approached, he said to that being: ‘Come, friend, let us go to gather rice.’ ‘Enough, friend, I have brought rice just once for the evening and morning meals.’ Then, Vāseṭṭha, that being, following the example of the other, brought rice just once for two days, thinking, ‘Friend, this way also seems good!’

“Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto yena so satto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [P 3.0090] taṃ sattaṃ etadavoca – ‘ehi, bho satta, sālāhāraṃ gamissāmā’ti. ‘Alaṃ, bho satta, āhato me sāli sakiṃdeva dvīhāyā’ti. Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto tassa sattassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno sāliṃ āhāsi sakiṃdeva catūhāya, ‘evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, another being approached that being; having approached, he said to that being: ‘Come, friend, let us go to gather rice.’ ‘Enough, friend, I have brought rice just once for two days.’ Then, Vāseṭṭha, that being, following the example of the other, brought rice just once for four days, thinking, ‘Friend, this way also seems good!’

“Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto yena so satto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ sattaṃ etadavoca – ‘ehi, bho satta, sālāhāraṃ gamissāmā’ti. ‘Alaṃ, bho satta, āhato me sāli sakideva catūhāyā’ti. Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto tassa sattassa [M 3.0075] diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno sāliṃ āhāsi sakideva aṭṭhāhāya, ‘evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, another being approached that being; having approached, he said to that being: ‘Come, friend, let us go to gather rice.’ ‘Enough, friend, I have brought rice just once for four days.’ Then, Vāseṭṭha, that being, following the example of the other, brought rice just once for eight days, thinking, ‘Friend, this way also seems good!’

“Yato kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sannidhikārakaṃ sāliṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Atha kaṇopi [V 3.0067] taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi, thusopi taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi; lūnampi nappaṭivirūḷhaṃ[T 3.0099], apadānaṃ paññāyittha, saṇḍasaṇḍā sālayo aṭṭhaṃsu.

Vāseṭṭha, from when those beings began to hoard and consume that rice, then broken grains and husk began to envelop the rice grains; what was reaped did not grow back again, a clear break became apparent, and the rice plants stood in separate clumps.

Sālivibhāgo

The Division of the Rice

128. “Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sannipatiṃsu, sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘pāpakā vata, bho, dhammā sattesu pātubhūtā. Mayañhi pubbe manomayā ahumhā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino, ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no amhākaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena rasapathavī udakasmiṃ samatani. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā. Te mayaṃ rasapathaviṃ hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamimha paribhuñjituṃ, tesaṃ no rasapathaviṃ hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamataṃ paribhuñjituṃ sayaṃpabhā antaradhāyi. Sayaṃpabhāya antarahitāya candimasūriyā pāturahesuṃ, candimasūriyesu pātubhūtesu nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni [P 3.0091] pāturahesuṃ, nakkhattesu tārakarūpesu pātubhūtesu rattindivā paññāyiṃsu, rattindivesu paññāyamānesu māsaḍḍhamāsā paññāyiṃsu. Māsaḍḍhamāsesu paññāyamānesu utusaṃvaccharā paññāyiṃsu. Te mayaṃ rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā rasapathavī antaradhāyi. Rasapathaviyā antarahitāya bhūmipappaṭako pāturahosi. So ahosi vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno. Te mayaṃ bhūmipappaṭakaṃ upakkamimha paribhuñjituṃ. Te mayaṃ taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā [T 3.0100] bhūmipappaṭako antaradhāyi. Bhūmipappaṭake antarahite padālatā pāturahosi. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā. Te mayaṃ padālataṃ upakkamimha paribhuñjituṃ. Te mayaṃ taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā [M 3.0076] padālatā antaradhāyi. Padālatāya antarahitāya akaṭṭhapāko sāli pāturahosi akaṇo athuso suddho sugandho taṇḍulapphalo. Yaṃ taṃ sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya āharāma, pāto taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ pāto pātarāsāya āharāma, sāyaṃ taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ. Nāpadānaṃ paññāyittha. Te mayaṃ akaṭṭhapākaṃ sāliṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā kaṇopi taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi, thusopi taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi, lūnampi nappaṭivirūḷhaṃ, apadānaṃ paññāyittha, saṇḍasaṇḍā [P 3.0092] sālayo ṭhitā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ [V 3.0068] sāliṃ vibhajeyyāma, mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyyāmā’ti! Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sāliṃ vibhajiṃsu, mariyādaṃ ṭhapesuṃ.

128. Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings gathered together and lamented: ‘Alas, sirs, evil qualities have appeared among beings. For we were formerly mind-made, feeding on joy, self-luminous, moving through the air, abiding in splendor—and we remained thus for a long, long time. For us, after a long period had passed, at some time or other, a savory earth spread out upon the water. It was endowed with color, fragrance, and taste. We began to break off and consume this savory earth with our hands. As we began to break off and consume this savory earth with our hands, our self-luminance vanished. With the vanishing of our self-luminance, the moon and sun appeared. With the appearance of the moon and sun, the stars and constellations appeared. With the appearance of the stars and constellations, night and day were distinguished. With the distinction of night and day, months and half-months were distinguished. With the distinction of months and half-months, seasons and years were distinguished. We, consuming that savory earth, feeding on it, sustained by it, remained for a long, long time. For us, due to the appearance of those same evil, unwholesome qualities, the savory earth vanished. With the vanishing of the savory earth, a ground-fungus appeared. It was endowed with color, fragrance, and taste. We began to consume this ground-fungus. We, consuming that ground-fungus, feeding on it, sustained by it, remained for a long, long time. For us, due to the appearance of those same evil, unwholesome qualities, the ground-fungus vanished. With the vanishing of the ground-fungus, a creeper appeared. It was endowed with color, fragrance, and taste. We began to consume this creeper. We, consuming that creeper, feeding on it, sustained by it, remained for a long, long time. For us, due to the appearance of those same evil, unwholesome qualities, the creeper vanished. With the vanishing of the creeper, uncultivated rice appeared, without powder, without husk, pure, fragrant, with rice grains as its fruit. What we brought in the evening for the evening meal, by morning was ripe and regrown. What we brought in the morning for the morning meal, by evening was ripe and regrown. No depletion was apparent. We, consuming that uncultivated rice, feeding on it, sustained by it, remained for a long, long time. For us, due to the appearance of those same evil, unwholesome qualities, powder enveloped the rice grain, and husk enveloped the rice grain; what was reaped did not grow back; depletion became apparent, and the rice stood in clumps. What if we were to divide the rice and set up boundaries?’ Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings divided the rice and set up boundaries.

129. “Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto lolajātiko sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ aññassa (?) bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyitvā paribhuñji. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ, gahetvā etadavocuṃ – ‘pāpakaṃ vata, bho satta, karosi, yatra hi nāma sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyitvā paribhuñjasi. Māssu, bho satta, punapi evarūpamakāsī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bho’ti kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto tesaṃ sattānaṃ paccassosi. Dutiyampi kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto…pe… tatiyampi kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyitvā paribhuñji. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ, gahetvā etadavocuṃ – ‘pāpakaṃ vata, bho satta, karosi, yatra hi nāma sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ [T 3.0101] ādiyitvā paribhuñjasi. Māssu, bho satta, punapi evarūpamakāsī’ti. Aññe pāṇinā pahariṃsu, aññe leḍḍunā pahariṃsu, aññe daṇḍena pahariṃsu. Tadagge kho, vāseṭṭha, adinnādānaṃ paññāyati, garahā paññāyati, musāvādo paññāyati, daṇḍādānaṃ paññāyati.

129. Then, Vāseṭṭha, a certain being of a fickle nature, while guarding his own portion, took another portion that was not given and consumed it. They seized him, and having seized him, said this: ‘Truly, O being, you do evil, in that while guarding your own portion, you take another portion that is not given and consume it. Do not, O being, do such a thing again.’ ‘So be it, sirs,’ Vāseṭṭha, that being assented to those beings. A second time, Vāseṭṭha, that being… a third time, Vāseṭṭha, that being, while guarding his own portion, took another portion that was not given and consumed it. They seized him, and having seized him, said this: ‘Truly, O being, you do evil, in that while guarding your own portion, you take another portion that is not given and consume it. Do not, O being, do such a thing again.’ Some struck him with their hands, some with clods, and some with sticks. From that time forth, Vāseṭṭha, taking what is not given became known, censure became known, speaking falsehood became known, and the taking up of the rod became known.

Mahāsammatarājā

The Great Elect

130. “Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sannipatiṃsu, sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘pāpakā vata bho dhammā sattesu pātubhūtā, yatra hi nāma [M 3.0077] adinnādānaṃ paññāyissati, garahā paññāyissati, musāvādo paññāyissati, daṇḍādānaṃ paññāyissati. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ ekaṃ sattaṃ sammanneyyāma, yo no sammā khīyitabbaṃ khīyeyya, sammā garahitabbaṃ garaheyya, sammā pabbājetabbaṃ pabbājeyya. Mayaṃ panassa sālīnaṃ bhāgaṃ anuppadassāmā’ti.

130. Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings gathered together, and having gathered, they lamented: ‘Alas, sirs, evil qualities have appeared among beings, in that taking what is not given will now be known, censure will be known, speaking falsehood will be known, and the taking up of the rod will be known. What if we were to appoint one being who would rightly rebuke one who should be rebuked, rightly censure one who should be censured, and rightly banish one who should be banished? And we, for our part, shall bestow upon him a portion of the rice.’

“Atha [P 3.0093] kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā yo nesaṃ satto abhirūpataro ca dassanīyataro ca pāsādikataro ca mahesakkhataro ca taṃ sattaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘ehi, bho satta, sammā khīyitabbaṃ khīya, sammā garahitabbaṃ garaha, sammā pabbājetabbaṃ [T 3.0102] pabbājehi. Mayaṃ pana te sālīnaṃ bhāgaṃ anuppadassāmā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bho’ti kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto tesaṃ sattānaṃ paṭissuṇitvā sammā khīyitabbaṃ khīyi, sammā garahitabbaṃ garahi, sammā pabbājetabbaṃ pabbājesi. Te panassa sālīnaṃ bhāgaṃ anuppadaṃsu.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings approached the one among them who was more handsome, more attractive, more pleasing, and more powerful, and said this: ‘Come, O being, rightly reproach him who should be reproached, rightly censure him who should be censured, and rightly banish him who should be banished. We, for our part, will provide you with a portion of our rice.’ ‘Very well, sirs,’ that being, Vāseṭṭha, consented to them and rightly reproached him who should be reproached, rightly censured him who should be censured, and rightly banished him who should be banished. They, for their part, provided him with a portion of the rice.

131. “Mahājanasammatoti [V 3.0069] kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘mahāsammato, mahāsammato’ tveva paṭhamaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Khettānaṃ adhipatīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘khattiyo, khattiyo’ tveva dutiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Dhammena pare rañjetīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘rājā, rājā’ tveva tatiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa khattiyamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ, anaññesaṃ. Sadisānaṃyeva, no asadisānaṃ. Dhammeneva, no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

131. ‘He is appointed by the great multitude,’ Vāseṭṭha, and so ‘Mahāsammata, Mahāsammata’ was the first designation to arise. ‘He is the lord of the fields,’ Vāseṭṭha, and so ‘Khattiya, Khattiya’ was the second designation to arise. ‘He pleases others with righteousness,’ Vāseṭṭha, and so ‘Rājā, Rājā’ was the third designation to arise. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, was the origin of this circle of Khattiyas by this ancient, primordial designation, for those very beings and not for others; for those who were like them, not unlike them; by righteousness only, not by unrighteousness. For Dhamma, Vāseṭṭha, is supreme among this populace, both in this present life and in the life to come.

Brāhmaṇamaṇḍalaṃ

The Circle of Brahmins

132. “Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃyeva tesaṃ yeva kho vāseṭṭha sattānaṃ (sī. pī.) ekaccānaṃ etadahosi – ‘pāpakā vata, bho, dhammā sattesu pātubhūtā, yatra hi nāma adinnādānaṃ paññāyissati, garahā paññāyissati, musāvādo paññāyissati, daṇḍādānaṃ paññāyissati, pabbājanaṃ paññāyissati. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ pāpake akusale dhamme vāheyyāmā’ti. Te pāpake akusale dhamme vāhesuṃ[P 3.0094]. Pāpake akusale dhamme vāhentīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘brāhmaṇā, brāhmaṇā’ tveva paṭhamaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Te araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭiyo [M 3.0078] karitvā paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti vītaṅgārā vītadhūmā pannamusalā [T 3.0103] sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya gāmanigamarājadhāniyo osaranti ghāsamesamānā ghāsamesanā (sī. syā. pī.). Te ghāsaṃ paṭilabhitvā punadeva araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti. Tamenaṃ manussā disvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ime kho, bho, sattā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭiyo karitvā paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti, vītaṅgārā vītadhūmā pannamusalā sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya gāmanigamarājadhāniyo osaranti ghāsamesamānā. Te ghāsaṃ paṭilabhitvā punadeva araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyantī’ti, jhāyantīti kho paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti jhāyantīti kho (sī. pī.), paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyantīti kho (ka.), vāseṭṭha, ‘jhāyakā, jhāyakā’ tveva dutiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Tesaṃyeva kho, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ ekacce sattā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu taṃ jhānaṃ anabhisambhuṇamānā anabhisaṃbhūnamānā (katthaci) gāmasāmantaṃ nigamasāmantaṃ osaritvā ganthe karontā acchanti. Tamenaṃ manussā disvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ime kho, bho, sattā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu taṃ jhānaṃ anabhisambhuṇamānā gāmasāmantaṃ nigamasāmantaṃ osaritvā ganthe karontā acchanti, na dānime jhāyantī’ti. Na dānime na dānime jhāyantī na dānime (sī. pī. ka.) jhāyantīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘ajjhāyakā ajjhāyakā’ tveva tatiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Hīnasammataṃ kho pana, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena hoti, tadetarahi seṭṭhasammataṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa brāhmaṇamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ[P 3.0095], anaññesaṃ sadisānaṃyeva no asadisānaṃ dhammeneva[V 3.0070], no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

132. Then, Vāseṭṭha, it occurred to some of those beings: ‘Sirs, evil qualities have indeed appeared among beings, in that theft has become known, censure has become known, falsehood has become known, the taking up of the rod has become known, and banishment has become known. What if we were to set adrift these evil, unwholesome qualities?’ And so they set adrift evil, unwholesome qualities. Because they set adrift evil, unwholesome qualities, Vāseṭṭha, ‘Brāhmaṇas, Brāhmaṇas’ was the first designation to arise. They built leaf-huts in a forest region and meditated in those leaf-huts—with embers gone, with smoke gone, with pestles laid aside. In the evening for their evening meal and in the morning for their morning meal, they would descend to a village, town, or royal city, seeking sustenance. Having obtained sustenance, they would return to the forest region and meditate in their leaf-huts. People saw them and said this: ‘Sirs, these beings build leaf-huts in a forest region and meditate in those leaf-huts—with embers gone, with smoke gone, with pestles laid aside. In the evening for their evening meal and in the morning for their morning meal, they descend to a village, town, or royal city, seeking sustenance. Having obtained sustenance, they return to the forest region and meditate in their leaf-huts.’ Because they meditate, Vāseṭṭha, ‘Jhāyakas, Jhāyakas’ was the second designation to arise. Then, Vāseṭṭha, some of those very beings, being unable to accomplish that meditation in the leaf-huts in the forest region, descended to the vicinity of a village or town and dwelt there composing texts. People saw them and said this: ‘Sirs, these beings, being unable to accomplish that meditation in the leaf-huts in the forest region, have descended to the vicinity of a village or town and dwell there composing texts. Now they do not meditate.’ ‘Now they do not meditate,’ Vāseṭṭha, and so ‘Ajjhāyakas, Ajjhāyakas’ was the third designation to arise. At that time, Vāseṭṭha, this was considered a lowly designation, but now it is considered a supreme one. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, was the origin of this circle of Brāhmaṇas by this ancient, primordial designation, for those very beings and not for others; for those who were like them, not unlike them; by righteousness only, not by unrighteousness. For Dhamma, Vāseṭṭha, is supreme among this populace, both in this present life and in the life to come.

Vessamaṇḍalaṃ

The Circle of Vessas

133. “Tesaṃyeva [T 3.0104] kho, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ ekacce sattā methunaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya visukammante vissutakammante (sī. pī.), vissukammante (ka. sī.), visuṃ kammante (syā. ka.) payojesuṃ. Methunaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya visukammante payojentīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘vessā, vessā’ tveva akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa vessamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaññeva sattānaṃ anaññesaṃ sadisānaṃyeva[M 3.0079], no asadisānaṃ, dhammeneva no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

133. Vāseṭṭha, among those very beings, certain beings, having adopted the practice of sexual union, engaged in various occupations. Vāseṭṭha, because they adopt the practice of sexual union and engage in various occupations, the designation ‘Vessas, Vessas’ arose. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, was the origin of this circle of Vessas by this ancient, primordial designation, for those very beings and not for others; for those who were like them, not unlike them; by righteousness only, not by unrighteousness. For Dhamma, Vāseṭṭha, is supreme among this populace, both in this present life and in the life to come.

Suddamaṇḍalaṃ

The Circle of Suddas

134. “Tesaññeva kho, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ ye te sattā avasesā te luddācārā khuddācārā ahesuṃ. Luddācārā khuddācārāti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘suddā, suddā’ tveva akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa suddamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ anaññesaṃ, sadisānaṃyeva no asadisānaṃ, dhammeneva, no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

134. Vāseṭṭha, among those very beings, those who remained were of cruel conduct and base conduct. Vāseṭṭha, because they are of cruel and base conduct, the designation ‘Suddas, Suddas’ arose. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, was the origin of this circle of Suddas by this ancient, primordial designation, for those very beings and not for others; for those who were like them, not unlike them; by righteousness only, not by unrighteousness. For Dhamma, Vāseṭṭha, is supreme among this populace, both in this present life and in the life to come.

135. “Ahu kho so, vāseṭṭha, samayo, yaṃ khattiyopi sakaṃ dhammaṃ garahamāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati – ‘samaṇo bhavissāmī’ti. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha, sakaṃ dhammaṃ garahamāno [P 3.0096] agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati – ‘samaṇo bhavissāmī’ti. Imehi kho, vāseṭṭha, catūhi maṇḍalehi samaṇamaṇḍalassa abhinibbatti ahosi, tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ anaññesaṃ, sadisānaṃyeva no asadisānaṃ, dhammeneva no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

135. Vāseṭṭha, there was a time when a Khattiya, reproaching his own practice, went forth from the household life into homelessness, thinking, ‘I will become a recluse.’ Vāseṭṭha, a Brahmin also... Vāseṭṭha, a Vessa also... Vāseṭṭha, a Sudda also, reproaching his own practice, went forth from the household life into homelessness, thinking, ‘I will become a recluse.’ From these four groups, Vāseṭṭha, the arising of the Samaṇa group occurred. This was for those very beings and not for others, for those who were similar indeed, not for those who were dissimilar; it was by righteousness, not by unrighteousness. For, Vāseṭṭha, Dhamma is supreme among this populace, both in this present life and in the life to come.

Duccaritādikathā

Discourse on Misconduct and Other Topics

136. “Khattiyopi [V 3.0071] kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ [T 3.0105] caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā micchādiṭṭhiko micchādiṭṭhikammasamādāno idaṃ padaṃ sī. ipotthakesu natthi micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha… samaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā micchādiṭṭhiko micchādiṭṭhikammasamādāno micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati.

136. Vāseṭṭha, a Khattiya also, having practiced misconduct by body, having practiced misconduct by speech, having practiced misconduct by mind, is of wrong view and undertakes actions based on wrong view. Because of undertaking actions based on wrong view, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a downfall, in hell. Vāseṭṭha, a Brahmin also... Vāseṭṭha, a Vessa also... Vāseṭṭha, a Sudda also... Vāseṭṭha, a Samaṇa also, having practiced misconduct by body, having practiced misconduct by speech, having practiced misconduct by mind, is of wrong view and undertakes actions based on wrong view. Because of undertaking actions based on wrong view, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a downfall, in hell.

“Khattiyopi [M 3.0080] kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā vācāya sucaritaṃ caritvā manasā sucaritaṃ caritvā sammādiṭṭhiko sammādiṭṭhikammasamādāno idaṃ padaṃ sī. pī. potthakesu natthi sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha… samaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā vācāya sucaritaṃ caritvā manasā sucaritaṃ caritvā sammādiṭṭhiko sammādiṭṭhikammasamādāno sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati.

Vāseṭṭha, a Khattiya also, having practiced good conduct by body, having practiced good conduct by speech, having practiced good conduct by mind, is of right view and undertakes actions based on right view. Because of undertaking actions based on right view, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Vāseṭṭha, a Brahmin also... Vāseṭṭha, a Vessa also... Vāseṭṭha, a Sudda also...
