Friends, there are beings with unified bodies and unified perception, such as the Subhakiṇha devas. This is the fourth abode of beings.

“Santāvuso, sattā asaññino appaṭisaṃvedino, seyyathāpi devā asaññasattā. Ayaṃ pañcamo sattāvāso.

Friends, there are beings who are non-percipient and do not experience feeling, such as the non-percipient devas. This is the fifth abode of beings.

“Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho sattāvāso.

Friends, there are beings who, by completely transcending perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and by not attending to perceptions of diversity, have reached the base of infinite space, perceiving, ‘Space is infinite.’ This is the sixth abode of beings.

“Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ sattamo sattāvāso.

Friends, there are beings who, by completely transcending the base of infinite space, have reached the base of infinite consciousness, perceiving, ‘Consciousness is infinite.’ This is the seventh abode of beings.

“Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo sattāvāso.

Friends, there are beings who, by completely transcending the base of infinite consciousness, have reached the base of nothingness, perceiving, ‘There is nothing.’ This is the eighth abode of beings.

“Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ navamo sattāvāso. Ime nava dhammā pariññeyyā.

Friends, there are beings who, by completely transcending the base of nothingness, have reached the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. This is the ninth abode of beings. These nine states are to be fully understood.

(Gha) “katame nava dhammā pahātabbā? Nava taṇhāmūlakā [P 3.0289] dhammā – taṇhaṃ paṭicca pariyesanā, pariyesanaṃ paṭicca lābho, lābhaṃ paṭicca vinicchayo, vinicchayaṃ paṭicca chandarāgo[V 3.0245], chandarāgaṃ paṭicca ajjhosānaṃ, ajjhosānaṃ paṭicca pariggaho, pariggahaṃ paṭicca macchariyaṃ, macchariyaṃ paṭicca ārakkho, ārakkhādhikaraṇaṃ ārakkhādhikaraṇaṃ paṭicca (syā. pī. ka.) daṇḍādānasatthādānakalahaviggahavivādatuvaṃtuvaṃpesuññamusāvādā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti. Ime nava dhammā pahātabbā.

(Gha) What nine states are to be abandoned? The nine states rooted in craving: dependent on craving, seeking arises; dependent on seeking, gain arises; dependent on gain, decision arises; dependent on decision, desire and lust arise; dependent on desire and lust, attachment arises; dependent on attachment, possessiveness arises; dependent on possessiveness, stinginess arises; dependent on stinginess, guarding arises; and with guarding as the cause, the taking up of rods and weapons, conflict, dispute, contention, ‘you, you’ speech, slander, and false speech—many such evil, unwholesome states come into being. These nine states are to be abandoned.

(Ṅa) “katame [T 3.0331][M 3.0254] nava dhammā hānabhāgiyā? Nava āghātavatthūni – ‘anatthaṃ me acarī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati, ‘anatthaṃ me caratī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati, ‘anatthaṃ me carissatī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acarī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… ‘anatthaṃ caratī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… ‘anatthaṃ carissatī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acarī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… ‘atthaṃ caratī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… ‘atthaṃ carissatī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati. Ime nava dhammā hānabhāgiyā.

(Ṅa) What nine states partake of decline? The nine grounds for resentment: one harbors resentment, thinking, ‘He has done me harm’; one harbors resentment, thinking, ‘He is doing me harm’; one harbors resentment, thinking, ‘He will do me harm’; one harbors resentment, thinking, ‘He has done harm to one who is dear and beloved to me’... ‘He is doing harm to one who is dear and beloved to me’... ‘He will do harm to one who is dear and beloved to me’; one harbors resentment, thinking, ‘He has done a service to one who is not dear and beloved to me’... ‘He is doing a service to one who is not dear and beloved to me’... ‘He will do a service to one who is not dear and beloved to me.’ These nine states partake of decline.

(Ca) “katame nava dhammā visesabhāgiyā? Nava āghātapaṭivinayā – ‘anatthaṃ me acari, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti; ‘anatthaṃ me carati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti; ‘anatthaṃ me carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti; ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti; ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ [T 3.0332] paṭivineti. Ime nava dhammā visesabhāgiyā.

(Ca) What nine states partake of distinction? The nine ways of subduing resentment: one subdues resentment, thinking, ‘He has done me harm—but what is to be gained from that?’; one subdues resentment, thinking, ‘He is doing me harm—but what is to be gained from that?’; one subdues resentment, thinking, ‘He will do me harm—but what is to be gained from that?’; one subdues resentment, thinking, ‘He has done harm to one who is dear and beloved to me... he is doing harm... he will do harm—but what is to be gained from that?’; one subdues resentment, thinking, ‘He has done a service to one who is not dear and beloved to me... he is doing a service... he will do a service—but what is to be gained from that?’. These nine states partake of distinction.

(Cha) “katame nava dhammā duppaṭivijjhā? Nava nānattā – dhātunānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṃ, phassanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṃ, vedanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṃ, saññānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṃ, saṅkappanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṃ, chandanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṃ, pariḷāhanānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṃ, pariyesanānānattaṃ paṭicca uppajjati lābhanānattaṃ. Ime nava dhammā duppaṭivijjhā.

What are the nine things that are hard to penetrate? The nine diversities: dependent on diversity of elements, diversity of contact arises; dependent on diversity of contact, diversity of feeling arises; dependent on diversity of feeling, diversity of perception arises; dependent on diversity of perception, diversity of thought arises; dependent on diversity of thought, diversity of desire arises; dependent on diversity of desire, diversity of burning arises; dependent on diversity of burning, diversity of seeking arises; dependent on diversity of seeking, diversity of gain arises. These nine things are hard to penetrate.

(Ja) “katame nava dhammā uppādetabbā? Nava saññā – asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhārepaṭikūlasaññā[V 3.0246], sabbalokeanabhiratisaññā anabhiratasaññā (syā. ka.), aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe [P 3.0290] anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā. Ime nava dhammā uppādetabbā.

What are the nine things that should be developed? The nine perceptions: the perception of unattractiveness, the perception of death, the perception of revulsion in food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in the impermanent, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, and the perception of dispassion. These nine things should be developed.

(Jha) “katame nava dhammā abhiññeyyā? Nava anupubbavihārā – idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ [M 3.0255] pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Pītiyā ca virāgā [T 3.0333] …pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ime nava dhammā abhiññeyyā.

What are the nine things to be known through direct knowledge? The nine successive abidings: Here, friends, a bhikkhu, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna... he enters and dwells in the second jhāna... he enters and dwells in the third jhāna... he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna... he enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite space... having completely transcended the sphere of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ he enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite consciousness... having completely transcended the sphere of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ he enters and dwells in the sphere of nothingness... having completely transcended the sphere of nothingness, he enters and dwells in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... having completely transcended the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling. These nine things are to be known through direct knowledge.

(Ña) “katame nava dhammā sacchikātabbā? Nava anupubbanirodhā – paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa kāmasaññā niruddhā hoti, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā niruddhā honti, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa pīti niruddhā hoti, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa assāsapassāssā niruddhā honti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa rūpasaññā niruddhā hoti, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā [T 3.0334] niruddhā hoti, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca niruddhā honti. Ime nava dhammā sacchikātabbā.

What are the nine things to be realized? The nine successive cessations: For one who has attained the first jhāna, perception of sensual pleasure has ceased. For one who has attained the second jhāna, thought and examination have ceased. For one who has attained the third jhāna, rapture has ceased. For one who has attained the fourth jhāna, in-breaths and out-breaths have ceased. For one who has attained the sphere of infinite space, perception of form has ceased. For one who has attained the sphere of infinite consciousness, perception of the sphere of infinite space has ceased. For one who has attained the sphere of nothingness, perception of the sphere of infinite consciousness has ceased. For one who has attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, perception of the sphere of nothingness has ceased. For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have ceased. These nine things are to be realized.

“Iti ime navuti dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.

Thus, these ninety things are actual, true, real, unfailing, not otherwise, and have been rightly and fully awakened to by the Tathāgata.

Dasa dhammā

The Group of Ten

360. “Dasa [V 3.0247] dhammā bahukārā…pe… dasa dhammā sacchikātabbā.

360. Ten things are of great benefit... ten things are to be realized.

(Ka) “katame dasa dhammā bahukārā? Dasa nāthakaraṇādhammā – idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu, yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti…pe… sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

(a) What are the ten things of great benefit? The ten refuge-making things. Here, friends, a bhikkhu is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint, accomplished in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults; he undertakes and trains in the training rules. That a bhikkhu is virtuous... and trains in the training rules—this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna [M 3.0256] caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto [T 3.0335] …pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto…pe… ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is learned... has thoroughly penetrated it by wisdom. That a bhikkhu is learned... this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu…pe… kalyāṇasampavaṅko. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, and is inclined towards the virtuous. That a bhikkhu... is inclined towards the virtuous—this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato, khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu…pe… anusāsaniṃ. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is easy to admonish, possessed of qualities that make one easy to admonish, is patient, and accepts instruction respectfully. That a bhikkhu... accepts instruction respectfully—this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni tattha dakkho hoti analaso tatrupāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato, alaṃ kātuṃ, alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu…pe… alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, in regard to the various duties, great and small, for his companions in the holy life, a bhikkhu is skilled and not lazy, endowed with wisdom concerning the means thereto, able to carry them out, and able to arrange them. That a bhikkhu... is able to arrange them—this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu…pe… uḷārapāmojjo. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is a lover of the Dhamma, is of pleasant speech, and has great joy in the higher Dhamma and the higher Vinaya. That a bhikkhu... has great joy—this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarehi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu [T 3.0336] …pe… ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is content with whatever robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick he may get. That a bhikkhu... this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna [V 3.0248] caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati…pe… kusalesu dhammesu. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu…pe… ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu dwells with aroused energy... in wholesome qualities. That a bhikkhu... this too is a refuge-making thing.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti, paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu…pe… ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and sagacity, able to remember and recollect what was done and said long ago. That a bhikkhu... this too is a refuge-making quality.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato, ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu…pe… ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo. Ime dasa dhammā bahukārā.

Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu is wise, endowed with wisdom that comprehends arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and rightly leads to the complete destruction of suffering. That a bhikkhu... this too is a refuge-making quality. These ten qualities are of great benefit.

(Kha) “katame [M 3.0257] dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā? Dasa kasiṇāyatanāni – pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ. Āpokasiṇameko sañjānāti…pe… tejokasiṇameko sañjānāti… vāyokasiṇameko sañjānāti… nīlakasiṇameko sañjānāti… pītakasiṇameko sañjānāti… lohitakasiṇameko sañjānāti… odātakasiṇameko sañjānāti… ākāsakasiṇameko sañjānāti… viññāṇakasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ[T 3.0337]. Ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā.

(Kha) What ten qualities are to be developed? The ten kasiṇa bases. One perceives the earth kasiṇa above, below, and across, non-dual and immeasurable. One perceives the water kasiṇa... one perceives the fire kasiṇa... one perceives the air kasiṇa... one perceives the blue kasiṇa... one perceives the yellow kasiṇa... one perceives the red kasiṇa... one perceives the white kasiṇa... one perceives the space kasiṇa... one perceives the consciousness kasiṇa above, below, and across, non-dual and immeasurable. These ten qualities are to be developed.

(Ga) “katame dasa dhammā pariññeyyā? Dasāyatanāni – cakkhāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ. Ime dasa dhammā pariññeyyā.

(Ga) What ten qualities are to be fully understood? The ten bases: the eye base, form base, ear base, sound base, nose base, odor base, tongue base, taste base, body base, and tangible base. These ten qualities are to be fully understood.

(Gha) “katame dasa dhammā pahātabbā? Dasa micchattā – micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṃ, micchāvimutti. Ime dasa dhammā pahātabbā.

(Gha) What ten qualities are to be abandoned? The ten wrongnesses: wrong view, wrong thought, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, and wrong liberation. These ten qualities are to be abandoned.

(Ṅa) “katame dasa dhammā hānabhāgiyā? Dasa akusalakammapathā – pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi. Ime dasa dhammā hānabhāgiyā.

(Ṅa) What are the ten qualities that partake of decline? The ten unwholesome courses of action: killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter, covetousness, ill will, and wrong view. These ten qualities partake of decline.

(Ca) “katame [V 3.0249][P 3.0291] dasa dhammā visesabhāgiyā? Dasa kusalakammapathā – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi. Ime dasa dhammā visesabhāgiyā.

(Ca) What are the ten qualities that partake of distinction? The ten wholesome courses of action: abstinence from killing living beings, abstinence from taking what is not given, abstinence from sexual misconduct, abstinence from false speech, abstinence from divisive speech, abstinence from harsh speech, abstinence from idle chatter, non-covetousness, non-ill will, and right view. These ten qualities partake of distinction.

(Cha) “katame dasa dhammā duppaṭivijjhā? Dasa ariyavāsā – idhāvuso[T 3.0338], bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti, chaḷaṅgasamannāgato, ekārakkho, caturāpasseno, paṇunnapaccekasacco, samavayasaṭṭhesano, anāvilasaṅkappo, passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro, suvimuttacitto, suvimuttapañño.

(Cha) What are the ten qualities that are difficult to penetrate? The ten noble abodes. Here, friends, a bhikkhu has abandoned five factors, is endowed with six factors, has a single guard, has four supports, has dispelled individual truths, has abandoned all quests, has untroubled intentions, has calmed bodily formations, is well-liberated in mind, and is well-liberated in wisdom.

“Kathañcāvuso[M 3.0258], bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmacchando pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti.

And how, friends, has a bhikkhu abandoned five factors? Here, friends, a bhikkhu has abandoned sensual desire, has abandoned ill will, has abandoned sloth and torpor, has abandoned restlessness and remorse, and has abandoned doubt. It is in this way, friends, that a bhikkhu has abandoned five factors.

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu chaḷaṅgasamannāgato hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu chaḷaṅgasamannāgato hoti.

And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one who possesses six factors? Here, friends, a bhikkhu, having seen a form with the eye, is neither joyful nor dejected, but dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending. Having heard a sound with the ear… smelled an odor with the nose… tasted a flavor with the tongue… touched a tangible with the body… cognized a mental object with the mind, he is neither joyful nor dejected, but dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one who possesses six factors.

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu ekārakkho hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satārakkhena cetasā samannāgato hoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu ekārakkho hoti.

And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one who has one guard? Here, friends, a bhikkhu is endowed with a mind guarded by mindfulness. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one who has one guard.

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu caturāpasseno hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṃ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṃ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṃ vinodeti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu caturāpasseno hoti.

And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one who has four supports? Here, friends, a bhikkhu, with reflection, makes use of something; with reflection, he endures something; with reflection, he avoids something; with reflection, he dispels something. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one who has four supports.

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu paṇunnapaccekasacco hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno yāni [T 3.0339] tāni puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ [V 3.0250] puthupaccekasaccāni, sabbāni tāni nunnāni honti paṇunnāni cattāni vantāni muttāni pahīnāni paṭinissaṭṭhāni. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu paṇunnapaccekasacco hoti.

And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one who has dispelled individual truths? Here, friends, whatever various individual truths there are of the many ascetics and brahmins, all those are removed, repelled, given up, expelled, released, abandoned, and relinquished. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one who has dispelled individual truths.

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu samavayasaṭṭhesano hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmesanā pahīnā hoti, bhavesanā pahīnā hoti, brahmacariyesanā paṭippassaddhā. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu samavayasaṭṭhesano hoti.

And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one whose quests are allayed and discarded? Here, friends, for a bhikkhu the quest for sensual pleasures is abandoned, the quest for existence is abandoned, and the quest for the holy life is calmed. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one whose quests are allayed and discarded.

“Kathañcāvuso[M 3.0259], bhikkhu anāvilasaṅkappā hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, byāpādasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, vihiṃsāsaṅkappo pahīno hoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu anāvilasaṅkappo hoti.

And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one with untroubled intentions? Here, friends, a bhikkhu has abandoned sensual intentions, abandoned intentions of ill will, and abandoned intentions of cruelty. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one with untroubled intentions.

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro hoti.

And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one who has calmed bodily formation? Here, friends, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and sorrow, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one who has calmed bodily formation.

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttacitto hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno rāgā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti, dosā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti, mohā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttacitto hoti.

“And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one with a well-liberated mind? Here, friends, a bhikkhu’s mind is liberated from lust, liberated from hatred, and liberated from delusion. Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one with a well-liberated mind.”

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttapañño hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘rāgo me pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti. ‘Doso me pahīno…pe… āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti. ‘Moho me pahīno [T 3.0340] …pe… āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttapañño hoti. Ime dasa dhammā duppaṭivijjhā.

“And how, friends, is a bhikkhu one who is well-liberated by wisdom? Here, friends, a bhikkhu understands: ‘Lust has been abandoned by me, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future.’ He understands: ‘Hatred has been abandoned by me… and is of a nature not to arise in the future.’ He understands: ‘Delusion has been abandoned by me… and is of a nature not to arise in the future.’ Thus, friends, a bhikkhu is one who is well-liberated by wisdom. These ten things are difficult to penetrate.”

(Ja) “katame dasa dhammā uppādetabbā? Dasa saññā – asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhārepaṭikūlasaññā, sabbalokeanabhiratisaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā. Ime dasa dhammā uppādetabbā.

“What ten things are to be developed? Ten perceptions: the perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of revulsion in food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in the impermanent, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, and the perception of cessation. These ten things are to be developed.”

(Jha) “katame [V 3.0251] dasa dhammā abhiññeyyā? Dasa nijjaravatthūni – sammādiṭṭhissa micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā hoti. Ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti. Sammāsaṅkappassa micchāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāvācassa micchāvācā… sammākammantassa micchākammanto… sammāājīvassa micchāājīvo… [T 3.0341] sammāvāyāmassa micchāvāyāmo… sammāsatissa micchāsati… sammāsamādhissa micchāsamādhi… sammāñāṇassa micchāñāṇaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ hoti. Sammāvimuttissa [T 3.0342] micchāvimutti [M 3.0260] nijjiṇṇā hoti. Ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti. Ime dasa dhammā abhiññeyyā.

“What ten things are to be fully understood? The ten grounds for wearing away: for one with right view, wrong view is worn away. And whatever numerous evil, unwholesome things come into being dependent on wrong view, those too are worn away for him. For one with right intention, wrong intention… for one with right speech, wrong speech… for one with right action, wrong action… for one with right livelihood, wrong livelihood… for one with right effort, wrong effort… for one with right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness… for one with right concentration, wrong concentration… for one with right knowledge, wrong knowledge is worn away. For one with right liberation, wrong liberation is worn away. And whatever numerous evil, unwholesome things come into being dependent on wrong liberation, those too are worn away for him. These ten things are to be fully understood.”

(Ña) “katame [P 3.0292] dasa dhammā sacchikātabbā? Dasa asekkhā dhammā – asekkhā sammādiṭṭhi, asekkho sammāsaṅkappo, asekkhā sammāvācā, asekkho sammākammanto, asekkho sammāājīvo, asekkho sammāvāyāmo, asekkhā sammāsati, asekkho sammāsamādhi, asekkhaṃ sammāñāṇaṃ, asekkhā sammāvimutti. Ime dasa dhammā sacchikātabbā.

“What ten things are to be realized? The ten qualities of one beyond training: the right view of one beyond training, the right intention of one beyond training, the right speech of one beyond training, the right action of one beyond training, the right livelihood of one beyond training, the right effort of one beyond training, the right mindfulness of one beyond training, the right concentration of one beyond training, the right knowledge of one beyond training, and the right liberation of one beyond training. These ten things are to be realized.”

“Iti ime satadhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā”ti. Idamavocāyasmā sāriputto. Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

“Thus, these one hundred principles are actual, true, as they are, not unreal, not otherwise, and have been rightly and fully awakened to by the Tathāgata.” This is what the Venerable Sāriputta said. Gratified, those bhikkhus delighted in the Venerable Sāriputta’s words.

Dasuttarasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ ekādasamaṃ.

The Dasuttara Sutta, the eleventh, is concluded.

Pāthikavaggo pāṭikavaggo (sī. syā. pī.) niṭṭhito.

The Pāthika Vagga is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Pāthiko [V 3.0252] ca pāṭikañca (syā. kaṃ.) udumbaraṃ pāṭikodumbarīceva (sī. pī.), cakkavatti aggaññakaṃ;

Sampasādanapāsādaṃ [P 3.0293] sampasādañca pāsādaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ.

The Pāthika and the Udumbara, the Cakkavatti and the Aggañña; the Sampasādaniya and the Pāsādika, the Mahāpurisalakkhaṇa.

Siṅgālāṭānāṭiyakaṃ[T 3.0343], saṅgīti ca dasuttaraṃ;

Ekādasahi suttehi, pāthikavaggoti vuccati.

The Siṅgāla and the Āṭānāṭiya, the Saṅgīti and the Dasuttara; with these eleven suttas, it is called the Pāthika Vagga.

Pāthikavaggapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāli of the Pāthika Vagga is concluded.

Tīhi vaggehi paṭimaṇḍito sakalo

Adorned with three vaggas, the entire

Dīghanikāyo samatto.

Dīgha Nikāya is complete.
